repo.description: cuDNN Frontend is NVIDIA's modern, open-source entry point to the cuDNN library and a growing collection of high-performance open-source kernels.
repo.name: cudnn-frontend

detail.body:
# cuDNN Frontend v1.32.0 Release Notes

cuDNN Frontend v1.32.0 adds Mamba-2, Qwen sparse attention training, Rubin triangle operations, and a CuTe DSL normalization backend. FROST SDPA gains more native forward and backward configurations, broader paged-cache support, and lower setup overhead. This release also adds FROST plan serialization, expands JAX grouped GEMM support, and updates Python bindings and dependencies.

## New: Mamba-2 linear attention 🚀 🚀

Mamba-2 joins the FROST linear-attention family with forward, backward, and state-summary operations on SM100, SM103, and SM107. The Python entry point is `cudnn.linear_attention.ops.mamba2` ([#1577](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1577)).

- Supports packed sequences, BF16/FP16 inputs, initial and final recurrent states, optional skip connections, output gating, and step-size controls. The supported state dimension is 128.
- State summaries expose the per-sequence end state and transition needed to compose sequence segments. Summary backward is also available.
- Checkpoints can use `checkpoint_dtype=torch.float32`; Mamba-2 checkpoint intervals are multiples of 128 tokens ([#1694](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1694)).

The wider linear-attention family also gains persistent caching for common forward kernels, a faster KDA backward pipeline, and fixes for multistream workspace reuse, GDP interleaved layouts and cached summaries, and GDN-2 NaNs under steep per-channel decay ([#1708](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1708), [#1699](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1699), [#1569](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1569), [#1664](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1664), [#1695](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1695), [#1644](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1644)).

## New: Qwen sparse attention training 🚀 🚀

`cudnn.ops.qsa_forward` and `qsa_backward` provide explicit packed QSA training calls for Blackwell SM100/SM103 and Rubin SM107. They support BF16 D256 attention with 12Q/1KV or 24Q/2KV heads and four-token blocks. Forward returns the BF16 output, an FP32 saved output, and natural-log LSE for backward. These functions do not install an autograd wrapper ([#1765](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1765), [#1778](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1778)).

- **Indexed training** accepts existing token selections through `qsa_indexed_forward` and `qsa_indexed_backward`, initially for BF16 12Q/1KV D256 on SM100/SM103. At 128K tokens with selection width 2052, compact IDs use 256.5 MiB in either direction, compared with 16 GiB for bitmap-forward IDs or 8 GiB for paired bitmap-backward IDs. The indexed path also avoids the 4 GiB selection bitmap. These figures describe selection metadata, not total memory ([#1774](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1774)).
- **Packed causal top-k backward** is available through `selection_mode="causal_topk"`, with explicit sequence boundaries and a bounded-workspace two-pass implementation. This mode has a stricter selection contract and requires the CUDA 13 CuTe DSL compiler ([#1781](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1781), [#1787](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1787)).
- QSA attention and selection functions are consolidated under `cudnn.ops.qsa_*`. Indexed attention consumes caller-supplied selections; the separate selector APIs compute them.

## Gated attention block: serving and packed training 🚀 🚀

The experimental Rubin SM107 D256 gated attention block gains paged-cache **EXTEND** and **DECODE** modes. These combine projection, optional QK normalization, RoPE, cache writes, attention, gating, and output projection through the block API. Weight loaders cover the documented Hugging Face and vLLM layouts ([#1471](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1471), [#1606](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1606), [#1619](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1619)).

- **Qwen sparse attention serving:** `QsaSpec` selects the index-list sparse attention path. Supported modes include caller-supplied lists and an integrated compression, scoring, and top-k indexer, including paged decode ([#1639](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1639), [#1789](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1789)).
- **Packed quantized execution:** the unfused MXFP8 forward and per-tensor FP8 backward gain packed-sequence support. Packed half forward can fuse the output gate, and supported packed backward plans accept an externally computed delta ([#1502](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1502), [#1505](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1505), [#1617](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1617), [#1497](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1497)).
- **Fewer launches:** MXFP8 backward fuses small operations and reuses block-scale dQ work. Serving paths add small-row projection kernels, fused preparation/cache writes, and programmatic dependent launch where supported ([#1466](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1466), [#1680](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1680), [#1763](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1763)).
- Compiled blocks can update quantization scales between steps through `update_quant_scales`. The fully fused MXFP8 projection also accepts MXFP4 weights ([#1506](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1506), [#1487](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1487)).

## SDPA: wider native forward support 🚀 🚀

**Blackwell SM100/SM103**

- Adds native FP16/BF16 **Q/K576, V512** attention with dense queries and dense or paged KV, including absorbed-MLA cache layouts. It supports partial GQA packing, split-KV, independent K/V tables and layouts, masks, sinks, and optional Stats. Packed queries remain outside this new flavor ([#1902](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1902)).
- Adds native paged per-tensor **FP8 D256** execution and physical-origin support for paged FP8 THD inputs. Paged FP8 attention can use sinks ([#1887](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1887), [#1895](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1895), [#1874](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1874)).
- Expands packed GQA prefill and D256 THD split coverage. Paged K and V can use independent physical layouts ([#1468](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1468), [#1533](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1533), [#1697](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1697)).

**Rubin SM107**

- Extends MXFP8 to packed D256 queries and paged K/V pools with sinks for supported dense D128/D256 queries ([#1488](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1488), [#1481](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1481)).
- Adds native D64 per-tensor FP8 attention, D128 GQA packing, and D512 packed/split plans. Half-precision sinks also work with split-KV ([#1878](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1878), [#1830](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1830), [#1863](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1863), [#1858](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1858)).
- MXFP8 and per-tensor FP8 forward rows are offered by default. The selected engine remains dependent on graph features and measured shape ranges ([#1478](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1478), [#1684](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1684)).

**SM120 and Ampere**

- SM120 gains specialized MXFP8 prefill kernels, including D512, plus FP16/BF16 decode tiles for small packed query counts. Split-KV supports attention sinks, and GQA packing no longer requires the full head group to divide the query tile ([#1599](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1599), [#1636](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1636), [#1768](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1768), [#1731](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1731), [#1740](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1740)).
- SM80 forward serves native packed THD graphs. Its backward reads the current ragged offsets on the device ([#1155](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1155), [#1058](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1058)).

Across the native THD paths, metadata setup is fused for small batches, tensor-map construction is parallelized, and setup overlaps kernel initialization. Context-parallel work lookup and paged scheduling use work prefixes and request lengths to reduce wasted work ([#1831](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1831), [#1851](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1851), [#1886](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1886), [#1696](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1696), [#1709](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1709)).

## SDPA: backward and numerical fixes 🚀 🚀

- **D128 backward on SM100/SM103:** adds FROST dense and packed execution, with supported GQA/MQA paths. Dense BF16/FP16 MHA can request a deterministic, fixed-order recompute implementation with zero workspace; grouped and THD deterministic requests remain unsupported ([#1688](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1688), [#1783](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1783), [#1875](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1875)).
- **More dense geometries:** adds native D64 backward and left sliding windows for dense D64/D128 MHA, plus native dense D192×128 half-precision backward on SM100 ([#1879](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1879), [#1883](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1883)).
- **D256 addressing:** supports batch-pitched backward and packed inputs with independent physical origins. Context-parallel backward reduces workspace and improves vector loads ([#1690](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1690), [#1872](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1872), [#1629](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1629)).
- Fixes negative attention-scale handling on supported SM100/SM107 and SM120 forward paths, masked leading KV tiles on Rubin, and D192 FP8 probability rounding ([#1445](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1445), [#1448](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1448), [#1544](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1544), [#1810](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1810)).
- Fixes D512 shared-ring phase reuse, split-KV softmax barrier ownership, scheduler back-edges, and terminal dQ barrier reuse ([#1521](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1521), [#1541](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1541), [#1547](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1547), [#1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698)).

## New: Rubin triangle operations 🚀 🚀

`cudnn.triangle_attention` and `cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update` provide experimental forward operations with cuEquivariance 0.12.0-compatible argument signatures ([#1607](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1607)).

- Triangle attention supports BF16/FP16 activations, pair bias, key masks or key lengths, and head dimensions divisible by 8 up to 64. Rows with no live keys return zero output and negative-infinity LSE.
- Triangle multiplicative update supports BF16 pair representations with channel widths 128 or 256, both directions, and optional pair masks.
- Both target **SM107 only** and require the documented FROST opt-in. Backward is not implemented.

## New: CuTe DSL normalization backend 🚀 🚀

SM100 gains forward and backward kernels for **LayerNorm, RMSNorm, GroupNorm, InstanceNorm, and BatchNorm**, with FP32, FP16, and BF16 I/O. They are available through graph engines and the direct `cudnn.norm.norm_fprop` / `norm_bprop` APIs ([#1509](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1509)).

GroupNorm, InstanceNorm, and BatchNorm have native channels-last paths that preserve layout through forward and backward. LayerNorm and RMSNorm reduce the last logical dimension and use the contiguous path for channels-last inputs.

Graph normalization APIs also accept optional RMSNorm scale, optional LayerNorm scale/bias, and optional AdaLayerNorm bias. RMSNorm and LayerNorm backward accept optional scale; LayerNorm validates matching statistics dimensions ([#1542](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1542), [#1548](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1548), [#1555](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1555), [#1552](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1552)).

## Sparse attention: DSA, BSA, and CSA ✨✨

- **Deterministic DSA:** adds deterministic indexer backward and standalone top-k, H32 indexer backward, and two-CTA H128 backward. A clustered reduction bounds workspace for long-context deterministic backward, including 1M-context workloads ([#1641](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1641), [#1637](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1637), [#1723](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1723), [#1666](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1666), [#1770](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1770)).
- **DSA indexer and execution:** adds MXFP4 scoring on SM100, native H96 target recomputation, and faster scale packing. Prepared DSA execution uses caller-owned outputs/workspace and preserves 64-bit addressing for long sequences ([#1775](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1775), [#1859](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1859), [#1564](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1564), [#1182](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1182), [#1767](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1767)).
- **Sage FP8 BSA:** adds native SM120 block-128 forward, SM90 block-64/block-128 forward, and SM100/SM103 block-128 forward. SM100 backward also supports padded KV blocks ([#1163](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1163), [#1752](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1752), [#1785](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1785)).
- **BSA correctness:** fixes SM90 shared-V lifetime, SM100 softmax stability for large logits, backward tail zero-fill, and FP32 computation of O·dO products ([#1498](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1498), [#1221](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1221), [#1682](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1682), [#1713](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1713)).
- **CSA:** adds deterministic dAPE reduction and parallelizes it. Ratio-128 forward handles NaN chunks and negative-infinity positions explicitly ([#1605](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1605), [#1717](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1717), [#1692](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1692)).

## GEMM, MoE, and JAX ✨✨

- **Canonical JAX grouped operations** expand across MXFP8, NVFP4/MXFP4, and BF16 wherever the underlying kernel supports the format. Coverage includes GLU, dGLU, weight gradients, quantization, SReLU/dSReLU, and Hadamard fusions. Packed FP4 travels as `uint8` with two values per byte ([#1399](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1399), [#1535](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1535), [#1600](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1600)).
- Grouped BF16, dGLU, gradient quantization, weight-gradient, and Hadamard paths accept canonical layouts. BF16 grouped execution no longer reads offsets back to the host ([#1422](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1422), [#1601](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1601), [#1602](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1602)).
- FROST GEMM gains SM120-specific tile scoring and split-K selection. The SM120 family adds MoE COMBINE and mixed MXFP4-weight/MXFP8-activation execution; callers can also own scheduler-counter initialization ([#1460](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1460), [#1500](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1500), [#1638](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1638), [#1881](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1881)).
- Fixes compiled-object cache reuse across CUDA devices in grouped GLU, Hadamard, and quantization. Also fixes the SM100 GLU/Hadamard/quant epilogue deadlock ([#1808](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1808), [#1813](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1813), [#1904](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1904), [#1901](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1901)).

## Graph API, serialization, and execution ✨✨

- **FROST plan serialization:** `pygraph.serialize()` records the selected Python engine, public knobs, graph IR, and optionally compiled kernels. Deserialization reuses kernels only when their recorded environment matches; otherwise it recompiles. `enforce_precompiled=True` rejects compilation. Python-plan blobs cannot be loaded by C++ `Graph::deserialize` ([#1862](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1862)).
- **Binary serialization:** `serialize(as_bytes=True)` returns `bytes`, and `deserialize()` accepts bytes. The default serialized return type remains `list[int]` ([#1725](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1725)).
- **CUDA Graph controls:** opt-in `populate_cuda_graph_direct()` / `update_cuda_graph_direct()` avoid an extra child graph for eligible plans. Applications that manage resource lifetimes can disable automatic retention with `cuda_graph_retention=NONE`; the default retains resources. Cleanup moves out of execution and into plan/graph destruction ([#1140](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1140), [#1495](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1495), [#1676](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1676)).
- **Shared compilation:** concurrent processes using the same compiled cache avoid duplicate compilation. SDPA plans also cache immutable function metadata ([#1707](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1707), [#1844](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1844)).
- **PyTorch integration:** `cudnn.torch.install_sdpa_overrides()` returns a removable handle for the cuDNN SDPA overrides, supporting PyTorch's Python-provider switch ([#1776](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1776)).
- **Unified SDPA compute precision** is forwarded to the backend with cuDNN 9.29 header/runtime gates. Explicit indexed execution remains independent of the selected plan, and legacy autotuning keeps metadata aligned with reordered plans ([#1746](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1746), [#1786](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1786), [#1806](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1806), [#1701](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1701)).

## Compatibility and API changes ✨✨

- **CuTe DSL minimum:** the package now requires `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0`. Windows ARM64 remains excluded from this dependency and `apache-tvm-ffi`, because those runtimes do not provide packages for that platform ([#1820](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1820), [#1837](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1837)).
- **Bindings:** Python bindings move from pybind11 to nanobind. Builds require CMake 3.26 or newer. Optional `CUDNN_FRONTEND_PYTHON_STABLE_ABI=ON` targets GIL-enabled CPython 3.12+; free-threaded Python continues to require version-specific builds ([#1523](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1523)).
- **Experimental aliases removed:** explicit KDA/BSA operations move to `cudnn.ops`, and grouped SwiGLU aliases are removed. Differentiable JAX KDA/BSA entry points remain in `cudnn.jax` ([#1727](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1727), [#1597](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1597)).

| Removed name | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `cudnn.jax.kimi_delta_attention_fwd` / `_bwd` | `cudnn.ops.kimi_delta_attention_forward_jax` / `kimi_delta_attention_backward_jax` |
| `cudnn.jax.block_sparse_attention_forward` / `_backward` | `cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_forward_jax` / `block_sparse_attention_backward_jax` |
| `cudnn.torch.block_sparse_attention_forward` / `_backward` / `_fp8_forward` | Corresponding `cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_*` functions |
| `cudnn.jax.grouped_gemm_swiglu` or `cudnn.torch.grouped_gemm_swiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_swiglu_wrapper_sm100` |
| `cudnn.jax.grouped_gemm_dswiglu` or `cudnn.torch.grouped_gemm_dswiglu` | `cudnn.grouped_gemm_dswiglu_wrapper_sm100` |

- **`Amax_S` is deprecated.** FROST FP8 plans do not produce this output; a materialized `Amax_S` requires a backend plan ([#1684](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1684)).
- **Windows:** adds CUDA 13 dynamic loading, correct runtime-major dispatch for changed CUDA entry points, and Windows ARM64 packaging fixes ([#1499](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1499), [#1566](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1566), [#1714](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1714)).

## Documentation, benchmarks, and tests 📊

- Redesigned documentation navigation and indexed the lazy public API. FlashInfer-facing capability queries and runtime helpers are now public ([#1587](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1587), [#1663](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1663), [#1592](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1592)).
- Attention benchmarks now include the default frontend engine choice, a report of selection cost versus the fastest measured plan, context-parallel THD training, and serving-style paged KV with mixed cache lengths ([#1848](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1848), [#1856](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1856), [#1867](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1867)).
- Added QSA training benchmarks, normalization benchmarks, and Mamba-2 examples and measurements. Expanded CUDA Graph replay, deterministic execution, long-sequence, and multi-device regression coverage.
- `cudnn-repro` handles malformed tensor-dump lines and missing log files, and restores Python 3.9 import compatibility for that standalone tool ([#1584](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1584), [#1582](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1582)).

+name: Security scan
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types:
+      - opened
+      - reopened
+      - synchronize
+      - ready_for_review
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - develop
+      - main
+  schedule:
+    - cron: "17 9 * * 1"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  codeql-cpp:
+    name: CodeQL C/C++
+    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@6f2ac81f5cd81fe351a197ba0b00d91d03cd2aee # v4
+        with:
+          languages: c-cpp
+          build-mode: none
+          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
+
+      - name: Analyze
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@6f2ac81f5cd81fe351a197ba0b00d91d03cd2aee # v4
+
+  codeql-python:
+    name: CodeQL Python
+    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@6f2ac81f5cd81fe351a197ba0b00d91d03cd2aee # v4
+        with:
+          languages: python
+          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
+
+      - name: Analyze
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@6f2ac81f5cd81fe351a197ba0b00d91d03cd2aee # v4
+
+  dependency-review:
+    name: Dependency review
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.draft == false
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: read
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Review dependency changes
+        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@a1d282b36b6f3519aa1f3fc636f609c47dddb294 # v5.0.0
+        with:
+          config-file: ./.github/dependency-review-config.yml

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Measure complete eager blk64 BSA invocations with reproducible synthetic inputs."""
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+
+
+def measure(fn, warmup, repeats, rounds, flush):
+    import torch
+
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    measurements = []
+    for _ in range(rounds):
+        samples = []
+        for _ in range(repeats):
+            flush.zero_()
+            start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            result = fn()
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end))
+        measurements.append({"median_ms": statistics.median(samples), "samples_ms": samples})
+    return measurements, result
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--expected-source-root", type=Path, required=True, help="Fail if cudnn is imported from another checkout")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--sq", type=int, default=8192)
+    parser.add_argument("--sk", type=int, default=8192)
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--blocks-per-row", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--layout", choices=("bhsd", "bshd"), default="bshd")
+    parser.add_argument("--metadata", choices=("fixed", "variable"), default="variable")
+    parser.add_argument("--bucket-size", type=int)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=15)
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260927)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if min(args.sq, args.sk, args.heads, args.blocks_per_row, args.warmup, args.repeats, args.rounds) <= 0:
+        parser.error("shapes and iteration counts must be positive")
+    if args.bucket_size is not None and args.bucket_size <= 0:
+        parser.error("bucket-size must be positive")
+
+    import torch
+    import cudnn
+    from cudnn import ops
+
+    root = args.expected_source_root.resolve()
+    expected_package = root / "python" / "cudnn"
+    if Path(cudnn.__file__).resolve().parent != expected_package:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"expected {expected_package}, imported {cudnn.__file__}")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        raise RuntimeError("this benchmark targets SM100/SM103")
+    nq, nk = (args.sq + 63) // 64, (args.sk + 63) // 64
+    width = min(args.blocks_per_row, nk)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(args.seed)
+    host_tensors = [torch.randn((1, args.heads, length, 128), generator=generator, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for length in (args.sq, args.sk, args.sk, args.sq)]
+    # Every row has unique KV IDs; cyclic neighborhoods include cross-window reuse.
+    rows = torch.arange(nq).view(1, 1, nq, 1)
+    heads = torch.arange(args.heads).view(1, args.heads, 1, 1)
+    indices = ((rows + heads * 7 + torch.arange(width)) % nk).int().contiguous()
+    counts = (width - (torch.arange(args.heads * nq) % min(width, 4))).int().view(1, args.heads, nq)
+    sizes = torch.full((nk,), 64, dtype=torch.int32)
+    sizes[-1] = args.sk - (nk - 1) * 64
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    for tensor in (*host_tensors, indices, counts, sizes):
+        digest.update(tensor.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).numpy().tobytes())
+    if args.layout == "bshd":
+        host_tensors = [t.transpose(1, 2).contiguous() for t in host_tensors]
+    q, k, v, do = [t.cuda() for t in host_tensors]
+    indices, sizes = indices.cuda(), sizes.cuda()
+    counts = counts.cuda() if args.metadata == "variable" else None
+    kwargs = dict(block_sparse_num=width, block_sizes=sizes, q2k_block_nums=counts, sparse_block_size=64, layout=args.layout)
+
+    def forward():
+        return ops.block_sparse_attention_forward(q, k, v, indices, **kwargs)
+
+    output, lse = forward()
+
+    def backward():
+        return ops.block_sparse_attention_backward(do, q, k, v, output, lse, indices, **kwargs, bucket_size_blocks=args.bucket_size)
+
+    flush = torch.empty(256 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    fwd_times, final_forward = measure(forward, args.warmup, args.repeats, args.rounds, flush)
+    bwd_times, final_backward = measure(backward, args.warmup, args.repeats, args.rounds, flush)
+    if not all(torch.isfinite(t).all().item() for t in (*final_forward, *final_backward)):
+        raise RuntimeError("nonfinite output; discard timing")
+    source_dir = expected_package / "block_sparse_attention"
+    report = {
+        "parameters": {key: str(value) if isinstance(value, Path) else value for key, value in vars(args).items()},
+        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(),
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "cutlass_dsl": importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl"),
+        "cudnn_source": cudnn.__file__,
+        "commit": subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(root), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip(),
+        "source_sha256": {str(p.relative_to(source_dir)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(source_dir.rglob("*.py"))},
+        "input_sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
+        "gpu_state": subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,driver_version,clocks.sm,clocks.mem,power.limit", "--format=csv"], text=True),
+        "timing": "CUDA events around complete eager API calls; CSR, pairing, preprocessing and output conversion included; 256 MiB flush before each sample",
+        "validation": "Finite outputs only; run the independent numerical tests before interpreting timings",
+        "forward": fwd_times,
+        "backward": bwd_times,
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps({"forward_ms": [x["median_ms"] for x in fwd_times], "backward_ms": [x["median_ms"] for x in bwd_times]}, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Interleaved, same-buffer SM100 blk64 forward A/B and independent A/A.
+
+Install the current checkout, then run on an idle GPU, for example:
+    python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm100_blk64_prefetch.py --baseline-ref <base-commit> --output results.json
+
+The baseline is loaded from git into two independent modules. Routing, allocation,
+compilation and reference checks are outside CUDA Graph timing. Every variant
+uses identical BSHD inputs and ascending mean-pool top-k block indices.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import math
+import random
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import cutlass
+import cudnn
+import torch
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda
+from cudnn.block_sparse_attention import _interface
+from cudnn.block_sparse_attention.csrc.fwd.sm100_blk64 import bsa_fwd_sm100
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+KERNEL = Path("python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/csrc/fwd/sm100_blk64/bsa_fwd_sm100.py")
+
+
+def load_baseline(source, directory, name):
+    path = directory / f"{name}.py"
+    path.write_bytes(source)
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[name] = module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module.BlockSparseAttnForwardSm100Blk64
+
+
+def gpu_snapshot():
+    properties = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
+    pci_bus = f"{properties.pci_domain_id:04x}:{properties.pci_bus_id:02x}:{properties.pci_device_id:02x}.0"
+    return subprocess.check_output(
+        [
+            "nvidia-smi",
+            "-i",
+            pci_bus,
+            "--query-gpu=name,uuid,clocks.sm,clocks.mem,power.draw,power.limit,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used",
+            "--format=csv,noheader",
+        ],
+        text=True,
+    ).strip()
+
+
+class Runner:
+    def __init__(self, cls, inputs, indices):
+        cache = _interface.bsa_attn_fwd_blk64_cutedsl.compile_cache
+        original_cls = _interface.BlockSparseAttnForwardSm100Blk64
+        cache.clear()
+
+        def api():
+            return cudnn.ops.block_sparse_attention_forward(*inputs, indices, sparse_block_size=64, layout="bshd", kv_splits=1)
+
+        try:
+            _interface.BlockSparseAttnForwardSm100Blk64 = cls
+            first = api()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            assert len(cache) == 1, "Expected one unsplit attention kernel."
+            key, fn = next(iter(cache.items()))
+            calls = []
+
+            def record(*args):
+                calls.append(args)
+                return fn(*args)
+
+            cache[key] = record
+            result = api()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            assert len(calls) == 1
+            self.fn, self.params = fn, calls[0][:-1]
+            self.output, self.lse = result["o_tensor"], result["lse_tensor"]
+            self.compile_key = str(key)
+            assert torch.equal(first["o_tensor"], self.output)
+            assert torch.equal(first["lse_tensor"], self.lse)
+        finally:
+            _interface.BlockSparseAttnForwardSm100Blk64 = original_cls
+            cache.clear()
+
+    def run(self):
+        self.fn(*self.params, cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream))
+
+
+def reference_check(inputs, indices, runners):
+    q, k, v = inputs
+    length, heads = q.shape[1:3]
+    records = {name: dict(output_max_abs=0.0, lse_max_abs=0.0, squared_error=0.0, squared_reference=0.0) for name in runners}
+    for head in sorted({0, heads // 2, heads - 1}):
+        for block in sorted({0, length // 128, length // 64 - 1}):
+            rows = torch.tensor([block * 64, block * 64 + 31], device="cuda")
+            keys = (indices[0, head, block].long()[:, None] * 64 + torch.arange(64, device="cuda")).flatten()
+            logits = q[0, rows, head].float() @ k[0, keys, head].float().T / math.sqrt(128)
+            expected = logits.softmax(-1) @ v[0, keys, head].float()
+            expected_lse = logits.logsumexp(-1)
+            for name, runner in runners.items():
+                actual, lse = runner.output[0, rows, head].float(), runner.lse[0, head, rows]
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0.005, rtol=0.005)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(lse, expected_lse, atol=0.0001, rtol=0.00001)
+                rec = records[name]
+                rec["output_max_abs"] = max(rec["output_max_abs"], (actual - expected).abs().max().item())
+                rec["lse_max_abs"] = max(rec["lse_max_abs"], (lse - expected_lse).abs().max().item())
+                rec["squared_error"] += (actual - expected).square().sum().item()
+                rec["squared_reference"] += expected.square().sum().item()
+    for rec in records.values():
+        rec["output_relative_l2"] = math.sqrt(rec.pop("squared_error") / max(rec.pop("squared_reference"), 1e-30))
+    return records
+
+
+def measure(runners, rounds, repeats, seed):
+    graphs, samples, orders = {}, {name: [] for name in runners}, []
+    for name, runner in runners.items():
+        for _ in range(5):
+            runner.run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            for _ in range(repeats):
+                runner.run()
+        graphs[name] = graph
+        runner.output.fill_(float("nan"))
+        runner.lse.fill_(float("nan"))
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.isfinite(runner.output).all() and torch.isfinite(runner.lse).all()
+    until = time.perf_counter() + 1.0
+    while time.perf_counter() < until:
+        for graph in graphs.values():
+            graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    for _ in range(rounds):
+        order = list(runners)
+        rng.shuffle(order)
+        orders.append(order)
+        for name in order:
+            start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            graphs[name].replay()
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            samples[name].append(start.elapsed_time(end) / repeats)
+    return {name: dict(median_ms=statistics.median(values), samples_ms=values) for name, values in samples.items()}, orders
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--baseline-ref", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--length", type=int, default=131072)
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=40)
+    parser.add_argument("--topks", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048])
+    parser.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[4593, 17, 2026])
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=15)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    assert args.length % 64 == 0 and all(0 < k <= args.length // 64 for k in args.topks)
+    assert Path(bsa_fwd_sm100.__file__).resolve() == (ROOT / KERNEL).resolve(), "Install this checkout before benchmarking."
+    baseline_sha = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", args.baseline_ref], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip()
+    baseline_source = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"{baseline_sha}:{KERNEL}"], cwd=ROOT)
+    torch.set_num_threads(1)
+    torch.set_grad_enabled(False)
+    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
+    metadata = dict(
+        baseline_commit=baseline_sha,
+        baseline_source_sha256=hashlib.sha256(baseline_source).hexdigest(),
+        candidate_source_sha256=hashlib.sha256((ROOT / KERNEL).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+        imported_kernel=bsa_fwd_sm100.__file__,
+        torch=torch.__version__,
+        cuda=torch.version.cuda,
+        cutlass=cutlass.__version__,
+        gpu=str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)),
+        gpu_start=gpu_snapshot(),
+        arguments=vars(args) | dict(output=str(args.output)),
+        scope="CUDA Graph attention kernel, O and LSE; excludes routing, allocations, compilation and references",
+        flops="4 * B * H * N * topK * 64 * D",
+    )
+    report = dict(metadata=metadata, cases=[])
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

+"""Compare native Sage FP8 KV128 with FP8 KV64 on exactly the same sparse mask.
+
+Run from the repository root on an idle SM120 GPU. Results use paired,
+alternating CUDA-graph replays, not profiler times. Metadata conversion is
+baseline setup only and is never used by the native implementation.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+

+
+
+def _capture(fn, warmup):
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(max(1, warmup)):
+            fn()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        output = fn()
+    return graph, output
+
+
+def _paired_times(graphs, repeats):
+    events = [[], []]
+    for repeat in range(repeats):
+        for index in ((0, 1) if repeat % 2 == 0 else (1, 0)):
+            start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            graphs[index].replay()
+            end.record()
+            events[index].append((start, end))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return [[start.elapsed_time(end) for start, end in pairs] for pairs in events]
+
+
+def _sample_error(q, k, v, outputs, indices):
+    refs, actual = [], [[], []]
+    for head, row in ((0, 0), (0, 127), (q.shape[1] - 1, q.shape[2] - 1), (q.shape[1] - 1, q.shape[2] // 2)):
+        selected = indices[0, head, row // 128].long()
+        tokens = (selected[:, None] * 128 + torch.arange(128, device=q.device)).flatten()
+        scores = k[0, head, tokens].float() @ q[0, head, row].float() * 128**-0.5
+        refs.append(torch.softmax(scores, dim=0) @ v[0, head, tokens].float())
+        for target, output in zip(actual, outputs):
+            target.append(output[0, head, row].float())
+    reference = torch.stack(refs)
+    errors = [(torch.stack(rows) - reference).norm().div(reference.norm().clamp_min(1e-8)).item() for rows in actual]
+    if not all(error < 0.1 for error in errors):
+        raise AssertionError(f"sampled FP8 relative L2 error exceeded 10%: {errors}")
+    return errors
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--sequence", type=int, default=142720)

+    parser.add_argument("--densities", type=float, nargs="+", default=(0.15, 0.2))
+    parser.add_argument("--patterns", choices=("strided", "local"), nargs="+", default=("strided", "local"))
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=21)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 12:
+        raise RuntimeError("this benchmark requires SM120")
+    if args.sequence <= 0 or args.sequence % 128 or args.heads < 1 or args.repeats < 1 or args.warmup < 0:
+        raise ValueError("sequence must be a positive multiple of 128; heads/repeats must be positive; warmup must be nonnegative")
+    if any(not 0 < density <= 1 for density in args.densities):
+        raise ValueError("density must be in (0, 1]")
+    torch.manual_seed(120128)
+    shape = (1, args.heads, args.sequence, 128)
+    q, k, v = (torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") for _ in range(3))
+    quantized = {
+        64: _quantize_sage_bhsd(q, k, v),
+        128: _quantize_sage_bhsd(q, k, v, v_block_size=128),
+    }
+    report = {
+        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "torch": str(torch.__version__),
+        "cutlass": str(_interface.cutlass.__version__),
+        "shape": shape,
+        "timing": "paired alternating CUDA-graph replay; medians; milliseconds",
+        "cases": [],
+    }
+    print(json.dumps({key: value for key, value in report.items() if key != "cases"}), flush=True)
+    for density in args.densities:
+        topk = _rounded_topk(args.sequence // 128, density)
+        for pattern in args.patterns:
+            indices128 = _make_block_indices(args.heads, args.sequence // 128, topk, pattern, q.device)
+            indices64 = torch.stack((2 * indices128, 2 * indices128 + 1), dim=-1).flatten(-2).repeat_interleave(2, dim=2)
+            case = {"density": density, "effective_density": topk / (args.sequence // 128), "pattern": pattern, "topk128": topk}
+            for mode in ("attention_only", "with_quantization"):
+                graphs, outputs = [], []
+                for block_size, indices in ((64, indices64), (128, indices128)):
+
+                    def run(block_size=block_size, indices=indices):
+                        if mode == "attention_only":
+                            return _interface._bsa_attn_fwd_sm120_fp8(
+                                *quantized[block_size],
+                                indices,
+                                indices.shape[-1],
+                                128**-0.5,
+                                sparse_block_size=block_size,
+                                v_block_size=128 if block_size == 128 else 0,
+                            )[0]
+                        return ops.block_sparse_attention_fp8_forward(q, k, v, indices, sparse_block_size=block_size)["o_tensor"]
+
+                    graph, output = _capture(run, args.warmup)
+                    graphs.append(graph)
+                    outputs.append(output)
+                samples = _paired_times(graphs, args.repeats)
+                medians = [statistics.median(values) for values in samples]
+                case[mode] = {
+                    "blk64_ms": medians[0],
+                    "blk128_ms": medians[1],
+                    "speedup": medians[0] / medians[1],
+                    "sample_relative_l2": _sample_error(q, k, v, outputs, indices128),
+                    "samples_ms": samples,
+                }
+                del graphs, outputs, graph, output
+            report["cases"].append(case)
+            print(json.dumps(case), flush=True)
+    if args.output:
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""Time the Hopper Sage FP8 block-sparse attention kernels (blk64 and blk128).
+
+Run with this checkout imported, for example:
+    PYTHONPATH=python python benchmark/bsa/benchmark_sm90_fp8.py --output /tmp/bsa-sm90-fp8.json
+
+Q/K/V are quantized once outside the timed region. Each block size gets its own random
+sparse graph with the same number of active KV tokens per query block, so the effective
+TFLOPS (4 * B * H * Sq * active_tokens * D, sparse QK and PV only) are comparable. Times
+are CUDA-event measurements of warmed CUDA graph replay of the attention kernel alone:
+they exclude quantization, JIT compilation, host allocation and Python launch overhead.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+
+import cutlass
+import cudnn
+import torch
+
+from cudnn.block_sparse_attention._fp8_quant import _quantize_sage_bhsd
+from cudnn.block_sparse_attention._interface import _bsa_attn_fwd_sm90_fp8_blk64, _bsa_attn_fwd_sm90_fp8_blk128
+
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+# (batch, heads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k, active KV tokens per query block)
+QUICK_SHAPES = [(1, 4, 256, 8192, 2048), (1, 8, 2048, 8192, 2048), (1, 8, 8192, 8192, 2048)]
+SHAPES = QUICK_SHAPES + [(2, 8, 8192, 8192, 384), (1, 4, 128, 32768, 8192), (1, 8, 32768, 32768, 2048)]
+KERNELS = {64: _bsa_attn_fwd_sm90_fp8_blk64, 128: _bsa_attn_fwd_sm90_fp8_blk128}
+
+
+def measure(fn, repeats, iterations):
+    """Median/min/max microseconds per call of one captured CUDA graph."""
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            output = fn()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            output = fn()
+        for _ in range(5):
+            graph.replay()
+        samples = []
+        for _ in range(repeats):
+            start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            for _ in range(iterations):
+                graph.replay()
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / iterations)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    # Keep graph outputs alive until the measurement has completed.
+    del output
+    return {"median_us": statistics.median(samples), "min_us": min(samples), "max_us": max(samples)}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true", help="Run only the three smallest shapes")
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=7)
+    parser.add_argument("--iterations", type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=529)
+    args = parser.parse_args()

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""A/B the atomic and deterministic CSA compressor backward class APIs.
+
+The two variants share all input/output addresses. Each round reverses measurement
+order (AB, then BA) to suppress boost-clock/order bias; ``--construct-order`` also
+reverses which independently compiled plan is built first. ``kernel_us`` measures
+only ``execute`` (the atomic dAPE buffer is cleared before its event); ``operation_us``
+includes the atomic path's required dAPE clear and every deterministic reduction
+launch. Allocations and JIT are outside both measurements.
+
+Run this script against an unchanged-source checkout with ``--atomic-only`` to record
+the independent upstream control. The atomic constructor deliberately omits the new
+keyword, so the same script works before and after this change.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+from cudnn.csa import CSACompressorBackward
+from cudnn.csa.compressor.compressor_sm100 import _BWD_ROWS
+
+# On the seeded 1M case, both deterministic trees stay within 2.1e-4 of the
+# FP64 sum while the atomic result varies by more than 1.9e-3.
+_DAPE_FP64_ATOL = 2.5e-4
+
+SHAPES = (
+    ("r4-c2-d128-1x8192", [8192], 128, 4, 2),
+    ("r4-c2-d128-3x8192", [8192] * 3, 128, 4, 2),
+    ("r4-c2-d512-1x8192", [8192], 512, 4, 2),
+    ("r4-c2-d512-3x8192", [8192] * 3, 512, 4, 2),
+    ("r128-c1-d128-1x8192", [8192], 128, 128, 1),
+    ("r128-c2-d128-3x8192", [8192] * 3, 128, 128, 2),
+    ("r128-c1-d512-1x8192", [8192], 512, 128, 1),
+    ("r128-c2-d512-3x8192", [8192] * 3, 512, 128, 2),
+)
+
+LONG_CONTEXT_SHAPES = (
+    (
+        "r4-c1-d128-packed256k-cp32-or64",
+        [1024, 3072, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 135168],
+        128,
+        4,
+        1,
+    ),
+    (
+        "r4-c1-d128-packed1m-cp64",
+        [4096, 12288, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144, 540672],
+        128,
+        4,
+        1,
+    ),
+)
+
+
+def _make_inputs(lens, d, ratio, coff):
+    """Seeded, contiguous class-API inputs."""
+    total = sum(lens)
+    width = coff * d
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(1234)
+    kv = torch.randn(total, width, generator=generator).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+    score = torch.randn(total, width, generator=generator).mul_(1.5).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+    ape = torch.randn(ratio, width, generator=generator).mul_(0.25).cuda()
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, *torch.tensor(lens).cumsum(0)], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    blocks = torch.tensor([length // ratio for length in lens]).cumsum(0)
+    cuc = torch.tensor([0, *blocks], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    total_comp = int(cuc[-1].item())
+    grad_out = torch.randn(total_comp, d, generator=generator).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+    return kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, grad_out
+
+
+def _build_plan(inputs, ratio, coff, deterministic):
+    """Compile one plan; only the deterministic plan receives the new keyword."""
+    kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, grad_out = inputs
+    kwargs = dict(
+        sample_kv=kv,
+        sample_score=score,
+        sample_ape=ape,
+        sample_cu_seqlens=cu,
+        sample_cu_seqlens_comp=cuc,
+        sample_out=torch.empty_like(grad_out, device="meta"),
+        ratio=ratio,
+        coff=coff,
+    )
+    if deterministic:
+        kwargs["deterministic"] = True
+    plan = CSACompressorBackward(**kwargs)
+    plan.check_support()
+    plan.compile()
+    return plan
+
+
+def _event_us(fn):
+    """One synchronized CUDA-event timing sample."""
+    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    start.record()
+    fn()
+    end.record()
+    end.synchronize()
+    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000.0
+
+
+def _dape_fp64_reference(workspace, total_comp, ratio, coff, d):
+    """Sum the reducer's FP32 producer partials independently in FP64."""
+    nelems = ratio * coff * d
+    if ratio == 4:
+        npartials = (total_comp + _BWD_ROWS - 1) // _BWD_ROWS
+    else:
+        # Ratio 128 chooses rows_per_cta from the runtime device shape; its
+        # workspace (like generic ratio 2) contains only the producer planes.
+        npartials = workspace.numel() // (nelems * 4)
+    partials = workspace[: npartials * nelems * 4].view(torch.float32).view(npartials, ratio, coff * d)
+    return partials.sum(dim=0, dtype=torch.float64)
+
+
+def _bench_shape(name, lens, d, ratio, coff, args):
+    inputs = _make_inputs(lens, d, ratio, coff)
+    kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, grad_out = inputs
+    variants = [False] if args.atomic_only else [False, True]
+    if args.construct_order == "deterministic-first":
+        variants.reverse()
+    plans = {det: _build_plan(inputs, ratio, coff, det) for det in variants}
+
+    grad_kv = torch.empty_like(kv)
+    grad_score = torch.empty_like(score)
+    grad_ape = torch.empty_like(ape)
+    workspace_bytes = plans[True].scratch_workspace_bytes() if True in plans else 0
+    workspace = torch.empty(workspace_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") if workspace_bytes else None
+
+    def execute(det):
+        operands = (kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, grad_out, grad_kv, grad_score, grad_ape)
+        if det:
+            plans[det].execute(*operands, workspace=workspace)
+        else:
+            plans[det].execute(*operands)
+
+    for _ in range(args.warmup):
+        grad_ape.zero_()
+        execute(False)
+        if True in plans:
+            execute(True)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    accuracy = {}
+    if True in plans:
+        grad_ape.zero_()
+        execute(False)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        atomic_kv, atomic_score, atomic_ape = grad_kv.clone(), grad_score.clone(), grad_ape.clone()
+        grad_ape.fill_(float("nan"))
+        execute(True)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(grad_kv, atomic_kv)
+        assert torch.equal(grad_score, atomic_score)
+        dape_reference = _dape_fp64_reference(workspace, grad_out.shape[0], ratio, coff, d)
+        accuracy["atomic_dape_fp64_max_abs"] = (atomic_ape.double() - dape_reference).abs().max().item()
+        accuracy["deterministic_dape_fp64_max_abs"] = (grad_ape.double() - dape_reference).abs().max().item()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(grad_ape.double(), dape_reference, rtol=0, atol=_DAPE_FP64_ATOL)
+        deterministic_ape = grad_ape.clone()
+        grad_ape.fill_(float("nan"))
+        execute(True)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(grad_ape, deterministic_ape)
+
+    kernel = {det: [] for det in plans}
+    operation = {det: [] for det in plans}
+    for round_idx in range(args.iters):
+        order = list(plans)
+        if round_idx % 2:
+            order.reverse()
+        for det in order:
+            if not det:
+                grad_ape.zero_()
+            kernel[det].append(_event_us(lambda det=det: execute(det)))
+            if det:
+                operation[det].append(_event_us(lambda: execute(True)))
+            else:
+                operation[det].append(_event_us(lambda: (grad_ape.zero_(), execute(False))))
+
+    result = {
+        "shape": name,
+        "workspace_mib": workspace_bytes / (1024 * 1024),
+        "atomic_kernel_us": statistics.median(kernel[False]),
+        "atomic_operation_us": statistics.median(operation[False]),
+        **accuracy,
+    }
+    if True in plans:
+        result.update(
+            deterministic_kernel_us=statistics.median(kernel[True]),
+            deterministic_operation_us=statistics.median(operation[True]),
+        )
+        result["kernel_slowdown"] = result["deterministic_kernel_us"] / result["atomic_kernel_us"]
+        result["operation_slowdown"] = result["deterministic_operation_us"] / result["atomic_operation_us"]
+    return result
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=30)
+    parser.add_argument("--construct-order", choices=("atomic-first", "deterministic-first"), default="atomic-first")
+    parser.add_argument("--atomic-only", action="store_true")
+    shape_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
+    shape_group.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true", help="Run one generic and one ratio=128 shape")
+    shape_group.add_argument(
+        "--long-context",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Run the unequal packed 256K/CP32-or-64 and 1M/CP64 production shapes",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    shapes = LONG_CONTEXT_SHAPES if args.long_context else (SHAPES[::4] if args.quick else SHAPES)
+    results = [_bench_shape(*shape, args) for shape in shapes]
+    print(json.dumps({"construct_order": args.construct_order, "results": results}, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Measure cuDNN Frontend deterministic Top-K overhead.
+
+The timed region is CUDA-graph replay only.  Compilation, allocation, capture,
+validation, and a 256 MiB L2 flush are outside each measured interval.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import statistics
+import sys
+
+import torch
+from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.indexer_top_k import (
+    indexer_top_k_decode_varlen as topk_kernel,
+)
+
+
+def _capture(call, warmup):
+    """Warm one implementation, capture it, and return its graph and outputs."""
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        for _ in range(warmup):
+            output = call()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        output = call()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return graph, output
+
+
+def _interleaved_median_graph_ms(graphs, flush, samples):
+    """Measure graph replay medians while rotating implementation order."""
+    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    times = {name: [] for name in graphs}
+    names = list(graphs)
+    for sample in range(samples):
+        offset = sample % len(names)
+        order = names[offset:] + names[:offset]
+        for name in order:
+            flush.zero_()
+            start.record()
+            graphs[name].replay()
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            times[name].append(start.elapsed_time(end))
+    return {name: statistics.median(values) for name, values in times.items()}
+
+
+def _validate(scores, seq_len, k, outputs):
+    """Require exact Top-K values, gather consistency, and canonical cuDNN ids."""
+    valid_k = min(seq_len, k)
+    expected = torch.topk(scores[:, :seq_len], valid_k, dim=-1, sorted=False).values.sort(dim=-1).values
+    for name, (values, indices) in outputs.items():
+        actual = values[:, :valid_k].sort(dim=-1).values
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+        gathered = scores.gather(1, indices[:, :valid_k].to(torch.int64))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(values[:, :valid_k], gathered, atol=0, rtol=0)
+        assert torch.all(indices[:, valid_k:] == -1), name
+        assert torch.all(torch.isneginf(values[:, valid_k:])), name
+        if name.startswith("cudnn_det") and valid_k > 1:
+            # The deterministic contract canonicalizes valid local ids.
+            assert torch.all(indices[:, 1:valid_k] >= indices[:, : valid_k - 1]), name
+
+
+def _make_call(scores, lengths, k, deterministic, ordering="auto"):
+    """Compile one fixed strategy and return an allocation-free launch closure."""
+    rows, cols = scores.shape
+    compiled = topk_kernel.compile_topk_kernel(
+        scores.dtype,
+        rows,
+        cols,
+        k,
+        1,
+        return_val=True,
+        deterministic=deterministic,
+        deterministic_ordering=ordering,
+    )
+    buffer = torch.empty(
+        rows,
+        topk_kernel.buffer_numbers(scores.dtype),
+        cols,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=scores.device,
+    )
+    indices = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=torch.int32, device=scores.device)
+    values = torch.empty(rows, k, dtype=scores.dtype, device=scores.device)
+
+    def call():
+        topk_kernel.launch_topk_kernel(compiled, scores, lengths, indices, values, buffer, 1)
+        return {"indices": indices, "values": values}
+
+    return call
+
+
+def benchmark_case(rows, cols, k, dtype, args):
+    """Validate and time every implementation for one Top-K shape."""
+    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
+    scores = torch.randn(rows, cols, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    if args.ties:
+        scores = (scores * 8).round_()
+    seq_len = min(args.seq_len if args.seq_len is not None else cols, cols)
+    lengths = torch.full((rows,), seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    flush = torch.empty(256 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
+
+    calls = {
+        "cudnn_fast": _make_call(scores, lengths, k, False),
+        "cudnn_det_auto": _make_call(scores, lengths, k, True),
+    }
+    if args.compare_ordering:
+        calls["cudnn_det_bitmap"] = _make_call(scores, lengths, k, True, "bitmap")
+        calls["cudnn_det_bitonic"] = _make_call(scores, lengths, k, True, "bitonic")
+    graphs = {}
+    raw_outputs = {}
+    try:
+        for name, call in calls.items():
+            graph, output = _capture(call, args.warmup)
+            graphs[name] = graph
+            raw_outputs[name] = (output["values"], output["indices"])
+        _validate(scores, seq_len, k, raw_outputs)
+
+        # Re-run deterministic graphs and require exact output identity.
+        det_baselines = {name: (values.clone(), indices.clone()) for name, (values, indices) in raw_outputs.items() if name.startswith("cudnn_det")}
+        for _ in range(5):
+            for name in det_baselines:
+                graphs[name].replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for name, (values, indices) in det_baselines.items():
+            current_values, current_indices = raw_outputs[name]
+            assert torch.equal(current_values, values), name
+            assert torch.equal(current_indices, indices), name
+
+        timings = _interleaved_median_graph_ms(graphs, flush, args.samples)
+        return {
+            "rows": rows,
+            "cols": cols,
+            "seq_len": seq_len,
+            "top_k": k,
+            "dtype": str(dtype).removeprefix("torch."),
+            "ties": args.ties,
+            **{f"{name}_ms": value for name, value in timings.items()},
+            **{f"{name}_over_fast": value / timings["cudnn_fast"] for name, value in timings.items() if name != "cudnn_fast"},
+        }
+    finally:
+        for graph in graphs.values():
+            graph.reset()
+
+
+def main():
+    """Run the requested benchmark matrix and optionally write its CSV rows."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, nargs="+", default=[16, 64, 256])
+    parser.add_argument("--cols", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8192, 32768, 131072])
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--seq-len",
+        type=int,
+        help="Effective length for every row; defaults to cols and is clamped to it.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, nargs="+", default=[512, 2048])
+    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
+    parser.add_argument("--ties", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--compare-ordering",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Time forced bitmap and bitonic deterministic ordering paths.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=10)
+    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=30)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--max-det-over-fast",
+        type=float,
+        help="Fail if deterministic / non-deterministic cuDNN exceeds this ratio.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--csv")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
+
+    writer = None
+    handle = open(args.csv, "x", newline="") if args.csv else None
+    try:
+        for rows in args.rows:
+            for cols in args.cols:
+                for k in args.top_k:
+                    if k > cols:
+                        continue
+                    result = benchmark_case(rows, cols, k, dtype, args)
+                    if writer is None:
+                        streams = [sys.stdout] + ([handle] if handle else [])
+                        writer = [csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=result.keys()) for stream in streams]
+                        for item in writer:
+                            item.writeheader()
+                    for item in writer:
+                        item.writerow(result)
+                    sys.stdout.flush()
+                    if handle:
+                        handle.flush()
+                    if args.max_det_over_fast is not None and result["cudnn_det_auto_over_fast"] > args.max_det_over_fast:
+                        raise RuntimeError(
+                            "cuDNN deterministic Top-K missed the performance gate: "
+                            f"{result['cudnn_det_auto_over_fast']:.3f} > "
+                            f"{args.max_det_over_fast:.3f} for "
+                            f"rows={rows}, cols={cols}, k={k}, dtype={args.dtype}, "
+                            f"ties={args.ties}"
+                        )
+                    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    finally:
+        if handle:
+            handle.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Benchmark the compact-H32 SM100 indexer backward interface.
+
+The default benchmark compares two end-to-end paths:
+
+* ``compact_h32``: compact H32 tensors passed directly to the default backend;
+* ``eager_pad_h64``: caller-side ``torch.nn.functional.pad`` to H64 before the

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+"""Measure E2E adaptive Q-pair DSA backward from unmodified top-k rows."""
+
+import argparse
+import math
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from cudnn import DSA
+
+
+def make_pair_indices(q_length: int, kv_length: int, topk: int, overlap: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Build unique adjacent rows with the requested exact intersection."""
+    pairs = q_length // 2
+    shared = round(topk * overlap)
+    offsets = (torch.arange(pairs, device="cuda") * 7919)[:, None]
+    columns = torch.arange(topk, device="cuda")[None, :]
+    first = (offsets + columns) % kv_length
+    second_unique = (offsets + topk + columns[:, : topk - shared]) % kv_length
+    second = torch.cat((first[:, :shared], second_unique), dim=1)
+    rows = torch.stack((first, second), dim=1).reshape(2 * pairs, topk)
+    if q_length % 2:
+        tail = torch.arange(topk, device="cuda")[None, :]
+        rows = torch.cat((rows, tail), dim=0)
+    return rows.to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+
+
+def make_inputs(heads: int, q_length: int, kv_length: int, topk: int, overlap: float):
+    """Create one common input set for both benchmark modes."""
+    dim = 576
+    q = torch.randn(q_length, heads, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+    kv = torch.randn(kv_length, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+    out = torch.randn(q_length, heads, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+    dout = torch.randn_like(out) / 10
+    lse = torch.full((q_length, heads), math.log(topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    sink = torch.linspace(-2.0, 2.0, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    indices = make_pair_indices(q_length, kv_length, topk, overlap)
+    return q, kv, out, dout, lse, sink, indices
+
+
+def make_run(inputs, mode: str):
+    """Create one wrapper closure with reusable workspace and gradient buffers."""
+    q, kv, out, dout, lse, sink, indices = inputs
+    plan = DSA.SparseAttentionBackward(q, kv, out, dout, lse, sink, indices, q_cluster_mode=mode)
+    if not plan.check_support():
+        raise RuntimeError(f"unsupported benchmark case: H{q.shape[1]} K{indices.shape[1]} mode={mode}")
+    workspace = torch.empty(plan.scratch_workspace_bytes(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    dq, dkv = torch.empty_like(q), torch.empty_like(kv)
+
+    def run():
+        return DSA.sparse_attention_backward_wrapper(
+            q,
+            kv,
+            out,
+            dout,
+            lse,
+            sink,
+            indices,
+            dq=dq,
+            dkv=dkv,
+            workspace=workspace,
+            q_cluster_mode=mode,
+        )
+
+    return run
+
+
+def capture(run):
+    """Warm and capture one complete backward invocation."""
+    result = run()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        result = run()
+    return graph, result
+
+
+def elapsed_ms(run, repeat: int) -> float:
+    """Return average device elapsed time over one sample."""
+    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    start.record()
+    for _ in range(repeat):
+        run()
+    end.record()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return start.elapsed_time(end) / repeat
+
+
+def benchmark_case(heads: int, q_length: int, kv_length: int, topk: int, overlap: float, repeat: int):
+    """Compare graph-captured baseline and adaptive E2E latency."""
+    inputs = make_inputs(heads, q_length, kv_length, topk, overlap)
+    baseline_run = make_run(inputs, "off")
+    adaptive_run = make_run(inputs, "adaptive_pair")
+    baseline_graph, baseline = capture(baseline_run)
+    adaptive_graph, adaptive = capture(adaptive_run)

+    adaptive_graph.replay()

+    return baseline_ms, adaptive_ms
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Run a compact overlap sweep for H16/H32 Dqk576."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", default="16,32")
+    parser.add_argument("--topks", default="1024,2048")
+    parser.add_argument("--overlaps", default="0,.2,.4,.6,.8,1")
+    parser.add_argument("--q-length", type=int, default=2048)
+    parser.add_argument("--kv-length", type=int, default=32768)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=20)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    print("heads,topk,overlap,baseline_ms,adaptive_e2e_ms,speedup", flush=True)
+    for heads in map(int, args.heads.split(",")):
+        for topk in map(int, args.topks.split(",")):
+            for overlap in map(float, args.overlaps.split(",")):
+                baseline_ms, adaptive_ms = benchmark_case(heads, args.q_length, args.kv_length, topk, overlap, args.repeat)
+                print(f"{heads},{topk},{overlap:.2f},{baseline_ms:.4f},{adaptive_ms:.4f},{baseline_ms / adaptive_ms:.3f}", flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Heuristics regret: is the frontend's default pick as fast as the best cuDNN path for the same case?
+
+Reads attention_training / attention_inference result CSVs and pairs, per identical case (every configuration column,
+data type included, except the backend and the measurement), the ``cudnn_auto`` row (default dispatch) with the
+``cudnn`` (native backend only) and ``cudnn_oss`` (FROST only) rows of the same CSV. A runner writes one timestamped CSV per invocation, so legs are
+only paired within a file: repeated runs in one directory stay separate cases rather than overwriting each other.
+``regret = t(cudnn_auto) / min(t(cudnn),
+t(cudnn_oss))``: 1.0 means the heuristics picked the faster path; above ``--threshold`` is reported as a misrank.
+A case where ``cudnn_auto`` fails while another leg succeeds is reported as a coverage loss. When ``cudnn_auto`` ran
+the same plan as the faster leg (``backend_detail``), the case is not a misrank whatever the timings say: their
+spread is run-to-run noise, reported as the noise floor the threshold has to clear.
+
+    python -m benchmark.heuristics_regret <results dir or CSV> [...] [--threshold 1.05] [--top 30] [--fail]
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import glob
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+from collections import defaultdict
+
+LEGS = ("cudnn", "cudnn_oss", "cudnn_auto")
+# Measurement / provenance columns; every other column identifies the case.
+NON_KEY = {
+    "backend",
+    "time_ms",
+    "tflops",
+    "gbps",
+    "sol_pct",
+    "max_diff",
+    "num_iterations",
+    "success",
+    "skipped",
+    "error_message",
+    "gpu_name",
+    "cudnn_version",
+    "cudnn_backend_version",
+    "peak_mma_tflops",
+    "backend_detail",
+}
+SHOW = ("config_name", "model_name", "phase", "profile_pass", "data_type", "kv_cache_dtype", "attn_mask", "batch_size", "layout", "kv_layout")
+SHAPE = ("q_seqlen", "kv_seqlen", "q_tokens", "kv_len", "num_q_heads", "num_kv_heads", "head_dim_qk", "sliding_window_size", "thd_min_fill", "kv_min_fill")
+
+
+def _csvs(paths):
+    for p in paths:
+        if os.path.isdir(p):
+            yield from sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(p, "**", "*.csv"), recursive=True))
+        else:
+            yield p
+
+
+def _load(paths):
+    cases = defaultdict(dict)
+    for f in _csvs(paths):
+        with open(f, newline="") as fh:
+            for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
+                leg = row.get("backend")
+                if leg not in LEGS:
+                    continue
+                key = (os.path.relpath(f),) + tuple(sorted((k, v) for k, v in row.items() if k and k not in NON_KEY))
+                ok = row.get("success") == "True" and row.get("skipped") != "True"
+                try:
+                    t = float(row["time_ms"]) if ok else None
+                except (TypeError, ValueError):
+                    t = None
+                if leg in cases[key]:
+                    raise SystemExit(f"{f}: two {leg} rows for one case; cannot tell which measurement to compare")
+                cases[key][leg] = (t if t and t > 0 else None, row.get("backend_detail") or "")
+    return cases
+
+
+def _plan(detail):
+    """The plan name in a backend_detail ("cudnn_auto plan=X" or a bare name); None when unrecorded or unknown."""
+    detail = (detail or "").strip()
+    plan = detail.split("plan=", 1)[1].strip() if "plan=" in detail else detail
+    return None if plan in ("", "unknown") else plan
+
+
+def _label(key):
+    d = dict(key[1:])
+    head = " ".join(d[k] for k in SHOW if d.get(k))
+    shape = " ".join(f"{k}={d[k]}" for k in SHAPE if d.get(k))
+    return f"{key[0]}: {head} {shape}"
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    ap.add_argument("paths", nargs="+")
+    ap.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=1.05)
+    ap.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=30)
+    ap.add_argument("--fail", action="store_true", help="exit 1 when any misrank or coverage loss is found")
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+
+    cases = _load(a.paths)
+    regrets, misranks, losses, same_plan = [], [], [], []
+    for key, legs in cases.items():
+        auto = legs.get("cudnn_auto")
+        ref = {leg: legs[leg][0] for leg in ("cudnn", "cudnn_oss") if leg in legs and legs[leg][0]}
+        if auto is None or not ref:
+            continue
+        best_leg = min(ref, key=ref.get)
+        if auto[0] is None:
+            losses.append((key, best_leg, ref[best_leg]))
+            continue
+        r = auto[0] / ref[best_leg]
+        if _plan(auto[1]) is not None and _plan(auto[1]) == _plan(legs[best_leg][1]):
+            same_plan.append(max(r, 1 / r))
+            regrets.append(1.0)
+            continue
+        regrets.append(r)
+        if r > a.threshold:
+            misranks.append((r, key, auto, best_leg, ref[best_leg]))
+
+    if not regrets and not losses:
+        print("no case has a cudnn_auto row next to a cudnn / cudnn_oss row")
+        return 0
+    gm = math.exp(sum(math.log(r) for r in regrets) / len(regrets)) if regrets else float("nan")
+    print(f"## Heuristics regret (cudnn_auto vs the faster of cudnn / cudnn_oss, same data type)\n")
+    print(f"- compared cases: {len(regrets)}; geomean regret {gm:.3f}; worst {max(regrets, default=float('nan')):.3f}")
+    print(f"- misranks (regret > {a.threshold:.2f}): {len(misranks)}; coverage losses (cudnn_auto failed, another leg ran): {len(losses)}")
+    if same_plan:
+        print(f"- same plan as the faster leg (regret 1.0): {len(same_plan)}; their timing spread, the noise floor: max {max(same_plan):.3f}")
+    print()
+    if misranks:
+        print(f"| regret | case | default pick | faster leg (ms) | default (ms) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|")
+        for r, key, auto, best_leg, tb in sorted(misranks, key=lambda x: -x[0])[: a.top]:
+            print(f"| {r:.2f} | {_label(key)} | {auto[1] or 'n/a'} | {best_leg} {tb:.4f} | {auto[0]:.4f} |")
+        print()
+    if losses:
+        print("| coverage loss | faster leg (ms) |\n|---|---|")
+        for key, best_leg, tb in losses[: a.top]:
+            print(f"| {_label(key)} | {best_leg} {tb:.4f} |")
+    return 1 if a.fail and (misranks or losses) else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
