+# Query Sparse Attention (QSA)
+
+QSA applies attention to the four-token blocks selected for each query. It uses
+the original K/V tensors; block selection is an input and receives no gradient.
+The API follows the Miles packed training interface.
+The source contract is Miles
+[`block_sparse_attention.py` at `0cc6516`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/0cc65167f991ab1f0d228f6c9b648d89bc60a203/miles/kernels/attention/qsa/block_sparse_attention.py).
+
+```python
+from torch import Tensor
+from cudnn.ops import qsa_forward, qsa_backward
+
+def qsa_forward(
+    q: Tensor,
+    k: Tensor,
+    v: Tensor,
+    sel_blocks: Tensor,
+    lo: Tensor,
+    hi: Tensor,
+    blk_base: Tensor,
+    tok_base: Tensor,
+    block_first: Tensor,
+    block_last: Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    block_size: int = 4,
+) -> TupleDict:
+    ...  # out, out_fp32, lse
+
+def qsa_backward(
+    grad_out: Tensor,
+    q: Tensor,
+    k: Tensor,
+    v: Tensor,
+    out_fp32: Tensor,
+    lse: Tensor,
+    sel_blocks: Tensor,
+    lo: Tensor,
+    hi: Tensor,
+    blk_base: Tensor,
+    tok_base: Tensor,
+    block_first: Tensor,
+    block_last: Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    block_size: int = 4,
+) -> TupleDict:
+    ...  # dq, dk, dv
+```
+
+Both calls return a `TupleDict`. Tuple unpacking follows the order above; string
+keys have the same names. Forward and backward are explicit calls. The forward
+call does not register a PyTorch autograd function.
+
+## Finding QSA attention and its indexer
+
+QSA's public functions use the `cudnn.ops.qsa_*` prefix. Their implementations
+live under `cudnn.QSA`; the selector shares scorer and top-k kernels with DSA.
+Choose an entry by its input and saved-state contract:
+
+| Need | Entry point | Contract |
+|---|---|---|
+| Packed training with a block-selection bitmap | `cudnn.ops.qsa_forward`, `qsa_backward` | The bitmap API documented on this page; 12Q/1KV or 24Q/2KV |
+| Packed training with selected token IDs | [`cudnn.ops.qsa_indexed_forward`, `qsa_indexed_backward`](qsa_indexed.md) | 12Q/1KV on SM100/SM103; shares the QSA attention kernels |
+| Generate selected blocks from indexer Q and compressed K | `cudnn.ops.qsa_select_forward`, `qsa_select_decode_forward` | QSA selector over the shared DSA scorer and top-k; returns local block IDs, not token IDs |
+| Decode selection over a paged compressed-key cache | `cudnn.ops.qsa_select_decode_paged_forward` | BF16 indexer cache; see the paged selector's architecture and layout requirements in its docstring |
+| Integrated projection, compression, selection and attention | [`GatedAttentionBlockFwd` with `QsaSpec(index_source="indexer")`](gated_attention_block.md) | Use the integrated block's own architecture, layout and inference support matrix |
+
+**Indexed attention consumes indices; the indexer generates them.** The indexed
+training calls do not run scoring or top-k. The selector's local block IDs need
+expansion to the attention input format, including the incomplete causal tail
+and the packed sequence's token origin. Its standalone wrapper can be imported
+as follows:
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import qsa_select_forward, qsa_select_decode_forward, qsa_select_decode_paged_forward
+```
+
+QSA's selector scores each complete compressed block as
+`scale * sum_h relu(qi[t, h] @ kbar[block])`. The existing
+`cudnn.DSA.indexer_forward_top_k_wrapper` provides this ratio-causal scorer and
+top-k operation with compression ratio four and constant head weights. Sharing
+these kernels avoids a second implementation. QSA-specific compression, block
+visibility and tail handling remain part of the QSA contract; this reuse does
+not make QSA and DeepSeek attention interchangeable. Numerical rounding and
+top-k tie rules must also be checked before replacing an external selector.
+
+The [internal two-pass backend](qsa_two_pass.md) has a different
+saved-state and selection contract: 12Q/1KV or 24Q/2KV, canonical block lists,
+optional packed `cu_seqlens`, and native FP32 saved output / `[Hq, T]` LSE
+(or the earlier BF16 saved output / `[T, Hq]` LSE pair). For 12Q/1KV, the public
+`qsa_indexed_backward(..., selection_mode="causal_topk")` selects this backend
+when the caller declares the stricter [complete-block and causal-tail contract](qsa_indexed.md#complete-blocks-and-causal-tails).
+The default indexed and bitmap calls retain their general selection contracts.
+The implementation remains under `cudnn.QSA`; no public op class or
+algorithm-specific entry is added.
+
+The experimental QSA entries previously under `cudnn.DSA` and
+`cudnn.gated_attention_block.qsa_select*` have moved without compatibility
+aliases. These entries were absent from stable v1.31.0; users of development
+builds should update their imports to the table above. DSA's shared indexer
+APIs remain in DSA. The integrated gated-attention block remains its own API.
+
+## Tensors
+
+`T` is the total packed token count. `NB` is the total number of blocks across
+all sequences. All tensors must be contiguous and on the same CUDA device.
+
+| Tensor | Shape | Dtype | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `q` | `[T, Hq, 256]` | BF16 | Query vectors |
+| `k`, `v` | `[T, Hkv, 256]` | BF16 | Key and value vectors |
+| `sel_blocks` | `[T, NB]` | uint8 | Nonzero selects a global block for that query |
+| `lo`, `hi` | `[T]` | int32 | Inclusive allowed key-token bounds |
+| `blk_base` | `[T]` | int32 | First global block of the query's sequence |
+| `tok_base` | `[T]` | int32 | First global token of the query's sequence |
+| `block_first`, `block_last` | `[NB]` | int32 | Inclusive global token span of each block |
+| `out` | `[T, Hq, 256]` | BF16 | Attention output |
+| `out_fp32` | `[T, Hq, 256]` | FP32 | Output before its BF16 cast; save for backward |
+| `lse` | `[Hq, T]` | FP32 | Natural-log softmax normalizer; save for backward |
+| `grad_out` | `[T, Hq, 256]` | BF16 | Upstream output gradient |
+| `dq` | Same as `q` | BF16 | Query gradient |
+| `dk`, `dv` | Same as `k`, `v` | BF16 | Key/value gradients, summed over query heads |
+
+Q/K/V, `grad_out`, and `out_fp32` must be 16-byte aligned. FP32 LSE and int32
+metadata must be 4-byte aligned. The implementation rejects unsupported layouts
+before launch. It does not copy or repack inputs.
+
+## Selection and components
+
+For query `t` and key token `j`, the Miles block lookup is:
+
+```python
+b = blk_base[t] + (j - tok_base[t]) // block_size
+allowed = lo[t] <= j <= hi[t] and 0 <= b < NB and sel_blocks[t, b] != 0
+```
+
+Metadata must describe a valid packed sequence partition. Each sequence starts
+its own block numbering, including when its first token is not divisible by four.
+Its block spans have at most four tokens; only the final block can be shorter.
+The spans, bases, and token bounds must agree. Values remain on the device and
+are a caller contract. No host read checks these relationships.
+
+Forward uses dense tiles for short key spans and gathers selected blocks for
+other tiles. GPU preparation checks the current K/V values and bounds, then
+builds exact masks. Nonfinite K/V uses the gather path to exclude unused values
+before arithmetic. Both paths compute scaled QK scores, apply the bounds, and
+use online softmax followed by PV. They write FP32 output and natural-log LSE,
+then cast output to BF16. Empty rows produce zero output and negative-infinity LSE.
+
+Backward compacts the current selection, computes
+`delta = sum(grad_out * out_fp32, dim=-1)`, reconstructs probabilities from QK
+and LSE, and forms dQ/dK/dV. Accumulation uses FP32; output gradients use BF16.
+K/V gradient contributions from all query heads are summed. Floating-point
+atomic reductions can change low bits between runs.
+On Blackwell and Rubin, the 12:1 path pairs adjacent queries and gathers their selected
+block union. Owner bits retain each query's mask while sharing K/V loads.
+A device-side K/V scan selects a per-query fallback when nonfinite values are
+present. The fallback reuses the compact union but applies each query's owner
+bits and bounds before dQ arithmetic, preventing a masked NaN from crossing
+between queries or packed sequences. Both launches test the current device flag;
+only one computes gradients. The flag is rebuilt during CUDA graph replay.
+
+For each query head and its shared KV head, the backward equations are:
+
+```python
+S = scale * Q @ K.T
+P = exp(S - lse[:, None])  # zero outside the allowed keys
+delta = sum(grad_out * out_fp32, dim=-1)
+dP = grad_out @ V.T
+dS = P * (dP - delta[:, None])
+dQ = scale * dS @ K
+dK = scale * dS.T @ Q
+dV = P.T @ grad_out
+```
+
+The implementation evaluates these equations in tiles. It does not allocate
+full score or probability matrices.
+
+| Call | GPU component | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| Forward | Tile bounds, K/V checks, exact mask preparation | Private tile modes, key ranges and token masks |
+| Both | Selection compaction | Private block IDs and counts for gathered queries |
+| Forward | Dense or gathered QK, online softmax, PV | `out`, `out_fp32`, `lse` |
+| Backward | Preparation | FP32 `delta`; cleared gradient accumulators |
+| Backward | Gather, probability reconstruction, gradient products | FP32 dQ/dK/dV accumulators |
+| Backward | Final cast | BF16 `dq`, `dk`, `dv` |
+
+The selection bitmap must include any desired causal tail. The implementation
+does not add a tail automatically and does not truncate selection at 512 blocks.
+Pass the same Q/K/V, selection, metadata, and scale to both calls. Casting `out`
+back to FP32 does not reconstruct `out_fp32`.
+
+## Support and execution
+
+Supported geometry is BF16, head dimension 256, head counts 12Q/1KV or 24Q/2KV,
+and `block_size=4`. `T > 0`, `NB > 0`, and `T * Hq * 256 <= INT32_MAX` are required.
+`scale` is a finite host scalar, normally `1 / sqrt(256)`.
+
+The public functions select one of two architecture families internally:
+
+| Family | Forward kernel | Backward kernel |
+|---|---|---|
+| Blackwell SM100/SM103 | `cudnn_frost_qsa_fprop_sm100` | `cudnn_frost_qsa_bprop_sm100` |
+| Rubin SM107 | `cudnn_frost_qsa_fprop_sm107` | Paired `cudnn_frost_qsa_bprop_sm100` (12:1), `cudnn_frost_qsa_bprop_sm107` (24:2) |
+
+Kernel symbols are implementation details; Rubin kernels compile for SM107.
+Rubin compaction scans 16 selection bytes per lane and preserves block order.
+CuTeDSL 4.7 or newer is
+required; Rubin also requires a build with the `sm_107a` target.
+
+Calls allocate outputs and scratch on the input device and enqueue work on its
+current PyTorch CUDA stream. Warm up the chosen head geometry before CUDA graph
+capture. Compiled kernels reuse symbolic token and block extents; metadata is
+rebuilt from the current bitmap on each call. Forward scratch includes an int32
+`[T, NB]` compact-index buffer and int32 `[T]` counts. The 12:1 backward path on both families
+uses `[ceil(T/2), NB]` indices and `[ceil(T/2)]` counts; other backward paths use
+the forward shapes. Backward also uses FP32 gradient accumulators and `[T, Hq]`
+delta. The paired backward safety scan also uses four int32 flags per 1024
+K/V elements plus one reduced flag. The dense route also uses packed token
+masks, tile ranges and K/V check flags. These buffers are rebuilt on each call.
+Full-call benchmarks must include forward preparation, compaction, backward
+preparation, and final gradient casts.
+At `T=131072` and `NB=32768`, the forward compact-index buffer alone uses 16 GiB.

+# Indexed QSA training
+
+These attention calls **consume existing indices**; they do not compute the
+indexer score or top-k. See [QSA entry points and the indexer](qsa.md#finding-qsa-attention-and-its-indexer)
+for block selection, bitmap training and the internal two-pass backend.
+
+`cudnn.ops.qsa_indexed_forward` and `qsa_indexed_backward` accept packed token
+indices directly. The implementation lives in `cudnn.QSA.indexed` and shares
+QSA's attention kernels. It supports BF16
+12Q/1KV, head dimension 256, and SM100/SM103 with CuTeDSL >= 4.7.
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import qsa_indexed_forward, qsa_indexed_backward
+
+out, out_fp32, lse = qsa_indexed_forward(q, k, v, indices, scale=1 / 16)
+dq, dk, dv = qsa_indexed_backward(grad_out, q, k, v, out_fp32, lse, indices, scale=1 / 16)
+```
+
+These explicit calls return `TupleDict` objects in the order shown. They do not
+register an autograd function. Save the original FP32 output and natural-log
+LSE; casting the BF16 output back to FP32 is insufficient.
+
+| Tensor | Shape | Dtype |
+|---|---|---|
+| Q, output, grad_out, dQ | `[T, 12, 256]` | BF16 |
+| K, V, dK, dV | `[T, 1, 256]` | BF16 |
+| indices | `[T, W]` | int32 |
+| out_fp32 | `[T, 12, 256]` | FP32 |
+| lse | `[12, T]` | FP32 |
+
+All tensors are contiguous on one CUDA device. Data tensors require 16-byte
+alignment; indices and LSE require four-byte alignment. `T > 0` and
+`T * 12 * 256 <= INT32_MAX`. Scale is a finite host scalar.
+
+`W` is a positive multiple of four, at most 2052. Each four-slot group describes
+one distinct complete block: `[start, start+1, start+2, start+3]`, or four `-1`
+padding slots. A partial causal tail is a consecutive prefix followed by `-1`.
+Valid tokens are absolute packed token IDs, belong to the query's document,
+and never exceed the query's absolute token ID. A tail begins at the document's
+own block origin; packed document starts need not be divisible by four. Groups
+may appear in any order and padding groups may occur between selected groups.
+Groups must not overlap or repeat within a row. These device-value relationships
+are caller contracts; execution does not read indices back to the host.
+
+The Relax layout with 512 complete four-token groups plus a four-slot causal
+tail fits directly, including invalid tail slots. A 2051-wide carrier must be
+padded explicitly by the caller; this API does not silently convert it. Empty
+rows produce zero output/gradients and negative-infinity LSE. Selection is not
+differentiated. Pass the same selection and scale to forward and backward.
+
+A GPU hash table compacts the selected starts. Backward unions adjacent queries'
+starts with owner bits, retaining each query's bounds and mask. Nonfinite K/V
+uses the device-side per-query fallback described in [QSA](qsa.md). Every call
+rebuilds metadata, including during CUDA Graph replay. Warm up before capture.
+
+The public wrappers allocate outputs and one workspace. The internal APIBase
+plan validates current storage and uses only caller-owned buffers in execute;
+its cache retains immutable geometry and compiled kernels. Indexed metadata
+storage is proportional to `T * W`, independent of the full key-block count.
+At 128K with W=2052, compact IDs occupy 256.5 MiB in either direction, compared
+with 16 GiB for bitmap-forward IDs or 8 GiB for paired bitmap-backward IDs. The
+4 GiB bitmap is also unnecessary. These are metadata sizes, not total process
+memory; saved state, outputs and FP32 gradient accumulators are additional.
+
+## Complete blocks and causal tails
+
+For top-512-block selection, backward can use the bounded-workspace
+two-pass implementation through the same public entry point:
+
+```python
+# cu_seqlens is a CUDA int32 tensor, for example [0, 43691, 87382, 131072].
+out, out_fp32, lse = qsa_indexed_forward(q, k, v, indices)
+dq, dk, dv = qsa_indexed_backward(
+    grad_out, q, k, v, out_fp32, lse, indices,
+    selection_mode="causal_topk", cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+    max_seq_len=43691,
+)
+```
+
+`selection_mode="general"` remains the default. The new mode declares the
+following stricter input contract; it is never inferred from tensor shapes:
+
+- Q/K/V, grad_out and saved FP32 output are finite. LSE is finite and comes
+  from forward with the same indices and scale. The general path's nonfinite
+  fallback does not apply to this mode.
+- `W=2052` and `scale=1/16`. For query position `p` within its document, select
+  exactly `min((p + 1) // 4, 512)` distinct, complete four-token blocks from
+  that document's causal prefix, followed by its incomplete causal tail.
+  Complete blocks fill consecutive groups starting at column zero, in any
+  order. No padding holes or empty selections are allowed. Before 512 blocks
+  are available, pad the unused groups with `-1`; the tail may follow the
+  complete blocks or occupy the last four slots, as in Relax. After 512 blocks
+  are available, the tail occupies the last four slots. Invalid tail slots
+  and all unused slots are `-1`.
+- Packed inputs require `cu_seqlens`: contiguous device int32 prefix sums
+  `[B + 1]`, starting at zero, ending at `T`, and nondecreasing. Empty documents
+  and document starts not divisible by four are supported. Indices use
+  absolute packed token IDs; block origins restart at each document boundary.
+  Without `cu_seqlens`, all `T` tokens are one document.
+- Optional `max_seq_len` is a host integer in `[1, T]` bounding every document
+  length. It defaults to `T`. Every replay must respect this bound. The kernel
+  rereads device `cu_seqlens` on replay; boundaries are not cached.
+
+These device-value promises are caller contracts, not host-side checks.
+Use `general` for arbitrary selections. Passing `cu_seqlens` or `max_seq_len`
+with `general` is rejected because that mode obtains its bounds from indices.
+The new keyword-only arguments preserve existing positional calls.
+
+Sparse 12Q/1KV two-pass execution requires the **CUDA 13 CuTeDSL compiler** in
+addition to CuTeDSL >= 4.7 and SM100/SM103. A CUDA 13 PyTorch build alone does
+not establish the DSL compiler version; unsupported compiler builds are
+rejected before kernel compilation. See [two-pass details](qsa_two_pass.md)
+for the bounded records and workspace sizing. At 128K, 12Q/1KV uses about
+2.487 GiB of workspace, including 0.376 GiB of reusable sparse records.
+
+The indexed entry is useful when a producer already has token IDs. It can be
+slightly slower than the bitmap entry at some lengths. Use the unchanged Relax
+comparison in `benchmark/qsa/benchmark_relax.py` for the intended workload;
+Miles ratios do not establish a speedup over Relax, and attention microbenchmarks
+do not measure selector, TE, tensor-parallel communication or model throughput.

+# QSA two-pass backend implementation notes
+
+The internal backend in `cudnn.QSA.two_pass` computes the gradients of the original
+12Q/1KV or 24Q/2KV, D256 QSA geometry on SM100/SM103. It requires CuTeDSL >= 4.7.0.
+The 12Q/1KV sparse path additionally requires the CUDA 13 compiler flavor
+(`pip install 'nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.7.0'` and a CUDA 13 compatible driver);
+the CUDA 12 flavor is rejected before its known compiler crash. The 24Q/2KV
+path also supports the CUDA 12 flavor.
+It supports one sequence or packed documents described by int32 `cu_seqlens`
+and a host upper bound `max_seq_len`. For the public packed training interface,
+use [indexed QSA](qsa_indexed.md). These are implementation notes,
+not a public API. The public `qsa_indexed_backward` selects this backend for
+12Q/1KV when the caller explicitly declares `selection_mode="causal_topk"`.
+
+All tensors must be contiguous on the same CUDA
+device. The softmax scale is fixed at `1 / 16`.
+
+| Tensor | Shape | Dtype |
+|---|---|---|
+| Q, dout, dQ | `[T, 12 * Hkv, 256]` | BF16 |
+| K, V, dK, dV | `[T, Hkv, 256]` | BF16 |
+| Saved output | `[T, 12 * Hkv, 256]` | FP32 (preferred) or BF16 |
+| Natural-log LSE | `[12 * Hkv, T]` with FP32 saved output; `[T, 12 * Hkv]` with BF16 saved output | FP32 |
+| topk_idxs | `[T, 2051]` or `[T, 2052]` | int32 |
+
+For row `i` at position `p` in its sequence, the indices contain `min((p+1)//4, 512)` distinct complete
+four-token blocks, followed by `(p+1)%4` causal tail tokens, then `-1` padding.
+The four IDs within each complete block are consecutive and begin at a multiple
+of four relative to the sequence origin. Each selected block belongs to that
+sequence's causal prefix. Token IDs address rows of the packed buffer. Up to `T=2051`,
+every row contains its entire causal prefix. The kernel derives the tail from
+the query position; it does not validate these device-value relationships.
+`1 <= T <= floor(INT32_MAX / (12 * Hkv * 256))` is supported. The FP32 saved-output mode reads the same output dtype and head-major LSE
+layout as the public FE/Miles-oriented interface natively, without a cast or
+repack. The BF16 mode retains the earlier internal saved-state contract.
+Selection remains restricted to the canonical complete-block-plus-tail format
+above, and packed execution also needs `cu_seqlens`. The public indexed mode
+requires native FP32 saved state and index width 2052; the more general default
+indexed and bitmap calls retain their existing implementation.
+
+The query-major pass computes dQ and writes BF16 P/dS records. An inverted
+block-to-query index lets the key-major pass accumulate dK/dV locally instead
+of scattering every query's contribution through global floating-point atomics.
+A separate dense kernel handles the early prefix, while long inputs are divided
+into KV passes. The records trade memory for reduced contention and reuse:
+sparse queries are processed in windows of at most 4096 compacted query IDs.
+Each window rebuilds its inverted index and consumes its records before reusing
+the same storage. dK/dV accumulate across windows; the dense prefix is computed
+once. All sequence and window counts stay on the device.
+
+P/dS records are bounded to approximately 0.376 GiB for 12Q/1KV and 0.752 GiB
+for 24Q/2KV. At 128K, total plan scratch is approximately 2.49 GiB and 4.87 GiB,
+respectively, for a single sequence or three packed sequences. Inputs and final
+outputs are additional. Gradient accumulators and sequence tables still grow
+with the total token count; the entire workspace is not constant-size.
+
+The internal APIBase plan retains explicit compilation and caller-owned
+workspace. Execution checks current tensor layouts and storage; it does not
+allocate or read indices to the host. The backend's regressions exercise dense
+and sparse crossovers, changed-input replay and explicit stream handling.
+
+See [all QSA entry points](qsa.md#finding-qsa-attention-and-its-indexer) for
+selection and the other attention contracts.

+# Triangle Attention (SM107)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+`cudnn.triangle_attention` is the AlphaFold-class triangle attention (AlphaFold 3 Algorithms 14 and 15: attention over one axis
+of the pair representation with a pair bias on every score and a key mask) behind the signature of
+`cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_attention` (pinned to cuequivariance-ops-torch **0.12.0**: the same parameter names, order and
+defaults, so a model switches providers by changing one import).
+
+```text
+q, k, v    (B, N, H, S, D)      bf16 / fp16     o[b, n, h, i] = sum_j softmax_j( scale * <q_i, k_j> + bias[b, h, i, j] ) v_j     over the live keys j
+bias       (B, 1, H, S_q, S_kv) the same dtype  the pair bias of outer entry b, shared by its N rows
+mask       (B, N, 1, 1, S_kv)   bool            a dense key mask (False = the key is masked for every query of that row)      -- or --
+kv_lengths (B, N, 1, 1, 1)      int32           right-padded lengths: keys j < kv_lengths[b, n] are live (never both)
+mask, mask_is_prefix=True       bool            the same mask ASSERTED prefix-shaped (True on [0, len), False after): its row lengths are
+                                                derived on the device -- no host synchronisation -- and the call rides the kv_lengths route
+-> o (B, N, H, S_q, D) in q's dtype
+```
+
+The attention core is **not a new kernel**: it is the shipped `sdpa` graph node served by the FROST engine row
+`sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm107` on its 32- / 64-wide head-dim tiles -- the additive bias held as a resident SMEM row-block (or streamed
+per kv tile above the resident budget), the boolean key mask folded into the kernel's bit-word mask, the right-padded lengths through
+the `seq_len_kv` padding path at zero kernel cost. `cudnn.triangle_attention` is the API layer: it flattens `(B, N)` onto the graph's
+batch axis (the `N` rows of an outer entry share one `[1, H, S_q, S_kv]` bias -- the graph's existing bias broadcast; one launch per
+outer entry), chooses the mask path from the arguments, caches one compiled plan per declaration and launches it on the caller's
+stream. The engine row's `Capabilities` and its `mismatch()` are the source of every typed decline below; the same row serves the graph
+form (`graph.sdpa(q, k, v, bias=..., kv_mask=... / seq_len_kv=...)`) with no wrapper.
+
+**Target: NVIDIA Rubin (SM107, compute capability 10.7) only.** Every other architecture is declined with a typed error
+(`NotImplementedError`), never served slowly. The engine row is opt-in: `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1` must be set before
+`import cudnn` (the call declines with that instruction otherwise).
+
+## Mathematics and numerics
+
+For every outer entry `b`, row `n`, head `h` and query `i`, over the keys `j` the mask keeps (all keys without a mask):
+
+```text
+s_j = scale * <q[b, n, h, i], k[b, n, h, j]> + bias[b, 0, h, i, j]       scale = 1 / sqrt(D) unless given
+o   = sum_j softmax_j(s) v[b, n, h, j]
+lse = max_j s_j + log( sum_j exp(s_j - max_j s_j) )                       (fp32, natural log; the class API's optional output)
+```
+
+`k` and `v` may carry fewer heads than `q` (`H_kv` dividing `H`, the GQA fold); the bias may be declared with a head extent of 1
+(broadcast over the heads) and a batch extent of 1 (shared by every outer entry).
+
+Rounding points: the scores accumulate in fp32 (the MMA), the bias enters the fp32 score by one FFMA of `bias * (1 / scale)` before the
+scale multiply (one more fp32 rounding than the eager `s * scale + bias`), the softmax statistics are fp32, `P` is rounded once to the
+io dtype as the second MMA's operand, `o` accumulates in fp32 and is rounded once to the io dtype at the store. **The bias is read in the
+activations' dtype** (bf16 with bf16, fp16 with fp16): the resident block loads the io dtype, so an fp32 bias is **cast once per call by
+the function** (counted, see the layouts section) -- never an fp32 arm of the kernel. `cudnn.triangle_attention.triangle_attention_reference`
+is the fp64 reference with this contract (pass it the bf16 bias the kernel reads). Measured on the test grid (`S` in 64..512 incl. a
+217 tail, `D` in {24, 32, 48, 64}, `B` in {1, 2}, the three mask forms, bf16 and fp16) against that reference: `o` within the engine
+row's own tolerance `atol 5e-2 / rtol 3e-2` (an fp32 accumulation, one 16-bit rounding at the store), the LSE within `1e-4 / 1e-4` --
+the SDPA row's tolerances, not widened for this layer.
+
+### Masked rows: three conventions, documented here, one chosen
+
+A row with **no live key** (a zero `kv_lengths`, a mask row that is all False) is read differently by the three implementations a
+model may have been validated against. This API follows the FROST SDPA invariant for an empty key range; the others are stated so a
+parity test knows what it compares (compare rows **with** keys only):
+
+| implementation | `o` on a row without a live key | `lse` | `max` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **`cudnn.triangle_attention`** (both mask forms) | **exactly 0** | **-inf** | **-inf** |
+| cuEquivariance, `kv_lengths` route | 0 (the row is zeroed by a device epilogue) | 0 | 0 |
+| cuEquivariance, dense-mask route | the uniform average of `v` (a finite `-1e9` is folded into the scores) | -1e9 | -1e9 |
+
+So `mask_to_kv_lengths(mask)` -- the conversion of a prefix-shaped mask into lengths -- changes what a fully masked row reads **on
+cuEquivariance** (uniform average -> zeros) and nothing here (both forms read 0 / -inf). Wherever such rows are padding, which the
+models mask out of the loss and of the next layer, the difference is invisible; a model that consumes fully masked rows should be
+checked against the table. The same contract holds in the forward's statistics, so a backward recomputing `P = exp(s - lse)` from the
+published `lse` yields no gradient into masked keys.
+
+## Served today, and the typed declines
+
+| what | served | otherwise |
+|---|---|---|
+| architecture | compute capability 10.7 (Rubin), the FROST engine row `sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm107` with `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1` | `NotImplementedError` (the instruction / the device found) |
+| dtype | bf16 or fp16 activations, the bias in the same dtype; the function casts an fp32 bias once per call (counted) | `NotImplementedError` |
+| head dim `D` | `D % 8 == 0` and `D <= 64` (the row's 32- and 64-wide tiles; 8 / 16 / 24 -> the 32-wide tile, 40 / 48 / 56 -> the 64-wide one, by TMA zero fill) | `NotImplementedError` quoting the engine (`D = 20`: the 16-byte stride rule; `D = 128`: no bias form on the d128 tile) |
+| `S_q`, `S_kv` | any; a compact bias needs `S_kv % 8 == 0` (the TMA 16-byte row-stride rule) -- the function pads the row otherwise (counted); the bias is resident in SMEM up to the engine's budget per tile (768 kv columns at `D <= 32` for a bias shared by two or more rows of an entry, 384 at `D <= 64`; 384 / 128..256 for a per-entry bias on a single row) and streamed per kv tile above it | `NotImplementedError` quoting the engine where neither bias form fits |
+| `B`, `N`, `H` | any (`B > 1` runs one launch per outer entry; `H_kv` dividing `H`) | `ValueError` on a mismatch |
+| key mask | `mask` (bool, dense -- the in-kernel bit-word path) OR `kv_lengths` (int32, right-padded -- the padding path) OR `mask` with `mask_is_prefix=True` (the mask asserted prefix-shaped: lengths derived on the device, the padding path, no host synchronisation); `mask_to_kv_lengths` converts a prefix-shaped mask with one synchronisation, `prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths` without one | both: `ValueError` (cuEquivariance's rule); a non-bool mask / non-int32 lengths: `ValueError`; `mask_is_prefix` without a mask: `ValueError`; a non-prefix mask under the assertion: `ValueError` naming the rows ONLY with the debug check on (below) |
+| `scale` | any positive finite float (default `1 / sqrt(D)`) | `ValueError` |
+| `return_aux` | `False` only: the row max is a side output the engine's bias arm does not store yet (the d128 tile stores it, the small tiles' bias arm declines it) | `NotImplementedError` quoting the engine ("without the score side outputs") |
+| layout | zero-copy on the token-major form (below); every other layout is repacked by the function with a counted copy | the class API: `NotImplementedError` naming the tensor (never a hidden copy) |
+| device | every `execute` tensor on the device the plan was declared on | `ValueError` |
+| autograd | the forward is served under grad mode (a `torch.autograd.Function` that saves `q, k, v, bias, o, lse`); the backward is a later item of this API | `NotImplementedError` from `.backward()` (never a silent zero gradient) |
+
+## Drop-in function
+
+```python
+import cudnn
+from cudnn import triangle_attention, mask_to_kv_lengths   # or: from cuequivariance_torch import triangle_attention
+
+o = triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, scale=scale)                 # the Boltz-2 / Protenix / OpenFold-3 call, unchanged
+o = triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, scale=scale, kv_lengths=mask_to_kv_lengths(mask))   # a prefix mask as lengths (one host sync per mask)
+o = triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=mask, scale=scale, mask_is_prefix=True)         # the same, derived on the device: no host sync
+```
+
+Signature (cuEquivariance 0.12.0, verbatim -- `kv_lengths` is its eighth parameter, positional-or-keyword there as here; the four
+keyword-only additions are appended, in the order they were added):
+
+```python
+triangle_attention(q, k, v, bias, mask=None, scale=None, return_aux=False, kv_lengths=None,
+                   *, out=None, stream=None, mask_is_prefix=False, check_prefix_mask=None) -> torch.Tensor
+```
+
+`out` writes the result into a caller-provided tensor (stable addresses for CUDA-graph users; copied into when it is not in the
+kernel's layout, counted); `stream` is a raw CUDA stream handle the allocations, copies and launches are ordered on (None = torch's
+current stream). The function caches one compiled plan per `(the q / k / v / bias shapes and strides, dtype, mask form, outputs, scale)` in the process
+(the `k` / `v` shapes carry `H_kv` and `S_kv`: a KV head slice of the same buffer is its own plan),
+allocates the output per call (and the workspace `get_workspace_size()` names: the plan's own bytes plus, on the `kv_lengths` form, the
+Q-side lengths below -- the torch allocator recycles it), and launches. Warm a shape once before capturing a
+`torch.cuda.graph` around the call; the captured graph replays the kernel and follows the inputs' contents.
+
+`mask_to_kv_lengths(mask)` returns `(B, N, 1, 1, 1)` int32 lengths when every row of the boolean mask is a prefix (True on `[0, len)`,
+False after), else `None` so the caller falls back to `mask=`. It performs one host synchronisation (the prefix test): call it once per
+mask, not once per layer.
+
+### The prefix-mask form: `mask_is_prefix=True`
+
+The models' key masks are padding masks -- every row True on `[0, len)` and False after -- and the padding (`kv_lengths`) route of the
+kernel trims the kv loop to the live tiles where the dense-mask route visits every tile. `mask_to_kv_lengths` buys that route at the
+price of one host synchronisation per mask (the prefix test is a device-wide `all`); `mask_is_prefix=True` buys it without one:
+
+- **The contract.** The CALLER asserts the mask is prefix-shaped. The API computes each row's True count on the device -- ONE launch of a
+  small row-popcount kernel (a warp per row, byte loads, `popc(ballot)`, one int32 store into a lengths chunk of the workspace: no cast
+  pass, no staging, no allocation, no host synchronisation, captured by a CUDA graph) -- and binds the counts as the `kv_lengths` form.
+  The kernel is arch-generic (it runs on every CUDA device the DSL targets) and serves any mask layout; the mask is never read on the
+  host, so a captured graph re-derives the lengths from the mask's contents at every replay.
+- **What a violation does.** The count of a non-prefix row is still a length: such a row is served as the prefix of its True count --
+  the WRONG keys, no error. A mask that may not be prefix-shaped belongs on `mask=` (the in-kernel dense mask) or on
+  `mask_to_kv_lengths`, which tests and falls back.
+- **The debug check.** `check_prefix_mask=True` (per call) or `CUDNN_FRONTEND_TRIANGLE_ATTENTION_CHECK_PREFIX_MASK=1` (the environment,
+  for every call that does not decide it itself) runs the prefix test after the derivation -- the device-wide test with its one host
+  synchronisation -- and raises a typed `ValueError` naming the violating `(b, n)` rows. Off by default; never on inside a CUDA-graph
+  capture (`make_cuda_graph` runs it on the warm-up calls only, as the environment decides, and never on the captured call).
+- **Masked rows.** Unchanged: a row whose count is 0 reads `o = 0`, `lse = max = -inf` -- the `kv_lengths` route's convention, which on
+  this provider is also the dense mask's (the table above).
+- **The device-side helper.** A caller that holds a mask and a plan of its own (a `kv_lengths=True` plan, the graph's `seq_len_kv`, or
+  cuEquivariance's `kv_lengths`) gets the same derivation from
+  `prefix_mask_to_kv_lengths(mask, out=None, *, workspace=None, check=None, stream=None) -> (B, N, 1, 1, 1) int32`: with `out` (an int32
+  `(B, N, 1, 1, 1)` contiguous tensor) the call allocates nothing and a CUDA graph captures it; without it the output is allocated (the
+  convenience form); `workspace` is accepted for compatibility with the two-kernel form this function shipped with first and unused
+  (`prefix_mask_workspace_bytes(B, N, S_kv)` is 0: the fused kernel stages nothing); `check` is the debug check (None = the
+  environment); `stream` the raw handle or torch stream the launch is ordered on. Any mask layout is served (a batch slice, a padded
+  row stride, a strided key view); a CPU mask takes torch's reduction; a DSL below the floor is a typed `NotImplementedError` naming the
+  version. It is the sync-free twin of `mask_to_kv_lengths`: that one TESTS the shape and returns `None` when it fails, this one TRUSTS
+  the assertion.
+
+### Layouts: the zero-copy forms and the counted fallbacks
+
+The kernel's TMA descriptors are built from the declared strides, so the layout is part of the plan. Zero-copy:
+
+- **activations** in the **`(B, N, S, H, D)` memory form** presented as `(B, N, H, S, D)` -- the head dim contiguous, the token
+  stride `>= H * head stride`, every stride a 16-byte multiple (a permuted view of a `(B, N, S, H, D)` buffer, compact or padded with
+  gaps; the "layout_left" form the models produce by projecting `z` and permuting);
+- the **bias** head-major with a **contiguous key dim** and 16-byte row strides (`S_kv % 8 == 0`, or a padded row stride);
+- a **contiguous mask / lengths** tensor -- at any base address for the byte mask (the kernel reads it one byte per lane) and
+  word-aligned for the int32 lengths, so a per-entry slice `mask[b:b+1]` / `kv_lengths[b:b+1]` binds as it is.

+# Triangle Multiplicative Update (SM100 / SM103 / SM107)
+
+**This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
+
+## Overview
+
+`cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update` is the AlphaFold-class triangle multiplicative update ("outgoing" / "incoming"
+triangle multiplication, AlphaFold 3 Algorithms 12 and 13) as three FROST CuTe-DSL launches on one stream, behind the
+signature of `cuequivariance_ops_torch.triangle_multiplicative_update` (pinned to cuequivariance-ops-torch **0.12.0**:
+the same parameter names, order and defaults, so a model switches providers by changing one import).
+
+```text
+x [B, N, N, c_z] bf16   (the pair representation; the caller adds the residual to the result)
+ |
+ |  K1  LayerNorm_in over the channel, the gated dual projections (value || gate) for a and b, sigmoid * mul, the pair mask
+ |      -> a, b   channel-major planes [c, B*N, n_pad] bf16                      LayerNorm-prologue dual GEMM (FROST)
+ |  K2  the per-channel contraction   y[c][i, j] = sum_k a[c][i, k] b[c][j, k]   (outgoing)   /   sum_k a[c][k, i] b[c][k, j]   (incoming)
+ |      -> y      channel-major [c, B*N, n_pad] bf16                             ONE batched GEMM (batch = c * B) on the FROST GEMM engine
+ |  K3  LayerNorm_out over the channel of y, LayerNorm_in of x recomputed, output projection * sigmoid(output gate)
+ v      -> out    pair-major [B, N, N, c_z] bf16
+```
+
+Every stage is a FROST kernel; there are no cuBLAS or cuDNN-backend call-outs. K1 and K3 are the two arms of one
+LayerNorm-prologue dual-GEMM body (`cudnn.gemm.frost.ln_prologue`), K2 is the shipped FROST GEMM template compiled for the
+contraction's tile (chosen per N from a measured prototype). The intermediate planes and `y` live in one workspace the
+caller provides (class API) or the function allocates (drop-in).
+
+**Target: NVIDIA Rubin (SM107, compute capability 10.7) and NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 / SM103, compute capability 10.0 / 10.3).**
+The three kernels are the same code on both: the LayerNorm-prologue dual-GEMM body is rendered once per architecture family at the
+part's geometry (Rubin: a 9-deep operand ring in the 327 KiB carveout, 576 TMEM columns; Blackwell: a 6-deep ring -- 4 in the output
+stage -- in the 227 KiB opt-in carveout, 512 TMEM columns, so `c_z = 256` fills the output stage's ring exactly), and the contraction's
+FROST GEMM template sizes its pipeline from the live device. Every other architecture is declined with a typed error
+(`NotImplementedError`), never served slowly. The measured performance below is Rubin's; the Blackwell column of the heuristics is its own
+measured table (every knob swept on a GB200, 152 SMs at a 1830 MHz lock, by the same protocol; the `N < 256` buckets carry the Rubin picks
+until measured there).
+
+## Mathematics and numerics
+
+For every pair `(i, j)` of a batch entry, with `c_z` the pair width, `c` the hidden width, `m` the pair mask (`None` = all valid):
+
+```text
+z_in = LayerNorm_{c_z}(x; norm_in_weight, norm_in_bias, eps)
+a    = sigmoid(z_in . g_in_weight[:c]^T + g_in_bias[:c]) * (z_in . p_in_weight[:c]^T + p_in_bias[:c]) * m
+b    = sigmoid(z_in . g_in_weight[c:]^T + g_in_bias[c:]) * (z_in . p_in_weight[c:]^T + p_in_bias[c:]) * m
+y    = einsum("bikc,bjkc->bijc", a, b)   (outgoing)      /      einsum("bkic,bkjc->bijc", a, b)   (incoming)
+u    = LayerNorm_c(y; norm_out_weight, norm_out_bias, eps)
+out  = sigmoid(z_in . g_out_weight^T + g_out_bias) * (u . p_out_weight^T + p_out_bias)
+```
+
+Parameter conventions are cuEquivariance's: `p_in_weight`, `g_in_weight` are `[2 c, c_z]` with rows `[a; b]`; `p_out_weight`
+is `[c_z, c]`; `g_out_weight` is `[c_z, c_z]`; the LayerNorm vectors are `[c_z]` (in) and `[c]` (out); every bias is optional
+(`None` = zero). The output is not masked (the mask acts on `a` and `b`), and the residual add is the caller's.
+
+Rounding points (all arithmetic fp32 with bf16 storage): LayerNorm statistics in fp32 (two-pass), the LayerNormed operand rounded
+once to bf16 as the MMA operand; `a` and `b` rounded once to bf16 **after** the mask multiplies in fp32 (a zero mask row is exactly
+`+0.0`; cuEquivariance multiplies a bf16-rounded product -- identical for `{0, 1}` and power-of-two masks, one bf16 ulp apart on
+fractional weights); `y` accumulated in fp32 and rounded once to bf16; the gate sigmoid through `tanh.approx`; the output rounded
+once to bf16. `cudnn.triangle_multiplicative_update.triangle_multiplicative_update_reference` is the fp64 reference with these
+rounding points inserted (`rounding="kernel"`) or without them (`rounding="none"`, the pure formula). Measured on the test grid

+1.68e-3 (= the output's bf16 rounding alone); per cell `|diff| <= 4e-3 + |ref| / 64` on all but 0.7..7.6 per million cells, every
+cell within `2e-2 + |ref| / 64` (the tail of bf16 rounding flips propagating through the contraction); relative RMS to the
+unrounded fp64 formula below 2e-2.

+measured neutral.

+## Traffic model and measured performance
+
+Compulsory HBM traffic per call: `18 N^2 C` bytes per batch entry (K1 reads `x` 2 B per pair-channel and writes `a`, `b` 4 B; K2
+reads 4 B and writes `y` 2 B; K3 reads `y` and `x` 4 B and writes 2 B) plus the mask (2 B per pair) --
+`TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateFwd.traffic_bytes()`. The figures below are the shipped heuristics (`recommend`'s pick per cell, no override)
+measured as the base of a sweep pass on ONE GPU of a Rubin node (cc 10.7, 212 SMs, SM clock locked at 2376 MHz and sampled per cell; every
+window CLEAN) against that node's HBM pin of a read + write copy kernel (10 237 GB/s); the competitor is cuEquivariance 0.12.0's generic route
+(its only route on this architecture) measured on the SAME GPU in the same reserved session with the same protocol (graph replay vs graph
+replay; 600-iteration competitor windows so the clock sampler sees the small cells -- the two N = 128 cells at 6000 iterations with the
+sampler's busy threshold at 20 % GPU utilization, because a 36-40 us call keeps the GPU at ~30 % busy and would otherwise leave no clock
+sample; and every competitor cell whose call is under ~200 us (N <= 512 here) in its OWN process at 1200 iterations, because a profiler
+session earlier in the same process leaves CUPTI attached and adds 3.5-4.5 us of launch latency to every later graph replay, which a
+short call cannot hide -- see the paragraph below the table).
+Speed-ups are `t_cuEq / t_FROST - 1` (positive = FROST faster); the all-valid mask, biases present, `c = c_z`. Three columns, three
+measurement states, never mixed: the FROST and cuEquivariance columns are graph replays of the whole call; the per-kernel column is the
+CUPTI device time of each kernel inside the eager chain -- the median over 10 calls with its min-max; under programmatic dependent launch

+2414 MB against 2418 MB modelled at N = 1024 (ratio 0.998: K1 794 MB = 0.98x its model with `x` read once, K2 822 MB = 1.02x, K3 798 MB =

+# Linear Attention
+
+Chunked linear-attention and state-space layers with a recurrent matrix state `S` per (sequence, head), served by the
+open-source FROST kernels (CuTe DSL, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`) through the Python frontend. There is no C++ API for these
+operations. Every variant has a forward, a full backward, and a pair of summary operations for context parallelism.
+
+| Variant | Recurrence (per token `t`) | Python op | Graph node types |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| GDN (Gated DeltaNet) | `S_t = alpha_t (I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) S_{t-1} + beta_t k_t v_t^T`, scalar `alpha_t`, scalar `beta_t` | `gated_delta_net` | `GDN`, `GDN_BWD`, `GDN_SUMMARY`, `GDN_SUMMARY_BWD` |
+| KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) | GDN with a per-key-channel decay `alpha_t in (0, 1]^K` | `kimi_delta_attention` | `KDA`, `KDA_BWD`, `KDA_SUMMARY`, `KDA_SUMMARY_BWD` |
+| GDN-2 | KDA with a per-key erase gate `beta_t in R^K` and a per-value write gate `w_t in R^V` | `gated_delta_net_v2` | `GDN2`, `GDN2_BWD`, `GDN2_SUMMARY`, `GDN2_SUMMARY_BWD` |
+| GDP (Gated DeltaProduct) | GDN with `n = num_householder` beta-gated Householder updates per token, one scalar decay per token | `gated_delta_product` | `GDP`, `GDP_BWD`, `GDP_SUMMARY`, `GDP_SUMMARY_BWD` |
+| Mamba-2 (SSD) | `S_t = exp(A dt_t) S_{t-1} + dt_t B_t x_t^T`, `dt_t = clamp(softplus(dt_t + dt_bias), dt_min, dt_max)`, no erase term | `mamba2` | `MAMBA2`, `MAMBA2_BWD`, `MAMBA2_SUMMARY`, `MAMBA2_SUMMARY_BWD` |
+
+The ops live in `cudnn.linear_attention.ops` and are PyTorch custom operators with autograd formulas; the summary ops
+are `<op>_summary` and `<op>_summary_bwd`. The same node types are available on the Python graph API.
+
+## Support Matrix
+
+Requires an SM100 / SM103 / SM107 GPU (Blackwell data center) and the CuTe DSL runtime the package depends on
+(`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, a required dependency except on Windows ARM64; these kernels need 4.7.0 or newer and the engines
+decline with an error that names the installed version otherwise). On Windows ARM64, the CuTe DSL and TVM-FFI runtime
+dependencies are excluded from the base installation, so the base install does not enable these kernels there.
+One linear-attention node per graph.
+
+| | GDN | KDA | GDN-2 | GDP | Mamba-2 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| io dtype (`q`, `k`, `v`, `O`, `dO`) | bf16, fp16 | bf16, fp16 | bf16, fp16 | bf16, fp16 | bf16, fp16 (`x`, `B`, `C`, `z`) |
+| `q`/`k` head dim `K` | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 128 (`N`, the state dim of `B` / `C`) |
+| `v` head dim `V` | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 64, 128 | 64 (`P`, the head dim of `x`) |
+| grouped query heads | `HK = H` or `HK = HV`; `O` and the states carry `HO = max(H, HV)` | same | same | same | `B`, `C` grouped over `G` with `H` a multiple of `G` |
+| gate `g` | `[T, HO]` scalar; fp32, bf16, fp16 | `[T, HO, K]` per channel | `[T, HO, K]` per channel | `[T, HO]` scalar, on real tokens | `dt` `[T, H]` raw step logits; fp32, bf16, fp16 |
+| write / erase gates | `beta` `[T, HO]`; fp32 or io dtype | `beta` `[T, HO]`; fp32 or io dtype | `beta` `[T, HO, K]`, `w` `[T, HO, V]`; io dtype | `beta` `[T * n, HO]`; fp32 or io dtype | none (`dt` is both the decay exponent and the write strength) |
+| gate forms | `gate_domain` log or linear, `safe_gate` (`-exp(a_log) softplus(g + dt_bias)`), `use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel`, `allow_neg_eigval` | same plus `gate_lower_bound` | same plus `beta_guard` (needs `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`) | same as GDN | `dt_softplus`, `dt_bias`, `dt_min`, `dt_max`, `A` `[H]`, skip `D` `[H]` or `[H, P]`, output gate `z` |
+| `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel` | yes | yes | yes | yes | n/a |
+| recurrent state | `initial_state` / `final_state` `[N, HO, V, K]`, fp32, bf16 or fp16 | same | same | same | `[N, H, P, N]`, fp32, bf16 or fp16 |
+| `state_checkpoints` (`checkpoint_every_n_tokens`) | multiple of 16 | multiple of 16 | multiple of 16 | multiple of 64 expanded sub-tokens | multiple of 128 |
+| `state_indices` (paged state pool, forward only) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
+| `overwrite_initial_state` (in place, inference) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
+| `batch_invariant` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
+| backward outputs | `dQ, dK, dV, dG, dBeta, d_initial_state` (+ `d_a_log`, `d_dt_bias` under `safe_gate`) | same | same plus `dW` | same as GDN | `dQ (dC), dK (dB), dV (dx), dG (ddt), dA, d_initial_state, d_dt_bias, dD, dZ` |
+| summaries (context parallelism) | `<op>_summary(k, v, g, beta, cu_seqlens[, initial_state])` gives `final_state` + `transition` `[N, HO, K, K]` fp32; `<op>_summary_bwd` gives `d_initial_state` + `transition` | same | same | same | `mamba2_summary(x, dt, A, B, cu_seqlens[, initial_state, dt_bias])`; `transition` `[N, H]` fp32, the log2 of the span's decay product |
+
+`T` is the total token count of the packed batch, `N` the number of sequences. Dtypes are kernel-native and strict:
+callers convert, and every gradient comes back in its input's dtype. `cu_seqlens` is int32 or int64.
+
+## Layout
+
+All operands use the packed THD layout: tokens of every sequence concatenated along the first axis, with
+`cu_seqlens` (`[N + 1]`) giving the sequence boundaries. A dense batch of `N` equal-length sequences is
+`cu_seqlens = [0, T, 2T, ...]` over the flattened tokens; no copy is needed.
+
+Operands may be strided views: the engines build their TMA descriptors from the buffer strides, and the only
+requirement is a contiguous innermost (head-dim) axis. A column slice of a wider per-token buffer (for example the
+`q`, `k`, `v` pieces of one fused projection) is accepted directly, forward and backward, without `.contiguous()`.
+Tensors are rank 3 (`[T, heads, dim]`); a hidden-fused `[T, heads * dim]` slice needs a `.view` to rank 3, which is
+free when `heads * dim` is contiguous.
+
+GDP runs on two timelines: `q` and `g` have one row per real token, while `k`, `v` and `beta` have `n` rows per token.
+They come either expanded (`[T * n, ...]`, update-major: the `n` updates of token `t` are rows `t * n` to `t * n + n - 1`)
+or token-major (`k` `[T, n, HK, K]`, `v` `[T, n, HV, V]`, `beta` `[T, n, HO]`, with the caller's token stride), so the
+per-token column slices of a joint `[V | K | Q]` projection (`[T, n * H * D]` viewed as `[T, n, H, D]`) are consumed in
+place; `dk`, `dv` and `dbeta` come back in the input's shape. `num_householder == 1` is exactly GDN.
+
+Mamba-2 uses the SSD vocabulary: `x` plays `v`, `B` plays `k`, `C` plays `q`, `dt` is the gate. The output is
+`y = C^T S + D x`, gated by `z sigmoid(z)` when `z` is given.
+
+## Semantics worth knowing
+
+- **States and checkpoints.** `output_final_state=True` returns the per-sequence state after the last token.
+  `checkpoint_every_n_tokens > 0` also returns the state series, one entry every `n` tokens strictly before each
+  sequence end, as a non-differentiable dump that the backward reuses instead of recomputing. The rows are io dtype by
+  default; every variant also takes `checkpoint_dtype=torch.float32` for fp32 rows (the backward reuses io rows at the
+  chunk cadence and regenerates the dense series from any other rows). `state_indices`
+  turns `initial_state` into a pool `[N_pool, ...]` addressed per sequence, written back in place; forward only
+  and exclusive with checkpoints.
+- **Summaries.** `<op>_summary` returns the end state of each sequence from a given start state together with the
+  span's state-transition operator `transition`: for the delta-rule variants a `[N, HO, K, K]` fp32 matrix (the
+  product of the span's decayed erase steps, in the backward's stored orientation), for Mamba-2 a `[N, H]` fp32 scalar
+  per head (the log2 of the decay product), so that across spans `S_final = S_init * transition + S_H`.
+  `<op>_summary_bwd` is the mirror for the state gradient. Together they implement context parallelism over
+  sequence spans. Both are non-differentiable.
+- **batch_invariant.** Each sequence's results are bitwise independent of the batch composition (whole-sequence
+  scheduling; split-K load balancing is disabled).
+- **Clamps and guards.** Mamba-2's `dt` clamp zeroes the gate gradient where active. GDN-2's `beta_guard` is
+  recomputed, not differentiated, in the backward.
+- **Engines.** The FROST engines are the only engines for these nodes and are pure pass-through: `check_support`
+  verifies the kernel-native dtypes and head dims listed above and declines everything else. A plan can be pinned by
+  name through `plan_name` (for example `gdn_frost`, `mamba2_frost`, `mamba2_summary_frost`).
+
+## Example
+
+```python
+import torch
+from cudnn.linear_attention.ops import gated_delta_net, mamba2
+
+T, H, K, V = 4096, 16, 128, 128
+cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, 1000, 2500, T], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+q = torch.randn(T, H, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+k = torch.randn(T, H, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+v = torch.randn(T, H, V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+g = -torch.nn.functional.softplus(torch.randn(T, H, device="cuda"))
+beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(T, H, device="cuda"))
+
+o, final_state = gated_delta_net(q, k, v, g, beta, cu_seqlens, output_final_state=True, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True)
+o.sum().backward()
+
+P, N, G = 64, 128, 2
+x = torch.randn(T, H, P, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+dt = torch.randn(T, H, device="cuda")
+A = -torch.exp(torch.randn(H, device="cuda"))
+B = torch.randn(T, G, N, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+C = torch.randn(T, G, N, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+y, final_state = mamba2(x, dt, A, B, C, cu_seqlens, D=torch.ones(H, device="cuda"), output_final_state=True)
+```
+
+Benchmarks against the reference implementations are in `benchmark/linear_attention/`.

+## RMSNorm Graph API
+
+`Graph::rmsnorm(x, scale, attributes)` (Python: `graph.rmsnorm(norm_forward_phase, input, scale=None, bias=None, epsilon)`)
+normalizes `x` by its root mean square and multiplies by `scale`. Training also returns `INV_VARIANCE`. Its dims are `x`'s
+dims, with 1 on every axis where `scale` is not 1. Those are the normalization axes.
+
+`scale` is optional. This was verified on Hopper with cuDNN 9.20, 9.24 and 9.27, and on Ampere and Blackwell with 9.27;
+older backends were not qualified. Without a scale, nothing states the normalization axes, so the node accepts only these cases:
+
+- `x` has at most one non-unit dimension after the first, e.g. `{rows, hidden, 1, 1}`. That dimension is normalized.
+- In training, the caller sets the `INV_VARIANCE` dims explicitly, e.g. `{B, S, 1}` for `x = {B, S, H}`.
+
+Any other shape is refused with `INVALID_VALUE`. Pass a scale of ones, or reshape, to get the axes you want.
+
+`Graph::rmsnorm_backward(dy, x, scale, inv_variance, attributes)` also takes an optional `scale` (Python: `scale=None`).
+Without it there is no `DSCALE` or `DBIAS`, so `has_dbias(true)` is refused. The `INV_VARIANCE` dims state the
+normalization axes. Verified on Hopper with cuDNN 9.12, 9.14, 9.18, 9.20, 9.24 and 9.27, and on
+Ampere and Blackwell with 9.27; older backends were not qualified.
+

+### Per-port token origins from the bound ragged offsets (SDPA THD backward, SM80)
+
+A ragged graph binds one ragged-offset tensor per port, and a padded THD layout
+(TE's `cu_seqlens_padded`) puts a sequence's rows somewhere other than
+`prefix(lengths)`. The SM80 backward reads those values on device (issue
+#737). Its existing setup launch, which turns the lengths into the compact
+`cu_seqlens`, also writes one **token origin per port and sequence**,
+`org_p[b] = ro_p[b] × M_p / ts_p` (`M_p` the port's `ragged_offset_multiplier`,
+`ts_p` its token stride in the CALLER's buffer, Int64 arithmetic), into an Int64
+`[rows, B]` workspace region with one row per port that binds offsets. No extra
+launch; the host only binds the current offset pointers, so the origins follow
+the bound values on every execute and CUDA-graph replay.
+
+Two kinds of row origin then coexist. The **internal** packed buffers (the fp32
+dQ accumulator, `do_dot`, the GQA dK/dV partials) stay at `prefix(lengths)`,
+so their sizing and the masks and loop bounds do not change. The **caller's**
+ports are addressed at their origins: the Q/dO and K/V loads, the Stats read,
+the direct-bound dK/dV stores, and the O·dO dot, dQ cast and dK/dV fold, which
+walk `(sequence, row)` over the envelope and touch `origin + row` for
+`row < len[b]` only. Gap rows are never read or written. A staged port (a head
+dim inside the flavor envelope) keeps its origins: the staging copy moves every
+row in place, which is why origins are computed from the caller's token stride.
+
+`tile_dsl.thd.write_thd_port_origins` / `thd_port_origin` are the shared
+helpers; each path materializes only the ports it needs. Whole-token offsets
+are a supported-input precondition of the FROST engines, not a restriction of
+the cuDNN tensor API, and are not checked on device. When the backend cannot
+lower a graph, the Python-side variant-pack order includes each port's ragged
+offset tensor, so the offsets reach the engine as bound slots.

+### Serializing a python-engine plan
+
+`serialize()` / `deserialize()` keep their classic signatures and follow the
+SELECTED plan. A backend plan is the cuDNN backend's blob, as before. A python
+engine's plan is not a blob: it is a deterministic function of the graph and its
+`(engine_id, knobs)`, the pair `create_execution_plan` replays. So its blob
+(`cudnn._plan_serdes`, magic `CUDNN_FE_PYPLAN`) carries:
+
+- **the graph**: every node and tensor of the IR, tensors by uid. A value the
+  format cannot represent exactly (a `score_mod` callback, a framework object)
+  refuses serialization; nothing is dropped. Buffers bound at build time
+  (`_data_bindings`) are not carried; pass them to `execute()`.
+- **the plan**: engine id, engine name (checked on load) and public knobs. Ids
+  and knob values are append-only, so the recipe stays valid on any frontend
+  that still ships the engine.
+- **the kernels** (`include_kernels=True`, the default): the compiled-cache
+  entries the plan's build used (`compiled_cache.record_entries()` around
+  `build_plan`), each with the environment manifest it was compiled under.
+
+`pygraph().deserialize(blob)` rebuilds the IR into an empty graph, installs each
+kernel with `compiled_cache.seed_entry` **only when its manifest equals this
+process's exactly** (the same identity as the cache directory, so a stale
+object is never loaded), then replays `create_execution_plan`, pins it and
+builds it: `compile_cached` hits the seeded entries and still checks each
+record's key. A refused or missing kernel compiles as usual;
+`enforce_precompiled=True` raises instead. Measured on B200 (bf16 SDPA prefill
+b2 h8 s1024 d128): build 3.1 s; deserialize into another process with an
+empty cache 33 ms, with imports already done (a backend plan takes 23-30 ms).
+3 kernels seeded, zero compiles, O bitwise equal.
+
+The kernels are native code: deserialize only blobs from a trusted source. The
+C++ `Graph::deserialize` does not read this format. Running a python-engine
+plan from C++ is a separate problem: the engine's host logic is Python.
+

+"""Host metadata checks; no device reads or DSL imports."""
+
+import math
+
+import torch
+
+
+def check_tensor(name, tensor, shape, dtype, device, alignment=4):
+    if not isinstance(tensor, torch.Tensor):
+        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a torch.Tensor")
+    if tensor.shape != tuple(shape):
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {tuple(shape)}, got {tuple(tensor.shape)}")
+    if tensor.dtype != dtype or tensor.device != device:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} must have dtype {dtype} on {device}")
+    if not tensor.is_contiguous() or tensor.data_ptr() % alignment:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be contiguous and {alignment}-byte aligned")
+
+
+def check_inputs(q, k, v, sel_blocks, lo, hi, blk_base, tok_base, block_first, block_last, scale, block_size):
+    if not isinstance(q, torch.Tensor) or q.ndim != 3 or not q.is_cuda:
+        raise ValueError("q must be a CUDA tensor with shape [T, Hq, 256]")
+    if not isinstance(k, torch.Tensor) or k.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError("k must have shape [T, Hkv, 256]")
+    total, hq, dim = q.shape
+    hkv = k.shape[1]
+    if total < 1 or dim != 256 or (hq, hkv) not in ((12, 1), (24, 2)):
+        raise NotImplementedError("QSA requires T > 0, D = 256, and 12/1 or 24/2 query/KV heads")
+    if q.numel() > 2**31 - 1:
+        raise NotImplementedError("QSA requires T * Hq * D <= INT32_MAX")
+    if q.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        raise NotImplementedError("QSA training requires BF16 q, k, v and grad_out")
+    if isinstance(block_size, bool) or not isinstance(block_size, int) or block_size != 4:
+        raise NotImplementedError("QSA supports block_size=4")
+    if isinstance(scale, bool) or not isinstance(scale, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(scale):
+        raise ValueError("scale must be a finite host scalar")
+    if not isinstance(sel_blocks, torch.Tensor) or sel_blocks.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError("sel_blocks must have shape [T, NB]")
+    blocks = sel_blocks.shape[1]
+    if blocks < 1 or blocks > 2**31 - 1:
+        raise ValueError("NB must be in [1, INT32_MAX]")
+    device = q.device
+    for name, tensor, heads in (("q", q, hq), ("k", k, hkv), ("v", v, hkv)):
+        check_tensor(name, tensor, (total, heads, dim), torch.bfloat16, device, 16)
+    check_tensor("sel_blocks", sel_blocks, (total, blocks), torch.uint8, device, 1)
+    for name, tensor in (("lo", lo), ("hi", hi), ("blk_base", blk_base), ("tok_base", tok_base)):
+        check_tensor(name, tensor, (total,), torch.int32, device)
+    for name, tensor in (("block_first", block_first), ("block_last", block_last)):
+        check_tensor(name, tensor, (blocks,), torch.int32, device)
+    return total, hq, hkv, blocks

+    hi,
+    bases,
+    origins,

+    last,

+                marked = packed[item] != 0

+                marked = sel[Int64(row), Int64(block)] != 0
+            if marked:
+                take = (last[block] >= low) & (first[block] <= high) & (low <= high)
+        chosen.append(take)
+
+    hits = Int32(0)
+    for item in cutlass.range_constexpr(16):
+        if chosen[item]:
+            hits = hits + 1
+
+    inclusive = hits
+    for offset in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16):
+        prior = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_up(inclusive, offset)
+        if lane >= offset:
+            inclusive = inclusive + prior
+    output = count + inclusive - hits
+    local = Int32(0)
+    for item in cutlass.range_constexpr(16):
+        if chosen[item]:
+            ids[Int64(row), Int64(output + local)] = base + item
+            local = local + 1
+    return count + Int32(cute.arch.shuffle_sync(inclusive, 31))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _compact_row(
+    sel: cute.Tensor,
+    lo: cute.Tensor,
+    hi: cute.Tensor,
+    first: cute.Tensor,
+    last: cute.Tensor,
+    ids: cute.Tensor,
+    counts: cute.Tensor,
+    row: Int64,
+    lane: Int32,
+    vectorized: cutlass.Constexpr = False,
+):
+    low, high = lo[row], hi[row]
+    count = Int32(0)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(vectorized):
+        bulk = (Int32(sel.shape[1]) // 512) * 512
+        for start in cutlass.range(0, bulk, 512, unroll=1):
+            count = _compact_chunk(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, row, lane, start + lane * 16, count, True)
+        count = _compact_chunk(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, row, lane, bulk + lane * 16, count, False)
+    else:
+        lower_lanes = (Uint32(1) << Uint32(lane)) - Uint32(1)
+        for start in cutlass.range(0, Int32(sel.shape[1]), 32, unroll=1):
+            block = start + lane
+            selected = Boolean(False)
+            if block < sel.shape[1]:
+                selected = (sel[Int64(row), Int64(block)] != 0) & (last[block] >= low) & (first[block] <= high) & (low <= high)
+            ballot = Uint32(cute.arch.vote_ballot_sync(selected))
+            if selected:
+                offset = count + Int32(cute.arch.popc(ballot & lower_lanes))
+                ids[Int64(row), Int64(offset)] = block
+            count = count + Int32(cute.arch.popc(ballot))
+    if lane == 0:
+        counts[row] = count
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_qsa_compact(
+    sel: cute.Tensor,
+    lo: cute.Tensor,
+    hi: cute.Tensor,
+    first: cute.Tensor,
+    last: cute.Tensor,
+    ids: cute.Tensor,
+    counts: cute.Tensor,
+    mode,
+    vectorized: cutlass.Constexpr = False,
+):
+    tid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
+    rows_per_warp = cutlass.const_expr(8 if mode is not None else 1)
+    row0 = cute.arch.block_idx()[0] * (4 * rows_per_warp) + tid // 32
+    lane = tid % 32
+    active = row0 < sel.shape[0]
+    if cutlass.const_expr(mode is not None):
+        if active:
+            active = mode[Int64(row0 // 128)] != 0
+    if active:
+        for step in cutlass.range(rows_per_warp, unroll=1):
+            row = row0 + step * 4
+            if row < sel.shape[0]:
+                _compact_row(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, Int64(row), Int32(lane), vectorized)
+
+
+frost_qsa_compact.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _compact_host(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, stream: cuda.CUstream, vectorized: cutlass.Constexpr = False):
+    frost_qsa_compact(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, None, vectorized).launch(
+        grid=(cute.ceil_div(sel.shape[0], 4), 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream
+    )
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _compact_gated_host(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, mode, stream: cuda.CUstream, vectorized: cutlass.Constexpr = False):
+    frost_qsa_compact(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, mode, vectorized).launch(
+        grid=(cute.ceil_div(sel.shape[0], 32), 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream
+    )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def _compile_args(gated):
+    """Cache storage-free signatures; compiled objects use the shared cache."""
+    total, blocks = cute.sym_int64(), cute.sym_int64()
+
+    def tensor(dtype, shape, alignment=4):
+        return make_fake_compact_tensor(dtype, shape, stride_order=tuple(reversed(range(len(shape)))), assumed_align=alignment)
+
+    sel = tensor(cutlass.Uint8, (total, blocks), 1)
+    rows, spans = tensor(Int32, (total,)), tensor(Int32, (blocks,))
+    ids = tensor(Int32, (total, blocks))
+    args = (sel, rows, rows, spans, spans, ids, rows)
+    if gated:
+        args += (tensor(Int32, (cute.sym_int64(),)),)
+    return (*args, make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False))
+
+
+def compile_kernel(arch, gated=False):
+    key = template_key(globals(), locals(), "compile_kernel")
+    return compile_cached(
+        _compact_gated_host if gated else _compact_host,
+        *_compile_args(gated),
+        arch == 107,
+        options=f"--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch=sm_{arch}a",
+        cache_key=key,
+        symbol="qsa_compact",
+    )
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_qsa_compact_group(
+    sel: cute.Tensor,
+    lo: cute.Tensor,
+    hi: cute.Tensor,
+    first: cute.Tensor,
+    last: cute.Tensor,
+    ids: cute.Tensor,
+    counts: cute.Tensor,
+    total: Int32,
+    NQ: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    BLK_BITS: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+):
+    """Union the selections of NQ consecutive queries; tag each block with its owners."""
+    tid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
+    group = cute.arch.block_idx()[0] * 4 + tid // 32
+    lane = tid % 32
+    if group < ids.shape[0]:
+        base = Int32(group) * Int32(NQ)
+        rows, lows, highs, live = [], [], [], []
+        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(NQ):
+            row = base + i
+            inside = row < total
+            if not inside:
+                row = total - 1
+            rows.append(row)
+            lows.append(lo[row])
+            highs.append(hi[row])
+            live.append(inside)
+        count = Int32(0)
+        lower_lanes = (Uint32(1) << Uint32(lane)) - Uint32(1)
+        for start in cutlass.range(0, Int32(sel.shape[1]), 32, unroll=1):
+            block = start + lane
+            mask = Int32(0)
+            if block < sel.shape[1]:
+                begin, end = first[block], last[block]
+                for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(NQ):
+                    taken = live[i] & (end >= lows[i]) & (begin <= highs[i]) & (lows[i] <= highs[i])
+                    if taken:
+                        taken = sel[Int64(rows[i]), Int64(block)] != 0
+                    if taken:
+                        mask = mask | Int32(1 << i)
+            selected = mask != Int32(0)
+            ballot = Uint32(cute.arch.vote_ballot_sync(selected))
+            if selected:
+                offset = count + Int32(cute.arch.popc(ballot & lower_lanes))
+                ids[Int64(group), Int64(offset)] = block | (mask << Int32(BLK_BITS))
+            count = count + Int32(cute.arch.popc(ballot))
+        if lane == 0:
+            counts[group] = count
+
+
+frost_qsa_compact_group.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _compact_group_host(
+    sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, total: Int32, stream: cuda.CUstream, NQ: cutlass.Constexpr[int], BLK_BITS: cutlass.Constexpr[int]
+):
+    frost_qsa_compact_group(sel, lo, hi, first, last, ids, counts, total, NQ, BLK_BITS).launch(
+        grid=(cute.ceil_div(ids.shape[0], 4), 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream
+    )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def _compile_group_args():
+    """Cache storage-free grouped signatures."""
+    total, blocks, groups = cute.sym_int64(), cute.sym_int64(), cute.sym_int64()
+
+    def tensor(dtype, shape, alignment=4):
+        return make_fake_compact_tensor(dtype, shape, stride_order=tuple(reversed(range(len(shape)))), assumed_align=alignment)
+
+    sel = tensor(cutlass.Uint8, (total, blocks), 1)
+    rows, spans = tensor(Int32, (total,)), tensor(Int32, (blocks,))
+    ids = tensor(Int32, (groups, blocks))
+    gcounts = tensor(Int32, (groups,))
+    return (
+        sel,
+        rows,
+        rows,
+        spans,
+        spans,
+        ids,
+        gcounts,
+        Int32(1),
+        make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False),
+    )
+
+
+def compile_group_kernel(arch, nq, blk_bits):
+    key = template_key(globals(), {"arch": arch, "nq": nq, "blk_bits": blk_bits}, "compile_group_kernel")
+    return compile_cached(
+        _compact_group_host,
+        *_compile_group_args(),
+        nq,
+        blk_bits,
+        options=f"--enable-tvm-ffi --gpu-arch=sm_{arch}a",
+        cache_key=key,
+        symbol="qsa_compact_group",
+    )

+"""Miles-compatible packed QSA forward and backward."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+import torch
+from torch import Tensor
+
+from cudnn._device import device_info
+
+from ._contract import check_inputs, check_tensor
+
+
+def _implementation(q, direction):
+    from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_arch_requirement_error, cutedsl_requirement_error, cutedsl_state, cutedsl_too_old
+
+    installed, version = cutedsl_state()
+    if not installed or cutedsl_too_old(version):
+        raise ImportError(cutedsl_requirement_error("QSA") or "QSA requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl")
+    cc = device_info(q.device.index).compute_capability
+    if cc not in ((10, 0), (10, 3), (10, 7)):
+        raise NotImplementedError(f"QSA requires SM100, SM103 or SM107, got SM{cc[0]}{cc[1]}")
+    reason = cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc)
+    if reason:
+        raise NotImplementedError(reason)
+    arch = cc[0] * 10 + cc[1]
+    family = 107 if arch == 107 else 100
+    if direction == "bprop" and q.shape[1] == 12:
+        family = 100
+    return importlib.import_module(f".kernels.{direction}_sm{family}", __package__), arch
+
+
+def _compact(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, arch, stream):
+    from ._metadata import compile_kernel
+
+    ids = torch.empty(sel_blocks.shape, dtype=torch.int32, device=sel_blocks.device)
+    counts = torch.empty((sel_blocks.shape[0],), dtype=torch.int32, device=sel_blocks.device)
+    compile_kernel(arch)(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, ids, counts, stream)
+    return ids, counts
+
+
+def _compact_backward(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, arch, stream, kv_heads):
+    if kv_heads == 1:
+        from ._metadata import compile_group_kernel
+        from .kernels.bprop_sm100 import NQ, BLK_BITS
+
+        total, blocks = sel_blocks.shape
+        if blocks > 1 << BLK_BITS:
+            raise NotImplementedError(f"Paired QSA requires NB <= {1 << BLK_BITS} for block-owner encoding")
+        groups = (total + NQ - 1) // NQ
+        ids = torch.empty((groups, blocks), dtype=torch.int32, device=sel_blocks.device)
+        counts = torch.empty(groups, dtype=torch.int32, device=sel_blocks.device)
+        compile_group_kernel(arch, NQ, BLK_BITS)(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, ids, counts, total, stream)
+        return ids, counts
+    return _compact(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, arch, stream)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _forward_runtime():
+    """Resolve forward imports after the DSL gate."""
+    from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda
+    from cudnn.api_base import TupleDict, _raw_stream
+    from . import _forward
+
+    return cuda, TupleDict, _raw_stream, _forward
+
+
+def qsa_forward(
+    q: Tensor,
+    k: Tensor,
+    v: Tensor,
+    sel_blocks: Tensor,
+    lo: Tensor,
+    hi: Tensor,
+    blk_base: Tensor,
+    tok_base: Tensor,
+    block_first: Tensor,
+    block_last: Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    block_size: int = 4,
+) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]:
+    """Return ``(out, out_fp32, lse)`` for packed THD QSA.
+
+    Selection and inclusive token bounds follow Miles. Block spans and bases must
+    describe the same packed sequences. See ``docs/fe-oss-apis/qsa.md``.
+    """
+    total, hq, hkv, _ = check_inputs(q, k, v, sel_blocks, lo, hi, blk_base, tok_base, block_first, block_last, scale, block_size)
+    with torch.cuda.device(q.device):
+        impl, arch = _implementation(q, "fprop")
+        cuda, TupleDict, raw_stream, _forward = _forward_runtime()
+        stream = cuda.CUstream(raw_stream(torch)(q.device.index))
+        out, out_fp32 = torch.empty_like(q), torch.empty_like(q, dtype=torch.float32)
+        lse = torch.empty((hq, total), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+        _forward.launch(impl, arch, q, k, v, sel_blocks, lo, hi, blk_base, tok_base, block_first, block_last, out, out_fp32, lse, float(scale), stream)
+        return TupleDict(out=out, out_fp32=out_fp32, lse=lse)
+
+
+def qsa_backward(
+    grad_out: Tensor,
+    q: Tensor,
+    k: Tensor,
+    v: Tensor,
+    out_fp32: Tensor,
+    lse: Tensor,
+    sel_blocks: Tensor,
+    lo: Tensor,
+    hi: Tensor,
+    blk_base: Tensor,
+    tok_base: Tensor,
+    block_first: Tensor,
+    block_last: Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    block_size: int = 4,
+) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]:
+    """Return ``(dq, dk, dv)`` using forward's FP32 output and natural-log LSE."""
+    total, hq, hkv, _ = check_inputs(q, k, v, sel_blocks, lo, hi, blk_base, tok_base, block_first, block_last, scale, block_size)
+    check_tensor("grad_out", grad_out, q.shape, q.dtype, q.device, 16)
+    check_tensor("out_fp32", out_fp32, q.shape, torch.float32, q.device, 16)
+    check_tensor("lse", lse, (hq, total), torch.float32, q.device)
+    with torch.cuda.device(q.device):
+        impl, arch = _implementation(q, "bprop")
+        import cutlass
+        from cuda.bindings import driver as cuda
+        from cudnn.api_base import TupleDict
+
+        stream = cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream(q.device).cuda_stream)
+        compiled = impl.compile_kernel(cutlass.BFloat16, hq, hkv, arch)
+        dq, dk, dv = torch.empty_like(q), torch.empty_like(k), torch.empty_like(v)
+        scratch = {
+            "delta": torch.empty((total, hq), dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device),
+            "dq_acc": torch.empty_like(q, dtype=torch.float32),
+            "dk_acc": torch.empty_like(k, dtype=torch.float32),
+            "dv_acc": torch.empty_like(v, dtype=torch.float32),
+        }
+        ids, counts = _compact_backward(sel_blocks, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, arch, stream, hkv)
+        num_sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(q.device).multi_processor_count
+        impl.launch(
+            compiled, grad_out, q, k, v, out_fp32, lse, ids, counts, lo, hi, block_first, block_last, dq, dk, dv, scratch, float(scale), stream, num_sms
+        )
+        return TupleDict(dq=dq, dk=dk, dv=dv)
