+The twin cuts the rank's ``[q_proj | k_proj | v_proj]`` rows and hands them to ``qkvg_from_hf``, so every cell here is a BITWISE pin:
+against ``qkvg_from_hf`` on the same HF tensors (the model's own per-head ``[q_h | gate_h]`` split, the ``(1 + w)`` norm form),
+against an independent spelling of the row permutation, and against the shard of the TP 1 ``W_qkvg`` -- at TP 1 and at the rank
+slices vLLM's ``QKVParallelLinear`` loads (the q shard by rank, the k / v shard by ``rank // num_kv_head_replicas``) of the 32 / 2 and
+24 / 2 geometries; the indexer band in both of its forms; the refusals, each naming the fix.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import warnings
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from cudnn.gated_attention_block import (
+    GatedAttentionBlockGeometry,
+    ProjBlock,
+    QsaSpec,
+    build_fused_qkvg_weight,
+    qkvg_from_hf,
+    qkvg_from_vllm,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+# The two serving geometries at TP 1 (d_head 256, RoPE on the first 64 dims): 32 query heads over 2 KV heads at d_model 4096, and
+# 24 over 2 at d_model 2560.  Their rank slices below follow the serving stack's shard rule.
+GEOM_32_2 = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=4096, h_q=32, h_kv=2, d_head=256, rope_dim=64)
+GEOM_24_2 = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=2560, h_q=24, h_kv=2, d_head=256, rope_dim=64)
+GEOMS = {"32_2": GEOM_32_2, "24_2": GEOM_24_2}
+# A small geometry for the arithmetic cells, and its indexer-band twin (a 192-column band keeps the 64-column tile alignment).
+GEOM_SMALL = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=256, h_q=4, h_kv=2, d_head=64, rope_dim=16)
+GEOM_SMALL_BAND = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(
+    d_model=256, h_q=4, h_kv=2, d_head=64, rope_dim=16, qsa=QsaSpec(index_band=True, index_heads=2, index_head_dim=64)
+)
+
+# The stage-(1) width of every rank slice (TP, h_q / h_kv -> n_qkvg): (2 h_q + 2 h_kv) x 256.
+RANK_WIDTHS = {("32_2", 1): 17408, ("32_2", 2): 8704, ("32_2", 4): 4608, ("32_2", 8): 2560, ("24_2", 1): 13312, ("24_2", 2): 6656, ("24_2", 4): 3584}
+
+
+class HfLayer(NamedTuple):
+    """One HF attention layer's weights at TP 1: the double-width ``q_proj`` (per-head ``[q_h | gate_h]``), ``k_proj``, ``v_proj``, the
+    two zero-centered QK-norm weights."""
+
+    q_proj: torch.Tensor
+    k_proj: torch.Tensor
+    v_proj: torch.Tensor
+    q_norm: torch.Tensor
+    k_norm: torch.Tensor
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def _hf_layer(name: str, seed: int = 0, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16) -> HfLayer:
+    """ONE CPU generator per geometry; the projections drawn in fp32 and rounded once into the checkpoint dtype (bf16)."""
+    g = GEOMS[name]
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+
+    def randn(*shape, std):
+        return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=gen, dtype=torch.float32) * std).to(dtype)
+
+    return HfLayer(
+        q_proj=randn(2 * hq * d, dm, std=0.02),
+        k_proj=randn(hkv * d, dm, std=0.02),
+        v_proj=randn(hkv * d, dm, std=0.02),
+        q_norm=torch.randn(d, generator=gen) * 0.1,
+        k_norm=torch.randn(d, generator=gen) * 0.1,
+    )
+
+
+def _merged(q, k, v):
+    """The serving stack's merged ``qkv_proj.weight``: ``[q_proj | k_proj | v_proj]`` along the rows, the per-head gate interleave kept."""
+    return torch.cat([q, k, v], dim=0).contiguous()
+
+
+def _rank_slices(hf: HfLayer, g_full: GatedAttentionBlockGeometry, tp: int, rank: int):
+    """The HF rows a serving stack's QKV linear gives rank ``rank`` of ``tp``, and the rank's geometry.
+
+    The q shard of rank ``r`` is rows ``[r * 2 h_q_r D, (r + 1) * 2 h_q_r D)`` of ``q_proj`` -- the per-head rows of query heads
+    ``[r h_q_r, (r + 1) h_q_r)`` -- and the k / v shard is KV head group ``r // num_kv_head_replicas``: one KV head per rank, replicated
+    ``tp / H_kv`` times, when ``tp >= H_kv``; ``H_kv / tp`` heads per rank otherwise.
+    """
+    d = g_full.d_head
+    assert g_full.h_q % tp == 0
+    hq_r = g_full.h_q // tp
+    if tp >= g_full.h_kv:
+        assert tp % g_full.h_kv == 0
+        hkv_r, replicas = 1, tp // g_full.h_kv
+    else:
+        assert g_full.h_kv % tp == 0
+        hkv_r, replicas = g_full.h_kv // tp, 1
+    kv_rank = rank // replicas
+    q = hf.q_proj[rank * 2 * hq_r * d : (rank + 1) * 2 * hq_r * d]
+    k = hf.k_proj[kv_rank * hkv_r * d : (kv_rank + 1) * hkv_r * d]
+    v = hf.v_proj[kv_rank * hkv_r * d : (kv_rank + 1) * hkv_r * d]
+    g_r = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=g_full.d_model, h_q=hq_r, h_kv=hkv_r, d_head=d, rope_dim=g_full.rope_dim)
+    return q, k, v, g_r, kv_rank
+
+
+def _permute_rows(w_merged: torch.Tensor, g: GatedAttentionBlockGeometry) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """An independent spelling of the permutation: split ``[2 q | kv | kv]``, view the Q block per head, cut ``[:D]`` / ``[D:]``,
+    concatenate ``Q | GATE | K | V``."""
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    q_gate, w_k, w_v = torch.split(w_merged, [2 * hq * d, hkv * d, hkv * d], dim=0)
+    per_head = q_gate.reshape(hq, 2 * d, dm)
+    return torch.cat([per_head[:, :d].reshape(hq * d, dm), per_head[:, d:].reshape(hq * d, dm), w_k, w_v], dim=0).contiguous()
+
+
+def _shard_of_the_tp1_weight(w_qkvg_tp1: torch.Tensor, g_full: GatedAttentionBlockGeometry, g_r: GatedAttentionBlockGeometry, rank: int, kv_rank: int):
+    """The rank's ``W_qkvg`` read out of the TP 1 one: the rank's query heads from the Q and GATE bands, its KV head group from K and V."""
+    d = g_full.d_head
+    o_q, o_g, o_k, o_v = g_full.qkvg_offsets
+    q_rows = slice(rank * g_r.h_q * d, (rank + 1) * g_r.h_q * d)
+    kv_rows = slice(kv_rank * g_r.h_kv * d, (kv_rank + 1) * g_r.h_kv * d)
+    return torch.cat(
+        [
+            w_qkvg_tp1[o_q:o_g][q_rows],
+            w_qkvg_tp1[o_g:o_k][q_rows],
+            w_qkvg_tp1[o_k:o_v][kv_rows],
+            w_qkvg_tp1[o_v:][kv_rows],
+        ],
+        dim=0,
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_three_equal(got, want):
+    for a, b, what in zip(got, want, ("w_qkvg", "w_q_norm", "w_k_norm")):
+        assert (a is None) == (b is None), what
+        if a is not None:
+            assert a.dtype == b.dtype and a.shape == b.shape and a.is_contiguous(), what
+            assert torch.equal(a, b), what
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# TP 1 and the rank slices: bitwise qkvg_from_hf, the independent permutation, the shard of the TP 1 weight
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", sorted(GEOMS))
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_is_bitwise_qkvg_from_hf_at_tp1(name):
+    g = GEOMS[name]
+    hf = _hf_layer(name)
+    merged = _merged(hf.q_proj, hf.k_proj, hf.v_proj)
+    assert merged.shape == (g.n_qkvg, g.d_model) == (RANK_WIDTHS[name, 1], g.d_model)
+    with warnings.catch_warnings():
+        warnings.simplefilter("error")  # the layout is fixed: no FutureWarning about an omitted q_gate_layout, ever
+        got = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, hf.q_norm, hf.k_norm, g)
+    want = qkvg_from_hf(hf.q_proj, hf.k_proj, hf.v_proj, hf.q_norm, hf.k_norm, g)
+    _assert_three_equal(got, want)
+    w_qkvg, w_q_norm, w_k_norm = got
+    assert w_qkvg.shape == merged.shape and w_qkvg.dtype == merged.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and w_qkvg.is_contiguous()
+    assert torch.equal(w_qkvg, _permute_rows(merged, g))
+    # A permutation of the input: K and V rows untouched, the Q / GATE bands a reordering of the q_proj rows, nothing else.
+    o_q, o_g, o_k, o_v = g.qkvg_offsets
+    assert torch.equal(w_qkvg[o_k:], merged[2 * g.h_q * g.d_head :])
+    assert not torch.equal(w_qkvg[:o_k], merged[: 2 * g.h_q * g.d_head])  # the per-head interleave really moves rows
+    assert torch.equal(w_qkvg[:o_k].view(2, g.h_q, g.d_head, g.d_model).transpose(0, 1).reshape(-1, g.d_model), merged[: 2 * g.h_q * g.d_head])
+    # The norm weights: (1 + w) formed in fp32, rounded once into the activation dtype.
+    assert torch.equal(w_q_norm, (1.0 + hf.q_norm.float()).to(torch.bfloat16)) and torch.equal(w_k_norm, (1.0 + hf.k_norm.float()).to(torch.bfloat16))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name, tp", [("32_2", 2), ("32_2", 4), ("32_2", 8), ("24_2", 2), ("24_2", 4)])
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_at_the_rank_slices(name, tp):
+    """Every rank of ``tp``: the twin on the rank's merged weight equals ``qkvg_from_hf`` on the rank's HF slices bitwise, equals the
+    independent permutation, and equals the rank's shard of the TP 1 ``W_qkvg``; the norm weights are the same on every rank."""
+    g = GEOMS[name]
+    hf = _hf_layer(name)
+    w_tp1, w_q_norm_tp1, w_k_norm_tp1 = qkvg_from_hf(hf.q_proj, hf.k_proj, hf.v_proj, hf.q_norm, hf.k_norm, g)
+    for rank in range(tp):
+        q, k, v, g_r, kv_rank = _rank_slices(hf, g, tp, rank)
+        g_r.validate()
+        assert g_r.n_qkvg == RANK_WIDTHS[name, tp] and g_r.n_qkvg % 256 == 0  # the forced 256-wide projection tile holds at every shard
+        merged = _merged(q, k, v)
+        got = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, hf.q_norm, hf.k_norm, g_r)
+        _assert_three_equal(got, qkvg_from_hf(q, k, v, hf.q_norm, hf.k_norm, g_r))
+        w_qkvg = got[0]
+        assert w_qkvg.shape == (g_r.n_qkvg, g.d_model) and w_qkvg.numel() == merged.numel()
+        assert torch.equal(w_qkvg, _permute_rows(merged, g_r))
+        assert torch.equal(w_qkvg, _shard_of_the_tp1_weight(w_tp1, g, g_r, rank, kv_rank))
+        assert torch.equal(got[1], w_q_norm_tp1) and torch.equal(got[2], w_k_norm_tp1)
+
+
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_projects_the_values_the_serving_stack_projects():
+    """fp64, CPU: ``h @ W^T`` through the merged weight, split as the serving layer splits it (``[2 q | kv | kv]``, the Q block viewed per
+    head and chunked into q / gate), equals ``h @ W_qkvg^T`` cut at the block's offsets, band by band."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    g = GEOM_SMALL
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    q, k, v = torch.randn(2 * hq * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm)
+    merged = _merged(q, k, v)
+    w_qkvg, _, _ = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, torch.zeros(d), torch.zeros(d), g, act_dtype=torch.float32)
+    t = 6
+    h = torch.randn(t, dm).double()
+    out_merged = h @ merged.double().t()
+    q_gate, k_out, v_out = torch.split(out_merged, [2 * hq * d, hkv * d, hkv * d], dim=-1)
+    q_out, gate_out = torch.chunk(q_gate.reshape(t, hq, 2 * d), 2, dim=-1)
+    out_block = h @ w_qkvg.double().t()
+    o_q, o_g, o_k, o_v = g.qkvg_offsets
+    tol = dict(rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_block[:, o_q:o_g], q_out.reshape(t, hq * d), **tol)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_block[:, o_g:o_k], gate_out.reshape(t, hq * d), **tol)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_block[:, o_k:o_v], k_out, **tol)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_block[:, o_v:], v_out, **tol)
+
+
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_takes_a_non_contiguous_merged_weight():
+    """A column slice of a wider buffer is a legitimate load-time input (the row cuts and the per-head view only split the row axis)
+    and gives the contiguous result bitwise."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    g = GEOM_SMALL
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    merged = _merged(torch.randn(2 * hq * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm))
+    sliced = torch.cat([merged, merged], dim=1)[:, :dm]
+    assert not sliced.is_contiguous() and torch.equal(sliced, merged)
+    w_n = torch.zeros(d)
+    _assert_three_equal(qkvg_from_vllm(sliced, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32), qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32))
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The norm form, the indexer band, the refusals
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _GeometryWithNormOffset(GatedAttentionBlockGeometry):
+    """The shape of the in-kernel offset form (``norm_weight_offset`` appended LAST); the loaders read it with ``getattr(..., 0.0)``."""
+
+    norm_weight_offset: float = 1.0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offset", [0.0, 1.0])
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_norm_form_is_derived_from_the_geometry(offset):
+    """The norm weights take exactly the form ``qkvg_from_hf`` hands over: ``(1 + w)`` at offset 0.0 (no field, or 0.0), ``w`` as is at
+    1.0 -- in fp32 bitwise, and rounded once into bf16."""
+    g = GEOM_SMALL if offset == 0.0 else _GeometryWithNormOffset(d_model=256, h_q=4, h_kv=2, d_head=64, rope_dim=16)
+    assert getattr(g, "norm_weight_offset", 0.0) == offset
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    merged = _merged(torch.randn(2 * hq * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm))
+    w = torch.randn(d) * 0.05
+    for act_dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
+        _, w_q_norm, w_k_norm = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w, w, g, act_dtype=act_dtype)
+        expected = ((1.0 + w) if offset == 0.0 else w).to(act_dtype)
+        assert torch.equal(w_q_norm, expected) and torch.equal(w_k_norm, expected)
+        _, hf_q, hf_k = qkvg_from_hf(
+            merged[: 2 * hq * d], merged[2 * hq * d : 2 * hq * d + hkv * d], merged[2 * hq * d + hkv * d :], w, w, g, act_dtype=act_dtype
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(w_q_norm, hf_q) and torch.equal(w_k_norm, hf_k)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="norm_weight_offset"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w, w, _GeometryWithNormOffset(d_model=256, h_q=4, h_kv=2, d_head=64, rope_dim=16, norm_weight_offset=0.5))
+
+
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_carries_the_indexer_band_in_both_forms():
+    """Under ``index_band`` the indexer projection arrives as ``index_qk_proj_weight`` (the HF loader's arm) or appended to the merged
+    weight's rows (a stack that packs the indexer into the QKV GEMM); the two are bitwise, both are bitwise ``qkvg_from_hf``; giving
+    both, neither, or the appended rows on a geometry without the band is refused with a message naming the fix."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    g = GEOM_SMALL_BAND
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    q, k, v = torch.randn(2 * hq * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm), torch.randn(hkv * d, dm)
+    w_i = torch.randn(g.qsa.index_band_cols, dm)
+    w_n = torch.randn(d) * 0.01
+    merged = _merged(q, k, v)
+    packed = torch.cat([merged, w_i], dim=0)
+    assert w_i.shape[0] == 192 and packed.shape[0] == g.n_qkvg
+    want = qkvg_from_hf(q, k, v, w_n, w_n, g, index_qk_proj_weight=w_i, act_dtype=torch.float32)
+    separate = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32, index_qk_proj_weight=w_i)
+    appended = qkvg_from_vllm(packed, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32)
+    _assert_three_equal(separate, want)
+    _assert_three_equal(appended, want)
+    assert separate[0].shape == (g.n_qkvg, dm) and torch.equal(separate[0][g.qkvg_offsets[ProjBlock.INDEX] :], w_i)
+    assert torch.equal(separate[0], build_fused_qkvg_weight(q, k, v, g, q_gate_layout="per_head", index_qk_proj_weight=w_i))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="given twice"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(packed, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32, index_qk_proj_weight=w_i)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="index_qk_proj_weight is required"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"must be \[192, 256\]"):  # the assembler's band checks propagate
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32, index_qk_proj_weight=torch.randn(640, dm))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="declares no indexer band"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, GEOM_SMALL, act_dtype=torch.float32, index_qk_proj_weight=w_i)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=rf"must have {merged.shape[0]} rows .*; got {packed.shape[0]}"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(packed, w_n, w_n, GEOM_SMALL, act_dtype=torch.float32)  # no band declared: the appended rows are a shape error
+    # The row-count message under a band geometry names BOTH admissible forms.
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=rf"must have {merged.shape[0]} rows .*or {packed.shape[0]} with the indexer band's 192 rows appended"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged[:-1], w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.float32)
+
+
+def test_qkvg_from_vllm_rejects():
+    g = GEOM_SMALL
+    d, hq, hkv, dm = g.d_head, g.h_q, g.h_kv, g.d_model
+    merged = torch.zeros(2 * hq * d + 2 * hkv * d, dm)
+    w_n = torch.zeros(d)
+    with pytest.raises(
+        ValueError,
+        match=rf"must have {merged.shape[0]} rows = \[{2 * hq * d} q_proj rows \(per-head \[q_h \| gate_h\]\) \| {hkv * d} k_proj \| {hkv * d} v_proj\]",
+    ):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged[:-d], w_n, w_n, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=rf"must have {dm} columns"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(torch.zeros(merged.shape[0], dm + 1), w_n, w_n, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="2-D"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged.flatten(), w_n, w_n, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="2-D"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged.unsqueeze(0), w_n, w_n, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="2-D"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm([merged], w_n, w_n, g)
+    # The HF loader's own refusals propagate unchanged.
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"q_norm_weight must be \[d_head=64\]"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, torch.zeros(d + 1), w_n, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="k_norm_weight is required"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, None, g)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="act_dtype"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, w_n, g, act_dtype=torch.int32)
+    # qk_norm=False: no norm weights in, None out; a tensor in a norm slot is refused.
+    g_nonorm = GatedAttentionBlockGeometry(d_model=256, h_q=4, h_kv=2, d_head=64, rope_dim=16, qk_norm=False)
+    w_qkvg, wq, wk = qkvg_from_vllm(merged, None, None, g_nonorm)
+    assert wq is None and wk is None and w_qkvg.shape == (g_nonorm.n_qkvg, dm) and w_qkvg.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="qk_norm=False"):
+        qkvg_from_vllm(merged, w_n, None, g_nonorm)

+def _former_route(geom, s_q, policy):
+    """The route BEFORE the table-driven rule (the (16, 32) table, i.e. ``decode_q_tile_max=32``): the packed decode tile in up to two
+    token units where the adapter's rule packs the group, else the tile UNPACKED up to 32 tokens, else not served -- re-derived from
+    the config's route functions, the way the former ``decode_route`` read them (``token_units`` is that rule verbatim; ``single_unit``
+    differs only where the prefill tile packs the group past the table)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.config_sm100 import decode_d256_q_units
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.config_sm107 import decode_d256_q_tile
+
+    g = geom.h_q // geom.h_kv
+    n_q = decode_d256_q_tile(s_q, g, paged=True, masked=True, max_q_tile=32) if g > 1 else 0
+    if n_q:
+        units = decode_d256_q_units(s_q, g, n_q)
+        return (_T, n_q, units, True, units)
+    n_q = decode_d256_q_tile(s_q, 1, paged=True, masked=True, max_q_tile=32)
+    return (_T, n_q, 1, False, g) if n_q else (None, 0, 0, False, 0)

+def test_the_prefill_routes_q_lengths_are_a_workspace_slot_not_plan_owned_memory():
+    """The paged THD leg's per-sequence Q lengths on the prefill route (the constant ``S_q`` of every sequence) are a ``[B]`` int32 slot
+    of the caller's workspace (Rule 8 recipes R2 + R4), reserved by the carve at the very END and only on that route: the layout with
+    ``decode_q_lens=0`` is byte-identical to before, a block on the decode tile reserves none, a block on the prefill tile reserves it
+    at declaration (before ``compile()``); the block holds no plan-owned device tensor for them and no first-execute flag -- the fill
+    rides every execute."""
+    import dataclasses
+
+    from cudnn.gated_attention_block.api import _WS_ALIGN, _align_up, _plan_workspace
+
+    geom, _ = _geom(16)
+    base = _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True)
+    assert base == _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True, decode_q_lens=0) and base.decode_q_lens == -1
+    lay = _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True, decode_q_lens=4)
+    assert lay.decode_q_lens == base.total_bytes and lay.decode_q_lens % _WS_ALIGN == 0, "the slot is appended, aligned"
+    assert lay.total_bytes == lay.engine_scratch == base.total_bytes + _align_up(4 * 4)
+    assert dataclasses.replace(lay, decode_q_lens=-1, total_bytes=base.total_bytes, engine_scratch=base.engine_scratch) == base
+    on, _ = _make_block(16, 32, 8)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 8 with 32 sequences (64 CTAs: the fill): the prefill tile
+    off, _ = _make_block(16, 32, 2)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 2: the decode tile
+    below, _ = _make_block(16, 4, 8)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 8 below the fill: two units of the decode tile, no slot
+    assert on.decode_route.prefill_tile and off.decode_route.decode_tile and below.decode_route.decode_tile
+    lay_on, lay_off = on._layout(), off._layout()
+    assert lay_on.decode_q_lens == lay_on.total_bytes - _align_up(32 * 4) >= 0 and lay_off.decode_q_lens == -1 and below._layout().decode_q_lens == -1
+    for blk in (on, off):
+        assert not any(k.startswith("_decode_q_lens") for k in vars(blk)), "no plan-owned Q-length tensor, no write-once flag"

+def _readback(case):
+    """What the adapter COMPILED for stage (4): the template, the body file, the packing / THD / paged / gate flags of its config."""
+    impl = case.blk._sdpa._impl
+    mod = impl._k_mod
+    cfg = getattr(mod, "CFG", None)
+    return dict(
+        template=impl.kernel_template,
+        file=mod.__file__,
+        heads_per_tile=getattr(mod, "HEADS_PER_TILE", None),
+        pack_gqa=int(getattr(cfg, "PACK_GQA", 0)),
+        thd=int(getattr(cfg, "THD_VARLEN", 0)),
+        paged=int(getattr(cfg, "PAGED_KV", 0)),
+        epilogue_gate=int(getattr(cfg, "EPILOGUE_GATE", 0)) if hasattr(cfg, "EPILOGUE_GATE") else getattr(getattr(mod, "PARAMS", None), "epilogue_gate", None),
+        n_q=getattr(cfg, "N_Q", None),
+        adapter_pack=impl.pack_gqa,
+        adapter_split=impl.split_kv,
+    )

+def _pin_route(case):
+    """The compiled kernel against the declared route: the prefill tile = the shared SM100 d256 paged THD body with the WHOLE group packed
+    and the gate in its epilogue; the decode tile = the Rubin swap-AB tile at the route's width, the gate in the combine."""
+    r, rb = case.blk.decode_route, _readback(case)
+    assert rb["template"] == r.tile, (r, rb)
+    if r.prefill_tile:
+        assert rb["file"].endswith("sm100/prefill_d256_f16.py") and rb["heads_per_tile"] == r.group and rb["adapter_pack"] is True, rb
+        assert (rb["pack_gqa"], rb["thd"], rb["paged"], rb["adapter_split"]) == (1, 1, 1, 1), rb
+        assert bool(rb["epilogue_gate"]) is case.blk.fuse_gate and case.blk.gate_fused is case.blk.fuse_gate and case.blk.decode_split_kv == 1, rb
+    else:
+        assert rb["file"].endswith("sm107/decode_d256_f16.py") and rb["n_q"] == r.n_q and rb["heads_per_tile"] == (r.group if r.pack_gqa else 1), rb
+        assert (rb["adapter_pack"] is True) == r.pack_gqa and rb["adapter_split"] == case.blk.decode_split_kv, rb
+    k0, v0 = case.block0_bits
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(case.k_cache[0]), k0) and torch.equal(_bits(case.v_cache[0]), v0), "block 0 (the NULL block) must never be written"

+def test_capture_of_the_first_execute_at_s_q_eight_replays_bitwise_and_takes_new_lengths_tables_slots_and_inputs():
+    """The serving stack's defaults at the MTP-7 verify step (32 / 2, ``S_q = 8``, the prefill route): the FIRST execute of a fresh
+    declaration captured on a NEW stream with no eager warm-up under ``set_sync_debug_mode("error")``; the capture launches nothing,
+    the replay is BITWISE a fresh eager run; a padded batch replays correctly; new ``kv_lens`` / ``block_table`` / ``slot_mapping`` /
+    ``h`` through the captured tensors replay bitwise the eager run over them."""
+    lens = (300, 0, 1000, 77) * 8  # 32 sequences: the prefill route's fill
+    case = _Case(16, 8, lens, seed=41)  # fresh: never executed
+    assert case.blk.decode_route.prefill_tile and case.blk.decode_route.batch == 32
+    case.blk.check_support()
+    case.blk.compile()
+    case.ws = torch.empty(case.blk.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+    case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+    k_before = _written(case.k_cache)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):

+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")

+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.isnan(case.out).all() and _written(case.k_cache) == k_before, "the capture launched work"
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        replayed = case.out.clone()
+        case.check_against_oracle(replayed, what="replay")
+        case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        case.execute()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(case.out, replayed), "the replay of the captured first execute differs from the eager run"
+        sib = _Case(16, 8, (301, 0, 1000, 77) * 8, seed=43, table_row_stride=case.block_table.shape[1])
+        case.k_cache.copy_(sib.k_cache)
+        case.v_cache.copy_(sib.v_cache)
+        case.block_table.copy_(sib.block_table)
+        case.kv_lens_t.copy_(sib.kv_lens_t)

+def _standalone_tile(case, *, pdl):
+    """The block's stage (4) as a standalone adapter on the block's OWN views (the decode module's ``_adapter_like``), with the switch."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl import SdpaFwdDslSm100
+
+    blk, g = case.blk, case.geom
+    q, gate_v, o, _ = case.slab_views()
+    o_buf = torch.empty_like(o)
+    bts = tuple(int(x) for x in blk._descs["block_table"].stride)
+    api = SdpaFwdDslSm100(
+        sample_q=q.transpose(1, 2),
+        sample_k=case.k_cache,
+        sample_v=case.v_cache,
+        sample_o=o_buf.transpose(1, 2),
+        sample_lse=None,
+        is_causal=g.is_causal,
+        causal_bottom_right=g.causal_bottom_right,
+        scale_softmax=g.scale,
+        seq_kv_lens_present=True,
+        sched_policy=blk._sdpa._impl.sched_policy,
+        split_kv=blk.decode_split_kv,
+        pack_gqa=True if blk.decode_route.pack_gqa else None,
+        paged_page_size=case.page,
+        paged_max_seq_len_kv=case.max_kv_len,
+        paged_table_stride=bts,
+        paged_table_v_stride=bts,
+        sample_gate=gate_v.transpose(1, 2),
+        use_pdl=pdl,
+    )
+    api.check_support()
+    api.compile()
+    assert api.kernel_template == DECODE_TILE and api.use_pdl is pdl
+    ws = torch.empty(max(api.scratch_workspace_bytes(), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+
+    def run():
+        api.execute(
+            q.transpose(1, 2),
+            case.k_cache,
+            case.v_cache,
+            o_buf.transpose(1, 2),
+            seq_kv_lens=case.kv_lens_t,
+            block_table=case.block_table,
+            workspace=ws,
+            gate=gate_v.transpose(1, 2),
+        )
+        return o_buf
+
+    return api, run, o_buf

+_SPIN_US = (300.0, 3000.0)  # the primary's late write: well past any launch latency, so a tile that does not wait reads the NaN
+

+def _race_the_tile(case, run, o_buf, ref):
+    """Ahead of each tile launch: NaN over the operand, then the primary that releases its dependent at once and restores the
+    operand late.  Returns, per (operand, spin), whether the tile's output equals ``ref``."""
+    verdicts = {}
+    slab = _slab(case)
+    slab_saved = slab.clone()
+    k_saved = case.k_cache.clone()
+    for spin in _SPIN_US:
+        slab.fill_(float("nan"))
+        delayed_write(slab_saved, slab, spin_us=spin)
+        run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        verdicts[("slab", spin)] = torch.equal(o_buf, ref)
+        slab.copy_(slab_saved)
+        case.k_cache.fill_(float("nan"))
+        delayed_write(k_saved, case.k_cache, spin_us=spin)
+        run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        verdicts[("k_pool", spin)] = torch.equal(o_buf, ref)
+        case.k_cache.copy_(k_saved)
+    return verdicts

+"""CPU subprocess tests for the standalone benchmark summary command."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+SCRIPT = Path(__file__).with_name("summarize_gdn2_steep_decay.py")
+LABELS = ("base-A1", "patch-B1", "patch-B2", "base-A2")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def runs():
+    """Create complete ABBA records with independently known timing ratios."""
+    records = {}
+    for label in LABELS:
+        median = 2.0 if label.startswith("base") else 1.0
+        records[label] = {
+            "label": label,
+            "script_sha256": "script",
+            "reference_sha256": "reference",
+            "helper_sha256": label.split("-")[0],
+            **dict.fromkeys(("torch", "cuda", "dsl", "cudnn_backend", "gpu", "capability", "seed"), "same"),
+            "results": [
+                {
+                    "tokens": tokens,
+                    "steep_channels": channels,
+                    "correct_within_one_percent": True,
+                    "errors_fp64": {name: {"relative_frobenius": 0.005, "max_abs": 0.001} for name in ("output", "q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w")},
+                    "eager": {"median_ms": median},
+                    "gpu_busy": {"median_ms": median},
+                    "scheduler_records": [{"plan": "CompiledGdn2Bwd", "schedulers": {"scheduler_bwd": [0, 2 if channels else 0]}}],
+                }
+                for tokens in (16, 256)
+                for channels in (0, 1, 64)
+            ],
+        }
+    return records
+
+
+def summarize(tmp_path, runs, optimized=False):
+    """Execute the real CLI against four input files."""
+    for label, record in runs.items():
+        (tmp_path / f"{label}.json").write_text(json.dumps(record))
+    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, *(["-O"] if optimized else []), str(SCRIPT), str(tmp_path)], capture_output=True, text=True)
+
+
+def test_complete_summary(tmp_path, runs):
+    """Preserve valid measurements and write JSON that strict readers accept."""
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    summary = json.loads((tmp_path / "summary.json").read_text(), parse_constant=lambda value: pytest.fail(f"Nonstandard JSON: {value}"))
+    assert len(summary["results"]) == 6
+    assert summary["reference_hash"] == "reference"
+    for row in summary["results"]:
+        for mode in ("eager", "gpu_busy"):
+            assert row[mode]["base_ms"] == 2.0
+            assert row[mode]["patch_ms"] == 1.0
+            assert row[mode]["speedup"] == 2.0
+            assert row[mode]["reduction_percent"] == 50.0
+        assert row["max_fp64_relative_error"] == 0.005
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["eager", "gpu_busy"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [float("nan"), float("inf"), -float("inf"), 0.0, -1.0])
+def test_invalid_timing_does_not_replace_summary(tmp_path, runs, mode, value):
+    """Reject invalid medians before overwriting a previous summary."""
+    sentinel = tmp_path / "summary.json"
+    sentinel.write_text("previous summary\n")
+    runs["patch-B1"]["results"][0][mode]["median_ms"] = value
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "finite and positive" in result.stderr
+    assert sentinel.read_text() == "previous summary\n"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("base,patch", [(1e308, 1e-308), (1e-308, 1e308)])
+def test_derived_overflow_is_rejected(tmp_path, runs, base, patch):
+    """Reject ratios that overflow despite finite positive inputs."""
+    for label, run in runs.items():
+        run["results"][0]["gpu_busy"]["median_ms"] = base if label.startswith("base") else patch
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "ValueError: Non-finite derived gpu_busy measurement" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [float("nan"), float("inf"), -0.001, 0.02])
+def test_invalid_error_cannot_hide_behind_pass_flag(tmp_path, runs, value):
+    """Check each relative error independently of the saved pass flag."""
+    runs["patch-B2"]["results"][0]["errors_fp64"]["q"]["relative_frobenius"] = value
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "ValueError: Invalid FP64 relative error for q" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("optimized", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fault", ["environment", "helper", "reference", "case", "pass_flag", "scheduler", "missing_gradient"])
+def test_validation_survives_optimized_python(tmp_path, runs, optimized, fault):
+    """Reject incomplete or mismatched records in both Python execution modes."""
+    messages = {
+        "environment": "Environment differs: torch",
+        "helper": "Helper hashes differ",
+        "reference": "FP64 reference hashes differ",
+        "case": "Incomplete or reordered cases",
+        "pass_flag": "FP64 check failed",
+        "scheduler": "Unexpected backward scheduler flags",
+        "missing_gradient": "Incomplete FP64 checks",
+    }
+    run = runs["patch-B2"]
+    if fault == "environment":
+        run["torch"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "helper":
+        run["helper_sha256"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "reference":
+        run["reference_sha256"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "case":
+        run["results"].pop()
+    elif fault == "pass_flag":
+        run["results"][0]["correct_within_one_percent"] = False
+    elif fault == "scheduler":
+        run["results"][0]["scheduler_records"] = []
+    else:
+        del run["results"][0]["errors_fp64"]["w"]
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs, optimized)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert f"ValueError: {messages[fault]}" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()

+def token_major_views(case, pad=24, return_buffers=False):
+    """The case's expanded k / v / beta as the per-token column slices of a joint projection buffer: ``[T, pad | n*HV*V |
+    n*HK*K | H*K | pad]`` viewed ``[T, n, HV, V]`` / ``[T, n, HK, K]`` with the joint token stride, beta from a ``[T, pad |
+    n*HO | pad]`` buffer viewed ``[T, n, HO]``.  Same bytes as the expanded leaves, a different row convention.
+    ``return_buffers`` adds the two joint buffers and the column slices of v, k and beta (to differentiate through the
+    buffers: a clone of a strided view is contiguous, so a leaf must be the buffer itself)."""
+    tokens, n = case.T * case.B, case.n
+    k, v, beta = to_thd(case.k), to_thd(case.v), to_thd(case.gates["beta"])
+    widths = (n * case.HV * case.V, n * case.HK * case.K, case.H * case.K)
+    joint = torch.randn(tokens, 2 * pad + sum(widths), device="cuda").to(case.dtype)
+    v_cols = slice(pad, pad + widths[0])
+    k_cols = slice(pad + widths[0], pad + widths[0] + widths[1])
+    v_tm = joint[:, v_cols].view(tokens, n, case.HV, case.V)
+    k_tm = joint[:, k_cols].view(tokens, n, case.HK, case.K)
+    v_tm.copy_(v.view(tokens, n, case.HV, case.V))
+    k_tm.copy_(k.view(tokens, n, case.HK, case.K))

+        o_d, fs_d, dq_d, dg_d, (dk_d, dv_d, dbeta_d) = run(
+            k_l.view(tokens, n, case.HK, case.K), v_l.view(tokens, n, case.HV, case.V), beta_l.view(tokens, n, case.HO), [k_l, v_l, beta_l]

+        check("dense views", o_d, fs_d, dq_d, dg_d, dk_d, dv_d, dbeta_d)
+        # mixed: strided k / v with the expanded beta (Megatron keeps beta contiguous)
+        joint_l, beta_l = leaf(joint), leaf(beta_e)

+        v_t = joint_l[:, v_cols].view(tokens, n, case.HV, case.V)

+"""Host-side concurrency invariants for cached linear-attention graphs."""
+
+import contextlib
+import threading
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from cudnn.linear_attention.ops import common
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+
+class _Graph:
+    """Minimal built graph exposing only the workspace-size contract."""
+
+    _is_built = True
+
+    def get_workspace_size(self):
+        """Return a stable fake workspace requirement."""
+        return 256
+
+
+class _Workspace:
+    """Small tensor stand-in used to observe host-side allocations."""
+
+    def __init__(self, size, device):
+        """Record the allocation size and device."""
+        self._size = size
+        self.device = device
+
+    def numel(self):
+        """Return the fake allocation size."""
+        return self._size
+
+
+def test_graph_workspace_is_caller_owned_per_execution(monkeypatch):
+    """Each invocation receives fresh scratch without retaining it on the graph."""
+    device = SimpleNamespace(index=0)
+    current = [SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=11)]
+    allocations = []
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch.cuda, "current_stream", lambda unused_device: current[0])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch.cuda, "device", lambda unused_device: contextlib.nullcontext())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch.cuda, "stream", lambda unused_stream: contextlib.nullcontext())
+
+    def allocate(size, *, dtype, device):
+        """Record each workspace allocation."""
+        workspace = _Workspace(size, device)
+        allocations.append(workspace)
+        return workspace
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch, "empty", allocate)
+
+    graph = _Graph()
+    first = common.graph_workspace(graph, device)
+    again = common.graph_workspace(graph, device)
+    current[0] = SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=22)
+    second = common.graph_workspace(graph, device)
+
+    assert first is not again
+    assert first is not second
+    assert len(allocations) == 3
+    assert not hasattr(graph, "_la_ops_workspaces")
+
+
+def test_cudnn_handles_are_thread_local_and_follow_each_threads_stream(monkeypatch):
+    """Concurrent host threads use distinct handles bound to their own streams."""
+    device = SimpleNamespace(index=0)
+    local = threading.local()
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
+    creation_lock = threading.Lock()
+    created = []
+    bindings = []
+    results = []
+
+    if hasattr(common, "cudnn_handles"):
+        common.cudnn_handles.clear()
+    if hasattr(common, "_tls"):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(common, "_tls", threading.local())
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch.cuda, "current_stream", lambda unused_device: local.stream)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.torch.cuda, "device", lambda unused_device: contextlib.nullcontext())
+
+    def create_handle():
+        """Return a distinct fake handle for each creation."""
+        with creation_lock:
+            handle = len(created) + 1
+            created.append(handle)
+            return handle
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.cudnn, "create_handle", create_handle)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(common.cudnn, "set_stream", lambda *, handle, stream: bindings.append((handle, stream)))
+

+        """Fetch the same thread-local handle twice on one fake stream."""
+        local.stream = SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=stream)
+        barrier.wait()
+        first = common.get_handle(device)
+        second = common.get_handle(device)
+        results.append((stream, first, second))
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(stream,)) for stream in (101, 202)]
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.start()
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.join()
+
+    assert len(results) == 2
+    assert all(first == second for _, first, second in results)
+    assert len({first for _, first, _ in results}) == 2

+
+
+def test_first_graph_execution_is_serialized(monkeypatch):
+    """Only the graph's first lazy execution is protected by its build lock."""
+    first_entered = threading.Event()
+    second_waiting = threading.Event()
+    release_first = threading.Event()
+    second_entered = threading.Event()
+    failures = []
+
+    class TrackingLock:
+        """Lock that exposes when a second thread starts waiting."""
+
+        def __init__(self):
+            """Initialize the underlying lock and attempt counter."""
+            self.lock = threading.Lock()
+            self.guard = threading.Lock()
+            self.attempts = 0
+
+        def __enter__(self):
+            """Record the acquisition attempt before blocking."""
+            with self.guard:
+                self.attempts += 1
+                if self.attempts == 2:
+                    second_waiting.set()
+            self.lock.acquire()
+
+        def __exit__(self, *unused):
+            """Release the underlying lock."""
+            self.lock.release()
+
+    class Graph:
+        """Fake graph whose first execution blocks until the test releases it."""
+
+        def __init__(self):
+            """Initialize execution accounting and the observable lock."""
+            self.calls = 0
+            self._la_ops_execution_lock = TrackingLock()
+
+        def execute(self, unused_variant_pack, *, workspace, handle):
+            """Block the first call and record entry into the second."""
+            assert workspace is sentinel_workspace
+            assert handle is sentinel_handle
+            self.calls += 1
+            if self.calls == 1:
+                first_entered.set()
+                assert release_first.wait(timeout=5)
+            else:
+                second_entered.set()
+
+    sentinel_workspace = object()
+    sentinel_handle = object()
+
+    graph = Graph()
+
+    def worker():
+        """Execute the graph and preserve failures from this host thread."""
+        try:
+            common.execute_graph(graph, {}, sentinel_workspace, sentinel_handle)
+        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- preserve thread failures
+            failures.append(exc)
+
+    first = threading.Thread(target=worker)
+    second = threading.Thread(target=worker)
+    first.start()
+    assert first_entered.wait(timeout=5)
+    second.start()
+    try:
+        assert second_waiting.wait(timeout=5)
+        assert not second_entered.is_set(), "the second execute overlapped the first graph initialization"
+    finally:
+        release_first.set()
+    first.join(timeout=5)
+    second.join(timeout=5)
+
+    assert not first.is_alive() and not second.is_alive()
+    assert not failures
+    assert graph.calls == 2
+    assert graph._la_ops_execution_ready

+    torch.float32: dict(fwd=3e-4, bwd=2e-4),
+    torch.float16: dict(fwd=6e-2, bwd=4e-2),
+    torch.bfloat16: dict(fwd=8e-2, bwd=7e-2),
+}
+DTYPES = [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16]
+
+
+def _check(name, got, ref, dtype, kind):
+    if got is None and ref is None:
+        return True
+    got = got.float()
+    ref = ref.float()
+    amax = (got - ref).abs().max().item()
+    scale = max(1.0, ref.abs().max().item())
+    ok = amax <= TOL[dtype][kind] * scale
+    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name:<22} {str(dtype):>16} maxabs={amax:.3e}")
+    return ok
+
+
+def _ref_grads(fn, x, g, b, dy):
+    xr = x.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    gr = g.float().detach().requires_grad_(True) if g is not None else None
+    br = b.float().detach().requires_grad_(True) if b is not None else None
+    y = fn(xr, gr, br)
+    ins = [t for t in (xr, gr, br) if t is not None]
+    grads = torch.autograd.grad(y, ins, grad_outputs=dy.float())
+    it = iter(grads)
+    dx = next(it)
+    dg = next(it) if gr is not None else None
+    db = next(it) if br is not None else None
+    return y.detach(), dx, dg, db
+
+
+def _check_variant(variant, xshape, ref_fn, *, glen, has_beta=True, fwd=None, bwd=None):
+    fwd = fwd or {}
+    bwd = bwd or {}
+    all_ok = True
+    print(f"\n=== {variant.value} shape={xshape} glen={glen} has_beta={has_beta} ===")
+    for dtype in DTYPES:
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        x = torch.randn(*xshape, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+        g = torch.randn(glen, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+        b = torch.randn(glen, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) if has_beta else None
+
+        y, mean, rstd = norm_fprop(variant, x, g, b, **fwd)
+        dy = torch.randn_like(y)
+        dx, dgamma, dbeta = norm_bprop(variant, dy, x, g, mean, rstd, has_beta=has_beta, **bwd)
+
+        y_ref, dx_ref, dg_ref, db_ref = _ref_grads(ref_fn, x, g, b, dy)
+        all_ok &= _check("fwd y", y, y_ref, dtype, "fwd")
+        all_ok &= _check("bwd dx", dx, dx_ref, dtype, "bwd")
+        all_ok &= _check("bwd dgamma", dgamma, dg_ref, dtype, "bwd")
+        if has_beta:
+            all_ok &= _check("bwd dbeta", dbeta, db_ref, dtype, "bwd")
+    return all_ok

+    D = 256

+    ok &= _check_variant(

+        lambda x, g, b: F.layer_norm(x, (D,), g, b, 1e-5),

+        bwd=dict(normalized_shape=[D]),

+        fwd=dict(num_groups=4, eps=1e-5),

+"""Long-row LayerNorm / RMSNorm: the CGA split, fprop + bprop.
+
+Rows past ~16K elements leave the one-CTA-per-row design and are split across a
+cluster, each CTA reducing its own slice and sharing partials through distributed
+shared memory. That path has failure modes the ordinary shapes cannot reach, so this
+file covers the (R, D) corners specifically:
+
+* **D beyond what a single CTA can stage.** D=65536 bf16 needs 262208 bytes against a
+  232448 limit; before the shared-memory guard this did not fail a check, it failed
+  the *launch*.
+* **Fewer rows than clusters**, and R=1. The grid is ``nclusters * CGA`` CTAs
+  grid-striding over rows, so a cluster may get one row or none. Every CTA in a
+  cluster must still reach the same cluster barriers the same number of times --
+  divergence there hangs rather than fails.
+* **R not a multiple of anything** (31), since the row loop is a grid stride.
+* **Both sides of the routing threshold.** The forward takes the split from D=16384;
+  the backward only from D=32768, or from 16384 when there are too few rows to fill
+  the machine otherwise. Below that the existing pipelined backward is simply better
+  -- routing D=16384 R=2048 to the split measured 0.23 against 0.60 -- so one case
+  asserts the split is NOT taken, which is the half of a threshold that silently
+  rots.
+
+Each case checks numerics against PyTorch autograd for dx, dgamma and dbeta, and
+asserts which kernel actually ran on each side.
+
+Run standalone (no built cuDNN extension required):
+
+    python test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_large_rows.py
+    pytest test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_large_rows.py -m L1

+    a stub installed during collection replaces the real module for every other test
+    in the session.

+    # from a method, so a placeholder is enough to reach the DSL version gate.

+geometry has real constraints -- C must divide into vectors and channel tiles --
+so plenty of ordinary channel counts have no NHWC tile at all, and those fall
+through to the contiguous kernels.

+(N, C, H, W) -> (N, C, S) view it takes EXISTS in channels-last memory: merging H
+and W is legal there, so ``reshape`` returns a strided view rather than copying,
+and the contiguous kernel then addresses it as if it were packed. fp32 [4,24,8,8]
+came back as 6144 untouched NaNs. GroupNorm and InstanceNorm took the same route
+but survived it, because their rowwise view is not expressible and reshape was
+forced to copy -- the same bug, hidden by an accident of layout.
+
+So these cases check the whole contract on an output buffer poisoned with NaN:
+every element written, and the values right. A C that the NHWC tile *does*
+accept is interleaved as a control, since a fix that simply stopped using the
+native kernels would also pass a correctness-only test.

+BatchNorm switches to a shared-memory pixel cache (KS > 0), and that loop's
+index collided with the shifted-statistics list added for the variance fix --
+so the whole route failed to compile while every tested shape stayed below the
+threshold. It is a cheap case to keep.

+lands on a different channel than the partials were accumulated for.

+sequence does not satisfy both -- rounding up to gps and then up to WPB breaks
+the gps divisibility again. gps=5 on 68 SMs produced 2184 warps (2184 % 5 == 4).
+dgamma was off by 179 and dx by 8.1, silently.
+

+
+* It needs enough rows to exceed the persistent cap. Below that the grid is one
+  wave, every warp sees exactly one row, and the mapping cannot drift -- the same
+  channel count passes at N=600 and fails at N=1000.
+* The cap is ``4 * SM_count * WPB``, so whether a given shape trips it depends on
+  the GPU. The reported failure was on 68 SMs; on 148 the same shape is fine.
+  So the SM count is simulated rather than taken from the device, and the sweep
+  covers counts this machine does not have.

+"""Numerical stability of the centered reductions: offset data with a small spread.
+
+Every centered norm here once computed its variance as ``E[x^2] - E[x]^2``. Both
+terms scale as ``|x|^2`` while their difference is the variance, so for data
+carrying a large common offset the subtraction cancels every significant bit.
+fp32 LayerNorm over values alternating 8191/8193 -- ordinary, finite, supported
+input -- returned +/-316.2 where the answer is +/-0.999995, and GroupNorm,
+InstanceNorm and training BatchNorm all failed the same way. The reductions are
+small (256 elements, 32, 49), so this is not a long-row problem that a
+long-row-only fix would cover.
+
+Two separate defects produced it, and this file pins both:
+
+1. **The reduction.** Fixed by subtracting a shift K drawn from the data before
+   squaring (``shifted_stats`` in ``_common_sm100``), so the cancellation is
+   proportional to the spread rather than the magnitude.
+2. **The affine.** Several kernels applied ``y = x*scale + shift`` with
+   ``shift = -mean*scale``. That recreates the same cancellation in the OUTPUT
+   even once the statistics are exact: both terms are O(|x|*rstd) and their sum
+   is O(1). Centering first (``(x - mean) * scale``) is exact by Sterbenz.
+   Statistics alone would not have caught this -- InstanceNorm (16,32,1,1) had a
+   correct rstd and a y error of 2.2e-02 -- so the output is asserted too.
+
+What the bounds mean. ``rstd`` is checked on a relative tolerance: it carries no
+offset and should be accurate to a few fp32 roundings. ``mean`` is checked
+against *half an ulp at its own magnitude*, i.e. it must be the correctly-rounded
+fp32 value -- the best an fp32 output can be. ``y`` is then allowed the error
+that a correctly-rounded fp32 mean necessarily induces, ``0.5*ulp(mean)*rstd``,
+plus a few roundings. These are tight: the pre-fix numbers exceed them by five
+orders of magnitude.
+
+Run standalone (no built cuDNN extension required):
+
+    python test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_stability.py
+    pytest test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_stability.py -m L1
+"""
+
+import math
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+
+def _install_repo_cudnn_stub():
+    """Point ``cudnn`` at the repo subtree, for STANDALONE runs only.
+
+    Never at import time under pytest: ``sys.modules["cudnn"]`` is process-global,
+    so a stub installed during collection replaces the real module for every other
+    test in the session.
+    """
+    if "cudnn" in sys.modules:
+        return
+    repo_cudnn = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "python" / "cudnn"
+    if not (repo_cudnn / "norm").is_dir():
+        return
+    stub = types.ModuleType("cudnn")
+    stub.__path__ = [str(repo_cudnn)]
+    stub.__file__ = str(repo_cudnn / "__init__.py")
+    stub.pygraph = type("pygraph", (), {})
+    stub._pybind_module = types.ModuleType("cudnn._pybind_module")
+
+    import enum
+
+    class _DataType(enum.Enum):
+        NOT_SET = 0
+        HALF = 1
+        BFLOAT16 = 2
+        FLOAT = 3
+
+    stub.data_type = _DataType
+    sys.modules["cudnn"] = stub
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    _install_repo_cudnn_stub()
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm kernels require a built cudnn frontend")
+
+from cudnn.norm._lazy import dsl_unavailable
+
+requirement_error = dsl_unavailable("FROST norm tests")
+if requirement_error:
+    pytest.skip(requirement_error, allow_module_level=True)
+
+from cudnn.norm import NormVariant, norm_fprop  # noqa: E402
+
+LN, RMS = NormVariant.LAYER_NORM, NormVariant.RMS_NORM
+GN, IN, BN = NormVariant.GROUP_NORM, NormVariant.INSTANCE_NORM, NormVariant.BATCH_NORM
+EPS = 1e-5
+_F32_EPS = 2.0**-24
+
+
+def _ulp(x):
+    """Spacing of fp32 at magnitude ``x`` (0 below the first normal binade)."""
+    x = abs(float(x))
+    if x == 0.0:
+        return 0.0
+    return 2.0 ** (math.floor(math.log2(x)) - 23)
+
+
+def _data(shape, offset, spread, device="cuda"):
+    """Alternating ``offset -/+ spread`` -- maximal cancellation, exact in fp32."""
+    t = torch.empty(shape, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    f = t.reshape(-1)
+    f[0::2] = offset - spread
+    f[1::2] = offset + spread
+    return t
+
+
+def _reference(variant, x, g, b, num_groups):
+    """fp64 reference plus the per-reduction mean/rstd it implies."""
+    xd = x.double()
+    if variant in (LN, RMS):
+        D = x.shape[-1]
+        flat = xd.reshape(-1, D)
+        if variant is LN:
+            y = F.layer_norm(xd, [D], g.double(), b.double(), EPS)
+            mean = flat.mean(-1)
+        else:
+            y = F.rms_norm(xd, [D], g.double(), eps=EPS)
+            mean = torch.zeros_like(flat[:, 0])
+        var = (flat - flat.mean(-1, keepdim=True)).pow(2).mean(-1) if variant is LN else flat.pow(2).mean(-1)
+    elif variant is BN:
+        y = F.batch_norm(xd, None, None, g.double(), b.double(), True, 0.1, EPS)
+        ch = xd.permute(1, 0, *range(2, xd.dim())).reshape(x.shape[1], -1)
+        mean, var = ch.mean(-1), ch.var(-1, correction=0)
+    else:
+        y = F.group_norm(xd, num_groups, g.double(), b.double(), EPS)
+        grp = xd.reshape(x.shape[0], num_groups, -1)
+        mean, var = grp.mean(-1).reshape(-1), grp.var(-1, correction=0).reshape(-1)
+    return y, mean, torch.rsqrt(var + EPS)
+
+
+def _check_case(variant, shape, *, offset, spread, num_groups=None, channels_last=False, label=""):
+    x = _data(shape, offset, spread)
+    if channels_last and x.dim() == 4:
+        x = x.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
+    width = shape[-1] if variant in (LN, RMS) else shape[1]
+    g = torch.ones(width, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    b = None if variant is RMS else torch.zeros(width, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    kw = {}
+    if variant in (LN, RMS):
+        kw["normalized_shape"] = [shape[-1]]
+    elif variant is BN:
+        kw["training"] = True
+    else:
+        kw["num_groups"] = num_groups
+    y, mean, rstd = norm_fprop(variant, x, g, b, eps=EPS, **kw)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    y_ref, mean_ref, rstd_ref = _reference(variant, x, g, b if b is not None else torch.zeros_like(g), num_groups)
+
+    # The error a correctly-rounded fp32 ``mean`` output forces, per reduction. Using
+    # the ACTUAL rounding rather than a worst-case half-ulp keeps the bounds tight
+    # where the exact mean happens to be representable -- which is precisely the
+    # InstanceNorm HW=1 case the fused affine broke while its statistics stayed
+    # correct. A half-ulp bound there would have been 0.154 and hidden a 2.2e-02 y.
+    mean_round = (mean_ref.float().double() - mean_ref).abs()
+
+    # rstd has no offset and loses at most a few fp32 rounding steps.
+    # The previous reduction exceeded this bound by about five orders of magnitude.
+    rstd_err = (rstd.double().reshape(-1) - rstd_ref.reshape(-1)).abs().max().item()
+    rstd_tol = 64 * _F32_EPS * rstd_ref.abs().max().item()
+    ok = rstd_err <= rstd_tol
+    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {label:36} rstd  err={rstd_err:.3e} tol={rstd_tol:.3e}")
+
+    # mean must be the correctly-rounded fp32 value at its own magnitude.
+    # RMSNorm is uncentered and returns a placeholder here, so it has none.
+    ok2 = True
+    if variant is not RMS:
+        mean_err = (mean.double().reshape(-1) - mean_ref.reshape(-1)).abs().max().item()
+        mean_tol = 4 * mean_round.max().item() + 1024 * _F32_EPS * max(1.0, spread)
+        ok2 = mean_err <= mean_tol
+        print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok2 else 'FAIL'}] {label:36} mean  err={mean_err:.3e} tol={mean_tol:.3e}")
+
+    # y may inherit that mean's rounding, amplified by rstd, and nothing beyond it.
+    y_err = (y.double() - y_ref).abs().max().item()
+    y_tol = 4 * (mean_round * rstd_ref).max().item() + 1024 * _F32_EPS * max(1.0, y_ref.abs().max().item())
+    ok3 = y_err <= y_tol
+    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok3 else 'FAIL'}] {label:36} y     err={y_err:.3e} tol={y_tol:.3e}")
+    return ok and ok2 and ok3
+
+
+# (variant, shape, num_groups, channels_last) -- chosen to reach distinct kernels:
+# the warp LN, the CGA LN, the blocked GN/IN, both NHWC paths and both BN paths.
+def _cases(full):
+    offsets = [8192.0, 1.0e6] if full else [8192.0]
+    spreads = [1.0, 1.0 / 64.0] if full else [1.0]
+    base = [
+        # the reviewer's four reported failures, verbatim
+        (LN, (4, 256), None, False),
+        (GN, (4, 8, 32), 4, False),
+        (IN, (4, 8, 32), 8, False),
+        (BN, (16, 8, 4), None, False),
+        # RMSNorm is uncentered: a control that must stay exact
+        (RMS, (4, 256), None, False),
+    ]
+    if full:
+        base += [
+            (LN, (4, 65536), None, False),  # CGA row split
+            (LN, (64, 37), None, False),  # non-vectorizable fallback
+            (RMS, (4, 65536), None, False),
+            (GN, (4, 32, 8, 8), 4, False),
+            (GN, (4, 32, 8, 8), 4, True),  # NHWC
+            (IN, (4, 32, 8, 8), 32, False),
+            (IN, (4, 32, 8, 8), 32, True),  # NHWC
+            (IN, (16, 32, 1, 1), 32, True),  # HW=1: rstd=1/sqrt(eps), amplifies any y error
+            (BN, (16, 32, 8, 8), None, False),
+            (BN, (16, 32, 8, 8), None, True),  # NHWC
+            (BN, (3, 7, 5, 5), None, False),  # odd S -> scalar fallback kernel
+        ]
+    out = []
+    for off in offsets:
+        for sp in spreads:
+            for variant, shape, ng, cl in base:
+                out.append((variant, shape, ng, cl, off, sp))
+    return out
+
+
+def main(full=True):
+    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA required"
+    ok = True
+    for variant, shape, ng, cl, off, sp in _cases(full):
+        name = str(variant).split(".")[-1]
+        label = f"{name} {tuple(shape)}{' NHWC' if cl else ''} off={off:g} sp={sp:g}"
+        print(f"\n=== {label} ===")
+        ok &= _check_case(variant, shape, offset=off, spread=sp, num_groups=ng, channels_last=cl, label=name)
+    print("\n" + ("ALL PASS" if ok else "SOME FAILED"))
+    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
+
+
+def _entry(full):
+    try:
+        main(full=full)
+    except SystemExit as exc:
+        assert not exc.code, "checks failed -- see captured stdout"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+def test_frost_norm_offset_stability_smoke():
+    """The four reported failures plus the uncentered control."""
+    _entry(full=False)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L1
+def test_frost_norm_offset_stability():
+    """Every centered kernel x offset x spread, outputs and saved statistics."""
+    _entry(full=True)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Coverage for every staging/vectorization path of the row-wise kernels.
+
+``norm_fprop``/``norm_bprop`` auto-pick TMA bulk staging + scalar stores, so this
+test forces each ``Cfg`` (STAGE_NONE / STAGE_CPASYNC / STAGE_BULK, vec on/off) on
+the LayerNorm and GroupNorm kernels directly and checks fprop + bprop vs PyTorch
+autograd. cp.async requires ``M % (bt*V) == 0``; the harness picks a valid ``bt``.
+
+    pytest test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_staging.py
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+import types
+
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm engines require a built cudnn frontend")
+
+from cudnn.norm._lazy import dsl_unavailable
+
+requirement_error = dsl_unavailable("FROST norm tests")
+if requirement_error:
+    pytest.skip(requirement_error, allow_module_level=True)
+
+from cudnn.norm.config_sm100 import (
+    STAGE_BULK,
+    STAGE_CPASYNC,
+    STAGE_NONE,
+    Cfg,
+    NormVariant as NV,
+    TemplateParams,
+    rowwise_spec,
+    vector_width,
+)
+from cudnn.norm.dtypes import DTYPE_BYTES, torch_dtype_to_str
+from cudnn.norm.fprop.kernels import groupnorm_sm100 as gf, layernorm_sm100 as lf
+from cudnn.norm.bprop.kernels import groupnorm_sm100 as gb, layernorm_sm100 as lb
+
+_OK = True
+
+
+def _chk(name, got, ref, tol):
+    global _OK
+    amax = (got.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()
+    scale = max(1.0, ref.float().abs().max().item())
+    ok = amax <= tol * scale
+    _OK &= ok
+    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name:<30} maxabs={amax:.3e}")
+
+
+def _cpasync_bt(M, V):
+    """Largest multiple-of-32 bt (<=256) with bt*V | M, or None."""
+    for bt in (256, 128, 64, 32):
+        if M % (bt * V) == 0:
+            return bt
+    return None
+
+
+def _modes(M, V, eb):
+    out = [
+        ("bulk+scal", Cfg(256, V, STAGE_BULK, False, eb)),
+        ("bulk+vec", Cfg(256, V, STAGE_BULK, True, eb)),
+        ("none+scal", Cfg(256, V, STAGE_NONE, False, eb)),
+        ("none+vec", Cfg(256, V, STAGE_NONE, True, eb)),
+    ]
+    cbt = _cpasync_bt(M, V)
+    if cbt is not None:
+        out.append(("cpasync+vec", Cfg(cbt, V, STAGE_CPASYNC, True, eb)))
+        out.append(("cpasync+scal", Cfg(cbt, V, STAGE_CPASYNC, False, eb)))
+    return out
+
+
+def _ln(dt):
+    D = 512
+    eb = DTYPE_BYTES[torch_dtype_to_str(dt)]
+    V = vector_width(eb)
+    tol = 6e-2 if dt != torch.float32 else 3e-4
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    x = torch.randn(6, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    g = torch.randn(D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    b = torch.randn(D, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    spec = rowwise_spec(NV.LAYER_NORM, x.shape, normalized_shape=[D])
+    p = TemplateParams(variant=NV.LAYER_NORM, io_dtype=torch_dtype_to_str(dt))
+    xr = x.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    gr = g.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    br = b.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    yref = F.layer_norm(xr, (D,), gr, br, 1e-5)
+    dy = torch.randn_like(yref)
+    dxr, dgr, dbr = torch.autograd.grad(yref, [xr, gr, br], grad_outputs=dy)
+    for name, cfg in _modes(spec.M, V, eb):
+        y, mean, rstd = lf.forward(spec, x.reshape(spec.R, spec.M), g, b, eps=1e-5, cfg=cfg, params=p)
+        dx, dgamma, dbeta = lb.backward(spec, dy.to(dt).reshape(spec.R, spec.M), x.reshape(spec.R, spec.M), g, mean, rstd, has_beta=True, cfg=cfg, params=p)
+        _chk(f"LN {name} y", y.reshape(x.shape), yref, tol)
+        _chk(f"LN {name} dx", dx.reshape(x.shape), dxr, tol)
+        _chk(f"LN {name} dgamma", dgamma, dgr, tol)
+
+
+def _gn(dt):
+    N, C, G, HW = 4, 8, 4, 64  # M = (C/G)*HW = 128
+    eb = DTYPE_BYTES[torch_dtype_to_str(dt)]
+    V = vector_width(eb)
+    tol = 8e-2 if dt != torch.float32 else 3e-4
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    x = torch.randn(N, C, HW, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    g = torch.randn(C, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    b = torch.randn(C, device="cuda", dtype=dt)
+    spec = rowwise_spec(NV.GROUP_NORM, x.shape, num_groups=G)
+    p = TemplateParams(variant=NV.GROUP_NORM, io_dtype=torch_dtype_to_str(dt))
+    xr = x.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    gr = g.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    br = b.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    yref = F.group_norm(xr, G, gr, br, 1e-5)
+    dy = torch.randn_like(yref)
+    dxr, dgr, dbr = torch.autograd.grad(yref, [xr, gr, br], grad_outputs=dy)
+    for name, cfg in _modes(spec.M, V, eb):
+        y, mean, rstd = gf.forward(spec, x.reshape(spec.R, spec.M), g, b, eps=1e-5, cfg=cfg, params=p)
+        dx, dgamma, dbeta = gb.backward(spec, dy.to(dt).reshape(spec.R, spec.M), x.reshape(spec.R, spec.M), g, mean, rstd, has_beta=True, cfg=cfg, params=p)
+        _chk(f"GN {name} y", y.reshape(x.shape), yref, tol)
+        _chk(f"GN {name} dx", dx.reshape(x.shape), dxr, tol)
+        _chk(f"GN {name} dgamma", dgamma, dgr, tol)
+
+
+def main():
+    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA required"
+    for dt in (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+        print(f"\n=== dtype={dt} ===")
+        _ln(dt)
+        _gn(dt)
+    print("\n" + ("ALL PASS" if _OK else "SOME FAILED"))
+    sys.exit(0 if _OK else 1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
+
+

+    """pytest entry point; this module also runs standalone via ``__main__``."""
+    try:
+        main()
+    except SystemExit as exc:
+        assert not exc.code, "checks failed -- see captured stdout"

+single fprop / bprop engine, buffer resolution (``resolve_variant_pack``), the
+kernel launch, and the copy-into-output-buffers step — everything except the C++
+``cudnn.pygraph`` lifecycle (which needs a built cuDNN frontend). Complements

+
+import os
+import sys
+import types
+
+
+import cudnn
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm engines require a built cudnn frontend")

+from cudnn.norm.bprop import engines as be

+_DT = cudnn.data_type
+_TDT = {torch.float16: _DT.HALF, torch.bfloat16: _DT.BFLOAT16, torch.float32: _DT.FLOAT}
+
+_OK = True
+
+
+def _expect(c, m):
+    global _OK
+    _OK &= bool(c)
+    print(f"  [{'PASS' if c else 'FAIL'}] {m}")
+
+
+class _T:
+    """Fake IR tensor wrapping a real torch buffer (the variant pack keys on it)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, buf):
+        self.buf = buf
+
+    def get_dim(self):
+        return tuple(self.buf.shape)
+
+    def get_stride(self):
+        return tuple(self.buf.stride())
+
+    def get_data_type(self):
+        return _TDT[self.buf.dtype]
+
+    def get_name(self):
+        return ""
+
+    def get_uid(self):
+        return 0
+
+
+class _Node:
+    def __init__(self, nt, params, inputs, outputs):
+        self.node_type = types.SimpleNamespace(name=nt)
+        self.params = params
+        self.inputs = inputs
+        self.outputs = outputs
+
+
+class _Graph:
+    def __init__(self, node):
+        self.nodes = [node]
+
+
+def _mk(shape, dt):
+    return _T(torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", dtype=dt))
+
+
+def _mkf(n):
+    return _T(torch.empty(n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32))
+
+
+def _tol(dt, base):
+    return base if dt != torch.float32 else base * 5e-3
+
+

+    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA required"
+    fspec = fe.ENGINE_SPECS[0]
+    bspec = be.ENGINE_SPECS[0]
+

+        # --- LayerNorm forward through the fprop engine ---

+
+        # --- LayerNorm backward through the bprop engine (reuse mean/inv_var) ---
+        dyt = _T(torch.randn(N, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt))
+        dxt = _T(torch.empty(N, D, device="cuda", dtype=dt))

+        dbt = _mkf(D)

+        ivtin = _T(ivt.buf)

+        )
+        bg = _Graph(bnode)
+        _expect(be.probe(bspec, bg), "LAYERNORM_BWD: bprop probe True")
+        _expect(fe.probe(fspec, bg) is False, "LAYERNORM_BWD: fprop probe False")
+        be.build(bspec, bg)({dyt: dyt.buf, xt: xt.buf, gt: gt.buf, mtin: mtin.buf, ivtin: ivtin.buf, dxt: dxt.buf, dst: dst.buf, dbt: dbt.buf})
+        xr = xt.buf.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+        gr = gt.buf.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+        br = bt.buf.float().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+        yref = F.layer_norm(xr, (D,), gr, br, 1e-5)
+        dxr, dgr, dbr = torch.autograd.grad(yref, [xr, gr, br], grad_outputs=dyt.buf.float())
+        tol = _tol(dt, 4e-2)
+        _expect((dxt.buf.float() - dxr).abs().max().item() <= tol * max(1, dxr.abs().max().item()), "LAYERNORM_BWD: DX matches")
+        _expect((dst.buf - dgr).abs().max().item() <= tol * max(1, dgr.abs().max().item()), "LAYERNORM_BWD: DScale matches")
+
+        # --- GroupNorm + BatchNorm forward through the SAME fprop engine (variant dispatch) ---
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        xg = _mk((4, 8, 32), dt)
+        gg = _mk((8,), dt)
+        bg2 = _mk((8,), dt)
+        yg = _T(torch.empty(4, 8, 32, device="cuda", dtype=dt))
+        mg = _mkf(16)
+        ig = _mkf(16)
+        gnode = _Node("GROUPNORM", {"epsilon": 1e-5, "num_groups": 4}, {"input": xg, "scale": gg, "bias": bg2}, {"Y": yg, "mean": mg, "inv_var": ig})
+        gG = _Graph(gnode)
+        _expect(fe.probe(fspec, gG), "GROUPNORM: fprop probe True (same engine)")
+        fe.build(fspec, gG)({xg: xg.buf, gg: gg.buf, bg2: bg2.buf, yg: yg.buf, mg: mg.buf, ig: ig.buf})
+        gref = F.group_norm(xg.buf.float(), 4, gg.buf.float(), bg2.buf.float(), 1e-5)
+        _expect((yg.buf.float() - gref).abs().max().item() <= _tol(dt, 6e-2), "GROUPNORM: Y matches torch")
+
+        torch.manual_seed(2)
+        xb = _mk((16, 8, 4), dt)
+        gbt = _mk((8,), dt)
+        bbt = _mk((8,), dt)
+        yb = _T(torch.empty(16, 8, 4, device="cuda", dtype=dt))
+        mb = _mkf(8)
+        ib = _mkf(8)
+        bnnode = _Node("BATCHNORM", {"epsilon": 1e-5, "momentum": 0.1}, {"input": xb, "scale": gbt, "bias": bbt}, {"Y": yb, "mean": mb, "inv_var": ib})

+        _expect(fe.probe(fspec, bnG), "BATCHNORM: fprop probe True (same engine)")
+        fe.build(fspec, bnG)({xb: xb.buf, gbt: gbt.buf, bbt: bbt.buf, yb: yb.buf, mb: mb.buf, ib: ib.buf})

+        _expect((yb.buf.float() - bref).abs().max().item() <= _tol(dt, 6e-2), "BATCHNORM: Y matches torch")
+
+    print("\n" + ("ALL PASS" if _OK else "SOME FAILED"))
+    sys.exit(0 if _OK else 1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+def test_frost_norm_engine_e2e():
+    """pytest entry point; this module also runs standalone via ``__main__``."""
+    try:
+        main()
+    except SystemExit as exc:
+        assert not exc.code, "checks failed -- see captured stdout"

+engine registration — using synthetic cuDNN norm nodes that mirror the real
+``cudnn._pygraph`` schema (node types ``LAYERNORM``/``LAYERNORM_BWD``/...; ports
+``input``/``scale``/``bias``/``grad``; outputs ``Y``/``mean``/``inv_var``/``DX``/
+``DScale``/``DBias``; backward takes ``mean``/``inv_variance`` as inputs).
+
+End-to-end graph execution (``select_engines`` -> ``execute``) requires a built
+cuDNN frontend and a real graph, and is not exercised here.
+
+    pytest test/python/norm/graph/test_frost_norm_engines.py
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+import os
+import sys
+import types
+
+
+import cudnn
+import pytest
+import torch  # noqa: E402
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm engines require a built cudnn frontend")
+
+from cudnn.norm import graph_analyzer as ga  # noqa: E402
+from cudnn.norm.config_sm100 import NormVariant as NV  # noqa: E402
+from cudnn.norm.fprop import engines as fe  # noqa: E402
+from cudnn.norm.bprop import engines as be  # noqa: E402
+
+_DT = cudnn.data_type
+
+
+class _T:
+    def __init__(self, dim):
+        self._d = tuple(dim)
+
+    def get_dim(self):
+        return self._d
+
+    def get_stride(self):
+        s = [1] * len(self._d)
+        for i in range(len(self._d) - 2, -1, -1):
+            s[i] = s[i + 1] * self._d[i + 1]
+        return tuple(s)
+
+    def get_data_type(self):
+        return _DT.HALF
+
+    def get_name(self):
+        return ""
+
+    def get_uid(self):
+        return 0
+
+
+class _Node:
+    def __init__(self, ntype, params, inputs, outputs):
+        self.node_type = types.SimpleNamespace(name=ntype)
+        self.params = params
+        self.inputs = inputs
+        self.outputs = outputs
+
+
+class _Graph:
+    def __init__(self, node):
+        self.nodes = [node]
+
+
+def _facts(node):
+    return dataclasses.replace(ga.analyze(_Graph(node)), device_cc=(10, 0))
+
+
+def main():
+    ok = True
+
+    def expect(cond, msg):
+        nonlocal ok
+        ok &= bool(cond)
+        print(f"  [{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}] {msg}")
+
+    D = 256
+    # LayerNorm forward (real cuDNN spelling)
+    ln = _Node("LAYERNORM", {"epsilon": 1e-5}, {"input": _T([8, D]), "scale": _T([D]), "bias": _T([D])}, {"Y": _T([8, D]), "mean": _T([8]), "inv_var": _T([8])})
+    f = _facts(ln)
+    expect(f.variant == NV.LAYER_NORM and f.phase == "fprop", "LAYERNORM -> LN fprop")
+    expect(f.normalized_shape == (D,) and f.has_beta and f.has_mean, "LN normalized_shape/flags")
+    # One fprop engine + one bprop engine, each serving all variants.
+    fcap = fe.ENGINE_SPECS[0].capabilities
+    bcap = be.ENGINE_SPECS[0].capabilities

+
+    # RMSNorm forward (no bias, no mean output)
+    rms = _Node("RMSNORM", {"epsilon": 1e-5}, {"input": _T([8, D]), "scale": _T([D])}, {"Y": _T([8, D]), "inv_var": _T([8])})
+    fr = _facts(rms)
+    expect(fr.variant == NV.RMS_NORM and not fr.has_mean and not fr.has_beta, "RMSNORM flags")
+    expect(fe.mismatch(fcap, fr) is None, "fprop engine accepts RMS (same engine)")
+
+    # BatchNorm forward with running stats
+    bn = _Node(
+        "BATCHNORM",
+        {"epsilon": 1e-5, "momentum": 0.1},
+        {"input": _T([16, 8, 4]), "scale": _T([8]), "bias": _T([8]), "in_running_mean": _T([8]), "in_running_var": _T([8])},
+        {"Y": _T([16, 8, 4]), "mean": _T([8]), "inv_var": _T([8]), "next_running_mean": _T([8]), "next_running_var": _T([8])},
+    )
+    fbn = _facts(bn)
+    expect(fbn.variant == NV.BATCH_NORM and fbn.wants_running_stats and fbn.training, "BATCHNORM running-stats")
+    expect(fe.mismatch(fcap, fbn) is None, "fprop engine accepts BatchNorm (same engine)")
+
+    # BatchNorm inference -> training False
+    bni = _Node(
+        "BATCHNORM_INFERENCE", {}, {"input": _T([16, 8, 4]), "mean": _T([8]), "inv_variance": _T([8]), "scale": _T([8]), "bias": _T([8])}, {"Y": _T([16, 8, 4])}
+    )
+    expect(not _facts(bni).training, "BATCHNORM_INFERENCE -> training=False")
+
+    # LayerNorm backward (mean/inv_variance are inputs; grad = DY)

+        {},

+        {"DX": _T([8, D]), "DScale": _T([D]), "DBias": _T([D])},
